entries.definition: GIB'BETHON (height), a town of Dan: given to the Kohathites, Josh 19:44; Josh 21:23; held by the Philistines in the reigns of Jeroboam, Nadab, Baasha, Elah, Zimri, and Omri. 1 Kgs 15:27; 1 Kgs 16:17. The siege lasted 27 years. Conder proposes to identify it with Gibbieh or Kibbieh, between Eltekah and Baalath.
entries.definition_ko: 단 지파의 성읍으로 고핫 자손에게 주어졌고(수 19:44, 21:23), 여로보암·나답·바아사·엘라·시므리·오므리 때 블레셋이 차지했다(왕상 15:27, 16:17). 그 포위는 27년간 계속되었다.

entries.definition: GIB'EA (hill), a name in the genealogy of Judah, 1 Chr 2:49; probably the name of a place rather than of a person. See Gibeah, 1.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 족보의 한 이름이나(대상 2:49) 사람보다 지명일 가능성이 높다.

entries.definition: GIB'EAH (a hill), the name of several towns. Gibeah in the hill-country of Judah, Josh 15:57; now probably Jeboh, 10 miles north of Hebron. This is doubted by Grove, but supported by Robinson, Porter, and Conder. Gibeah of Benjamin, 1 Sam 13:2; first mentioned in Jud 19; a shameful crime by some of its people nearly destroyed the tribe of Benjamin, Jud 20-21. It is generally regarded the same as Gibeah of Saul, and located at Tuleil el-Ful, "hill of beans," 4 miles north of Jerusalem, and east of the road from Jerusalem to Nabulus (Shechem). Gibeah of Saul is held by most authorities to be the same as Gibeah of Benjamin, but Baedeker's Hand-book assumes that they are distinct cities, and holds that Geba and Gibeah were sometimes confounded. For in 1 Sam 14:1-15, Geba near Michmash, or Jeba, would answer the conditions of Jonathan's exploit, but V. 1 Sam 14:16 suddenly takes us back to Gibeah of Benjamin, toward which the Philistines would hardly have retreated if any other route was open to them. Again, in 1 Sam 13:2, 1 Sam 13:15, Jonathan is at Gibeah of Benjamin, and Samuel also, but in v. 1 Sam 13:3 Jonathan smites the Philistines at Gebah, and he and Saul remain at "Geba," as many versions read, and Gibeah, as in our English version. For notices of Gibeah of Saul, see 1 Sam 10:26; 1 Sam 11:4; 1 Sam 15:34; 1 Sam 22:6; 1 Sam 23:19; Isa 10:29, etc. In the first passage it is called "Gibeah Elohim," meaning, in the Hebrew, "Gibeah of God," or "the hill," as our version reads in 1 Sam 7:1, and correctly. Gibeah in Kirjath-jearim was no doubt a hill in that city, 2 Sam 6:3-4, on which the house of Abinadab stood, where the ark was left. Gibeah in the field, Jud 20:31; probably the same as Geba. Gibeah-haaraloth, Josh 5:3, margin. See Gilgal.
entries.definition_ko: 여러 성읍의 이름이다. 1) 유다 산지의 기브아(수 15:57). 2) 베냐민의 기브아(삼상 13:2)로 삿 19장에 처음 언급되며, 그 주민 일부의 부끄러운 범죄로 베냐민 지파가 거의 멸절될 뻔했다(삿 20-21장). 대개 사울의 기브아와 같은 곳으로 여겨져, 예루살렘 북쪽 4마일의 '콩 언덕'이라는 뜻의 툴레일 엘풀에 비정된다.

entries.definition: GIB'EATH (hill), probably the same as Gibeah of Benjamin, Josh 18:28. See Gibeah, 2.
entries.definition_ko: 베냐민의 기브아와 같은 곳으로 추정된다(수 18:28).

entries.definition: GIB'EON (of a hill), a city of the Hivites, Josh 9:3-21, about 6 miles north of Jerusalem. History. — Gibeon, after its league with Joshua, was attacked by the Canaanites; secured Joshua's help; near it Joshua commanded the sun to stand still. Josh 10:12-13; Isa 28:21; the city was given to Benjamin and to the Levites, Josh 18:25; John 21:17; it was the scene of a mortal skirmish between twelve of Abner's and twelve of Joab's men, also of the murders of Asahel by Abner, and of Amasa by Joab, 2 Sam 2:12-24; 2 Sam 20:8-10; because Saul broke the covenant with the Gibeonites, in the days of David a famine broke out, which, after three years, stopped by the hanging of seven of Saul's sons, 2 Sam 21:1, 2 Sam 21:2-6; the tabernacle was set up at Gibeon, 1 Chr 16:39; and Solomon oftered great sacrifices there, 1 Kgs 3:4-5; 1 Kgs 9:2; 2 Chr 1:3, 2 Chr 1:13; Jehoram recovered captives at Gibeon, Jer 41:12-16; its people helped to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem after the Captivity, Neh 3:7; Neh 7:25; Ezr 2:20, margin. It is now called el-Jib, a small village in the midst of ancient ruins, and standing on a low circular hill, whose steep sides are covered with vineyards. At the eastern base of the hill is a fine spring; the water runs into a reservoir 120 by 100 feet, which is probably the "Pool of Gibeon."
entries.definition_ko: 히위 족속의 성읍으로(수 9:3-21) 예루살렘 북쪽 약 6마일에 있다. 여호수아와 화친한 후 가나안 사람들에게 공격받아 여호수아의 도움을 얻었고, 그 근처에서 여호수아가 해에게 멈추라 명했다(수 10:12-13). 베냐민과 레위인에게 주어졌고(수 18:25, 21:17), 아브넬의 열두 사람과 요압의 열두 사람 사이의 치명적 겨룸이 있던 곳이며 아브넬이 아사헬을, 요압이 아마사를 죽인 곳이다(삼하 2:12-24, 20:8-10). 사울이 기브온 사람과의 언약을 깨뜨렸기에 다윗 때 3년 기근이 들었고 사울의 아들 일곱을 매달아 그쳤다(삼하 21:1-6). 성막이 기브온에 세워졌고(대상 16:39) 솔로몬이 거기서 큰 제사를 드렸다(왕상 3:4-5).

entries.definition: GIB'EONITES, the inhabitants of Gibeon, 2 Sam 21:1-4, 2 Sam 21:9.
entries.definition_ko: 기브온 주민을 가리킨다(삼하 21:1-4,9).

entries.definition: GIB'LITES, THE, a people inhabiting Gebel, Josh 13:5.
entries.definition_ko: 그발에 살던 백성(수 13:5).

entries.definition: GIDDAL'TI (I have trained up), a Kohathite Levite, head of the twenty second course, 1 Chr 25:4, 1 Chr 25:29.
entries.definition_ko: 고핫 자손 레위인으로 스물두째 반차의 우두머리(대상 25:4,29).

entries.definition: GID'DELL (very great), names of two persons whose descendants returned with Zerubbabel. Ezr 2:47, Ezr 2:56; Neh 7:49, Neh 7:58.
entries.definition_ko: 스룹바벨과 함께 그 후손이 돌아온 두 사람의 이름(스 2:47,56, 느 7:49,58).

entries.definition: GID'EON (a hewer), the son of Joash the Abiezrite, and fifth judge of Israel. He first comes into notice when an angel appears to him under the oak in Ophrah and assures him of God's special favor, Jud 6:11-12. Subsequently, God commanded him to offer as a sacrifice to the Lord the bullock which his father had set apart for Baal, and to destroy the altar of Baal. He did both of these things, but only escaped the murderous wrath of his fellow-citizens through the wily intervention of his father, Jud 6:31. The great works of Gideon's life were the abolition of idolatry, Jud 8:33, and the deliverance of the land from the invasions of the Midianites. Before undertaking the latter enterprise, he secured a pledge of the divine favor in the phenomena of the dew and the fleece, Jud 6:36-40. God, desirous of showing the victory to be the immediate result of supernatural agency, diminished Gideon's army from 32,000 to 300. With this small force Gideon had recourse to stratagem, and in an assault by night completely terrified and successfully routed the enemy, Judges 7. Gideon refused the crown, Jud 8:23, from the whole nation, which his son Abimelech afterward received from a part. He judged Israel for 40 years, Jud 8:28, and the nation enjoyed peace and engaged in the worship of God, Jud 8:33. He was one of her greatest rulers, and is honorably mentioned Heb 11:32.
entries.definition_ko: 아비에셀 사람 요아스의 아들이자 이스라엘의 다섯째 사사다. 오브라의 상수리나무 아래서 천사가 나타나 하나님의 각별한 은총을 확언하면서 처음 등장한다(삿 6:11-12). 이어 하나님이 아버지가 바알을 위해 구별해 둔 수소를 여호와께 제물로 드리고 바알의 제단을 헐라 명하셨다. 둘 다 행했으나 아버지의 기지 어린 중재로 겨우 동네 사람들의 살기를 면했다(삿 6:31). 생애의 큰 업적은 우상숭배를 척결한 것과 미디안의 침략에서 땅을 건진 것이다. 후자에 나서기 전 이슬과 양털의 표징으로 하나님의 은총을 확인받았다(삿 6:36-40). 하나님은 승리가 초자연적 역사임을 보이시려 기드온의 군대를 3만 2천에서 300으로 줄이셨다.

entries.definition: GIDEO'NI (a cutting down),The father of the prince of Benjamin in the wilderness. Num 1:11; Num 2:22; Num 7:60, Num 7:65; John 10:24.
entries.definition_ko: 광야에서 베냐민 지도자의 아버지(민 1:11, 2:22, 7:60,65).

entries.definition: GI'DOM (cutting down, desolation), between Gibeah and the cliff of Rimmon, Jud 20:45. It has not been identified.
entries.definition_ko: 기브아와 림몬 바위 사이의 곳이다(삿 20:45). 아직 확인되지 않았다.

entries.definition: GIER'-EAGLE (racham = parental affection), the Egyptian vulture, an unclean bird. Lev 11:18; Deut 14:17.
entries.definition_ko: 애굽 독수리로 부정한 새다(레 11:18, 신 14:17).

entries.definition: GIFT, The practice of making presents as a token of esteem and respect prevailed very extensively in the East. They were frequently made to secure favor, as in the case of Jacob and Esau, Gen 32:13-15. Kings and princes often made splendid gifts. Gen 45:22-23, and subjects approached their kings with presents. 1 Kgs 4:21; 2 Chr 17:5, etc. To refuse to make presents to a king was a mark of contempt, 1 Sam 10:27. The articles thus bestowed were very various — cattle. Gen 32:13; garments, 2 Kgs 5:23; money, 2 Sam 18:11, etc. See, for a list of presents, 1 Kgs 10:25. The wise men from the East presented the infant Jesus with the most costly articles of the Orient — "gold, and frankincense, and myrrh." Matt 2:11. The peculiar offerings under the Law are spoken of as gifts. Deut 16:17; Matt 5:23-24. And it is with singular force that the blessings of the gospel through Jesus Christ are called gifts, inasmuch as they cannot be purchased, and nothing can be given in return for them.
entries.definition_ko: 존경과 경의의 표시로 예물을 주는 관습이 동방에 매우 널리 퍼져 있었다. 야곱과 에서의 경우처럼 호의를 얻으려 주는 일이 잦았다(창 32:13-15). 왕과 제후는 흔히 화려한 선물을 했고(창 45:22-23) 신하는 예물을 들고 왕께 나아갔다(왕상 4:21, 대하 17:5). 왕에게 예물을 바치지 않는 것은 멸시의 표시였다(삼상 10:27). 주는 물건은 매우 다양해 가축(창 32:13), 의복(왕하 5:23), 돈(삼하 18:11) 등이었다. 동방박사는 아기 예수께 동방의 가장 값진 것들, 곧 '황금과 유향과 몰약'을 드렸다(마 2:11). 그리스도를 통한 복음의 복을 '선물'이라 부르는 것은 그것이 살 수도, 무엇으로 갚을 수도 없기에 각별한 힘을 지닌다.

entries.definition: GIFTS. The word "gifts" is employed to describe those graces or qualities with which Christ endues his disciples. Eph 4:8, Eph 4:11-12. Some of these, which were bestowed on the early apostles, were miraculous, and designed to confirm their claims to apostolic authority, such as the gift of tongues, of prophecy, etc. The "ministry of gifts" ceased with the apostles, although some hold that they have been continued, and are still dispensed; as, for example, the Irvingites.
entries.definition_ko: '은사'는 그리스도께서 제자들에게 입히시는 은혜나 자질을 가리키는 데 쓰인다(엡 4:8,11-12). 초대 사도들에게 주어진 것 중 일부는 이적적이어서 그들의 사도적 권위를 확증하기 위한 것이었으니 방언과 예언의 은사 등이다. '은사의 사역'은 사도들과 함께 그쳤다고 보는 것이 일반적이나, 지금도 계속되고 있다고 보는 이들도 있다.

entries.definition: GI'HON (fountain, or stream). The name of the second river of Eden, Gen 2:13. Some identify it with the Nile. See Eden. A place near Jerusalem where Solomon was proclaimed king, 1 Kgs 1:33-45. Hezekiah stopped the upper watercourse of Gihon, and Manasseh built a wall on the west side of Gihon in the valley. 2 Chr 32:30; 2 Chr 33:14. Upper Gihon has been identified by some with Birket Mamilla, 150 rods west of the wall of Jerusalem, which is a pool 300 feet long, 200 wide, and 20 deep. Lower Gihon is supposed to have been the same as Birket es-Sultan, south-west of the Jaffa gate, a pool 600 feet long, 250 broad, and 40 deep. Warren, however, proposes the Pool of the Bath or Hezekiah as the Lower Gihon, the valley being that from the Jaffa gate to the temple-site, now filled up, while Grove and Conder favor the pool Siloam as the site of Gihon. See Jerusalem.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 에덴의 둘째 강의 이름(창 2:13). 나일과 동일시하는 이도 있다. 2) 예루살렘 근처, 솔로몬이 왕으로 선포된 곳이다(왕상 1:33-45). 히스기야가 기혼의 윗 물줄기를 막았고 므낫세가 골짜기 기혼 서쪽에 성벽을 쌓았다(대하 32:30, 33:14).

entries.definition: GIL'ALAI (dungy, or weighty), a musical priest in Nehemiah's day, Neh 12:36.
entries.definition_ko: 느헤미야 때의 음악 담당 제사장(느 12:36).

entries.definition: GILBO'A, or GIL'BOA (bubbling fountain), a mountain east of the plain of Jezreel, about 10 miles long, running east-south-east and west-north-west; the northern slope is steep; the southern was probably once covered with forests, though it is now inhabited and cultivated. History. — Gilboa was a place where Saul and Jonathan were slain in battle, and from whence Saul went to consult the witch of Endor. 1 Sam 28:4; 1 Sam 31:6; 1 Chr 10:1; 2 Sam 1:21. The mountain is now called Jebel Fukua'; the place is called Jelbon.
entries.definition_ko: 이스르엘 평야 동쪽의 산으로 길이 약 10마일이며 동남동에서 서북서로 뻗는다. 북쪽 비탈은 가파르고 남쪽은 한때 숲이었을 것이나 지금은 사람이 살며 경작한다. 사울과 요나단이 싸우다 죽은 곳이며, 사울이 여기서 엔돌의 신접한 여인을 찾아갔다(삼상 28:4, 31:6, 대상 10:1, 삼하 1:21). 지금은 제벨 푸쿠아라 불린다.

entries.definition:
GIL'EAD (hard). 1. The grandson of Manasseh, Num 26:29-30, etc. The father of Jephthah, Jud 11:1-2. A Gadite, 1 Chr 5:14.

GIL'EAD (rocky region), called also MOUNT GILEAD and LAND OF GILEAD, Gen 31:25; Num 32:1, and known in N.T. times as Peraja "beyond Jordan." Matt 4:15; John 1:28. Gilead was a region of country bounded on the north by Bashan, east by the Arabian desert, south by Moab and Ammon, and west by the Jordan. Gen 31:21,- Deut 3:12-17; 1 Sam 13:7; 2 Kgs 10:33. It was about 60 miles long, and 20 miles in its average breadth. Physical Features. — The region of Gilead combines hills, valleys, fields, streams, and forests, as if it were a collection of beautiful parks. Among its mountains are fields of grass and wheat, and forests with paths winding through them. Of these mountains named in Scripture are Abarim, Pisgah, Nebo, and Peor. The mountains of Gilead are 2000 to 3000 feet above the valley of the Jordan, gradually sinking away to the eastward into the Arabian plateau. The summits are broad, furnishing rich pasturage and extensive forests, and were famous for their aromatic gums and spices. Num 32:1; Gen 37:25. The balm of Gilead was held in high favor, Jer 8:22; Jer 46:11; it is said that only a spoonful could be collected in a day, and that was sold for twice its weight in silver. It was found along the Jordan valley. The region is still one of great fertility. Eleven living streams are found between the Yarmuk and the Jabbok, and canals dug for irrigating the fields in every direction. South of the Jabbok on the Jordan the country is barren and desolate from want of water as far as the Wady Nimrin, but beyond that are three streams and the land is again fertile. Several hot sulphur-springs have been found in Gilead. History. — Jacob fled toward Gilead, Gen 31:21; it was conquered by Israel, Num 21:24; Jud 10:22; Josh 12:2; Deut 2:36; was given to Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, Josh 17:6; under Jephthah it defeated the Ammonites, Jud 10:18; was a refuge for Saul's son and for David, 2 Sam 2:9; 2 Sam 17:22, 2 Sam 17:24; the home of Elijah, 1 Kgs 17:1; taken in part by Syria, 2 Kgs 10:33; by Assyria, 2 Kgs 15:25-29; referred to in the minor prophets, Hos 6:8; Hos 12:11; Am 1:3, Am 1:13; Ob 19; Mic 7:14. Zech 10:10. It is now under nominal Turkish rule, with a Turkish governor residing at es-Salt — Ramoth-gilead of Scripture — but it is really controlled by the semibarbarous Arabs and overrun by Bedouins. Mount Gilead of Jud 7:3 was probably near Mount Gilboa; a trace of the name is found in Jalud. Some German scholars, however, read "Gilboa" for "Gilead" in this passage. The well of Herod was near this mount.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 므낫세의 손자(민 26:29-30), 입다의 아버지(삿 11:1-2), 갓 사람(대상 5:14). 2) 길르앗산, 길르앗 땅이라고도 불리며(창 31:25, 민 32:1) 신약 시대에는 '요단 저편' 베레아로 알려졌다. 북쪽은 바산, 동쪽은 아라비아 사막, 남쪽은 모압과 암몬, 서쪽은 요단에 접한 지역이다(신 3:12-17, 왕하 10:33). 길이 약 60마일, 평균 너비 20마일이다. 언덕과 골짜기, 들과 시내와 숲이 어우러져 아름다운 공원의 모음 같다. 성경에 이름이 나오는 산으로 아바림, 비스가, 느보, 브올이 있다.

entries.definition: GIL'EADITES, a branch of the tribe of Manasseh, descended from Gilead. Num 26:29, etc.
entries.definition_ko: 길르앗에게서 난 므낫세 지파의 한 갈래(민 26:29).

entries.definition: GIL'GAL (rolling). 1 . The name of the first station of the Israelites after crossing the Jordan, and "in the east border of Jericho," Josh 4:19-20, the twelve stones were set up, and the tabernacle remained at Gilgal until removed to Shiloh. Josh 18:1. Samuel judged, and Saul was made king there, 1 Sam 7:16; 1 Sam 10:8; 1 Sam 11:14-15; at Gilgal the people gathered for war; there Agag was hewn in pieces. 1 Sam 13:4-7; 1 Sam 15:33. Later on, Gilgal became a seat of idolatry, but whether this one or the Gilgal above Bethel is yet unsettled. Gilgal is not named in the N.T. Josephus places this Gilgal 10 furlongs from Jericho and 50 from the Jordan; Jerome had it pointed out 2 miles from Jericho; Thomson and others locate it near the modern village of Riba; Zschokke, at Tell Jeljal, north of Wady Kelt. Conder favors this, and gives the name Jiljulieh. The Gilgal in Elijah's time was probably in the range of hills beyond Bethel, since the prophet "went down" from that Gilgal to Bethel, 2 Kgs 2:2. As Bethel is 3300 feet above the Jordan plain, it must have been a Gilgal not in that plain, but one higher up than Bethel. It has been identified with Jijilia, 8 miles north of Bethel, where the school of the prophets was probably established. Gilgal of Josh 12:23 is supposed to be at a Jiljulieh, 4 miles south of Antipatris, in the plain of Sharon. There is a Kilkilieh — another form of Gilgal — also, 2 miles east of Antipatris.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 이스라엘이 요단을 건넌 후 첫 진 친 곳으로 '여리고 동쪽 경계'에 있었다(수 4:19-20). 열두 돌을 세웠고 성막이 실로로 옮겨질 때까지 길갈에 있었다(수 18:1). 사무엘이 여기서 재판했고 사울이 왕이 되었다(삼상 7:16, 11:14-15). 백성이 전쟁을 위해 모였고 아각이 찍혀 죽은 곳이다(삼상 13:4-7, 15:33). 후에 우상숭배의 자리가 되었다. 신약에는 나오지 않는다. 2) 엘리야 때의 길갈은 벧엘 너머 산지에 있었을 것이니, 선지자가 그 길갈에서 벧엘로 '내려갔기' 때문이다(왕하 2:1-2).

entries.definition: GI'LOH (exile), a town in the hillcountry of Judah; the home of Ahithophel. Josh 15:51; 2 Sam 15:12; 2 Sam 17:23; perhaps now Beit Jala, a village of 3000 population, about 2 miles northwest of Bethlehem.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 산지의 성읍으로 아히도벨의 고향이다(수 15:51, 삼하 15:12, 17:23).

entries.definition: GI'LONITE, a native of Giloh, 2 Sam 15:12; 2 Sam 23:34.
entries.definition_ko: 길로 출신 사람을 가리킨다(삼하 15:12, 23:34).

entries.definition: GIM'ZO (fertile in sycamores), a town in the plain of Judah; taken by the Philistines, 2 Chr 28:18; now Jimzu, a village about 2 1/2 miles southwest of Ludd (Lydda).
entries.definition_ko: 유다 평지의 성읍으로 블레셋이 빼앗았다(대하 28:18). 지금은 룻다 남서쪽 2.5마일의 마을 짐주다.

entries.definition: GIN, a trap for beasts or birds, consisting of a net ("snare," Isa 8:14), and a stick to act as a spring ("gin," Am 3:5). See Hunting.
entries.definition_ko: 짐승이나 새를 잡는 덫으로, 그물(사 8:14의 '올무')과 튀는 장치 구실을 하는 막대기(암 3:5의 '덫')로 이루어진다. 사냥 참조.

entries.definition: GI'NATH (protection), the father of Tibni, the rival of Omri for the throne of Israel, 1 Kgs 16:21-22.
entries.definition_ko: 이스라엘 왕위를 두고 오므리와 겨룬 디브니의 아버지(왕상 16:21-22).

entries.definition: GIN'NETHO (gardener), a priest who returned from Babylon with Zerubbabel, Neh 12:4.
entries.definition_ko: 스룹바벨과 함께 바벨론에서 돌아온 제사장(느 12:4).

entries.definition: GIN'NETHON (gardener), a priest who "sealed the covenant," Neh 10:6. One of his descendants, mentioned in Neh 12:16.
entries.definition_ko: '언약에 인친' 제사장(느 10:6). 그 후손이 느 12:16에 언급된다.

entries.definition: GIRD, GIRD'LE. Girdles are worn in the East by both men and women for binding up the loose, flowing Ancient Girdles. 1, 2, Egyptian. (From Wilkinson and Rosellini.) 3, 4, Assyrian. (From Sculptures in the British Museum.) garments, so as to admit of their moving about freely. The girdles were usually of leather or of linen, and frequently were highly ornamented. Daggers were often carried in the girdle. See Clothes.
entries.definition_ko: 동방에서는 남녀 모두 헐렁하게 흘러내리는 옷을 여며 자유로이 움직이려 띠를 둘렀다. 대개 가죽이나 아마포로 만들었고 흔히 화려하게 장식했다. 단검을 띠에 차기도 했다. 의복 참조.

entries.definition: GIR'GASITE, Gen 10:16, or GIR'GASHITES, Gen 15:21. A tribe of the Canaanites who are supposed to have inhabited a section of the country east of the Sea of Galilee, whence the name of the city of Gergesa.
entries.definition_ko: 가나안 족속의 한 부족으로(창 10:16, 15:21) 갈릴리 바다 동쪽 지역에 살았던 것으로 추정되며, 거기서 거라사라는 성읍 이름이 나왔다.

entries.definition: GIS'PA (caress), one of the rulers of the Nethinim after the Captivity, Neh 11:21.
entries.definition_ko: 포로기 이후 느디님 사람의 지도자 중 하나(느 11:21).

entries.definition: GIT'TAH-HE'PHER, Josh 19:13. See Gath-Hepher.
entries.definition_ko: 가드헤벨 참조(수 19:13).

entries.definition: GIT'TAIM (two wine-presses), a town, probably in Benjamin. 2 Sam 4:3; Neh 11:33.
entries.definition_ko: '두 포도주 틀'이라는 뜻으로 아마도 베냐민에 있던 성읍이다(삼하 4:3, 느 11:33).

entries.definition: GIT'TITES. See Gath.
entries.definition_ko: 가드 참조.

entries.definition: GIT'TITH (a musical instrument), a word found in the titles of Ps 8; Ps 81; Ps 84. The derivation of the word is disputed. It may be associated with the city of Gath, or with the word signifying "wine-press," and consequently with the vintage-season.
entries.definition_ko: 시편 8편, 81편, 84편의 표제에 나오는 악기 이름이다. 어원에는 이견이 있어 가드 성읍과 관련되거나 '포도주 틀'을 뜻하는 말, 따라서 포도 수확기와 관련될 수 있다.

entries.definition: GI'ZONITE, the epithet given to Hashem, the father of some of David's warriors. 1 Chr 11:34,
entries.definition_ko: 다윗의 용사 몇 사람의 아버지 하셈에게 붙은 칭호(대상 11:34).

entries.definition: GIZ'RITES. See Gezrites.
entries.definition_ko: 게스 족속 참조.

entries.definition: GLASS was discovered by the Phoenicians, or perhaps earlier. Representations Egyptian Glass Blowers. (After Wilkinson.) Egyptian Glass Bottles. (After Wilkinson.) of the process of glass-blowing are found on Eyptian monuments, and glass beads and fragments of glass vases have been discovered of very ancient age. The only mention of glass in the O.T. is in Job 28:17, where it is translated "crystal." The mirrors referred to by the word "glass" in 1 Cor 13:12; 2 Cor 3:18; Jas 1:23 were not made of glass. See Looking-glass.
entries.definition_ko: 유리는 베니게인이, 혹은 그보다 앞서 발견했다. 유리를 부는 과정이 애굽 유적에 그려져 있고 매우 오래된 유리구슬과 유리병 조각이 발견되었다. 구약에서 유리에 대한 유일한 언급은 욥 28:17이며 '수정'으로 번역되어 있다. 고전 13:12, 고후 3:18, 약 1:23에서 '거울'로 옮긴 말은 유리로 만든 것이 아니었다.

entries.definition: GLEAN. Ruth 2:2. In the joyful season of harvest the Jewish farmer was not allowed to forget the poor and the stranger. A special command was given. Lev 19:9-10, that he should leave some of the fruits for them to gather.
entries.definition_ko: 기쁜 추수 때에 유대 농부는 가난한 자와 나그네를 잊어서는 안 되었다(룻 2:2). 그들이 거두도록 얼마를 남겨 두라는 특별한 명령이 주어졌다(레 19:9-10).

entries.definition: GLEDE, mentioned among the unclean birds of prey by a Hebrew name which probably indicates its keenness of vision. Deut 14:13. It is not certain what particular bird is meant, but most probably one of the buzzards, of which three species inhabit Palestine. The great red buzzard (Buteo ferox) is most common, and resembles an eagle in Bottle inscribed with the Name of Thothmes III. (After Wilkinson.) its size and habits. The original word is rendered "vulture" in Lev 11:14.
entries.definition_ko: 부정한 맹금 중에 언급되는 새로, 그 히브리 이름은 예리한 시력을 뜻하는 듯하다(신 14:13). 어떤 새인지 확실하지 않으나 팔레스타인에 세 종이 사는 말똥가리 중 하나일 가능성이 높다. 큰붉은말똥가리가 가장 흔하며 크기와 습성이 독수리와 비슷하다.

entries.definition: GLORY, GLORIFY, terms of frequent occurrence in the Bible. To " glorify " is to render glorious or to exalt. Dan 5:23; Acts 3:13; John 17:5. Hence the comprehensive precept of the apostle, 1 Cor 6:19-20, requiring the devotion of our whole powers and faculties to this one great end, "the glory of God," 1 Cor 10:31, or making God glorious. To "give glory" means to praise or exalt. Luke 17:18. Glory of God. This expression is almost equivalent to "brightness" or "effulgence" of God, and refers to the peculiar and absolute perfection of all the divine attributes. By contrast, men are said to have "come short of the glory of God," Rom 3:23, where the special reference, no doubt, is to the perfect holiness of the Almighty. God is denominated the "King of glory," Ps 24:8, or of resplendent brightness. The glory of God is displayed in the works of creation, Ps 19:1, in the redem])tion of the world through Christ, 2 Cor 4:6, and in the person of Christ. Heb 1:3. He is said to be "glorious in holiness." Our Lord is called the "Lord of glory," Jas 2:1, and the " hope of glory." Col 1:27. Different objects are said to have a glory, 1 Cor 15:41, and regenerate believers are said to have awaiting them the glory akin to that they have lost. Col 3:4; Heb 2:10.
entries.definition_ko: 성경에 자주 나오는 말이다. '영화롭게 하다'는 영광스럽게 하거나 높이는 것이다(단 5:23, 행 3:13, 요 17:5). 그래서 사도는 우리의 모든 힘과 능력을 '하나님의 영광'이라는 이 하나의 큰 목적에 바치라는 포괄적 교훈을 준다(고전 6:19-20, 10:31). '영광을 돌리다'는 찬양하고 높이는 것이다(눅 17:18). '하나님의 영광'은 하나님의 '광채'와 거의 같은 뜻으로, 모든 신적 속성의 독특하고 절대적인 완전함을 가리킨다. 대조적으로 사람은 '하나님의 영광에 이르지 못하더니'라 하는데(롬 3:23), 여기서는 전능자의 완전한 거룩하심을 특히 가리킨다. 하나님의 영광은 창조의 일(시 19:1), 그리스도를 통한 세상의 구속(고후 4:6), 그리스도의 인격(히 1:3)에 드러난다.

entries.definition: GNASH, GNASH'ING, a striking or grinding of the teeth in the paroxysms of anguish or despair. Ps 112:10;Matt 8:12.
entries.definition_ko: 고통이나 절망의 발작 중에 이를 갈거나 부딪는 것이다(시 112:10, 마 8:12).

entries.definition: GNAT. Matt 23:24. This insect, a species of "mosquito," is common in hot countries. In the passage cited, the words "strain at" (a typographical error) should rather be "strain out;" the phrase will then better express the gross inconsistencies which our Saviour reproved.
entries.definition_ko: '모기'의 일종으로 더운 나라에 흔하다(마 23:24). 인용된 구절의 '하루살이는 걸러 내고'는 인쇄 오류로 '걸러 내다'가 옳으며, 그래야 구주께서 책망하신 심한 모순이 더 잘 드러난다.

entries.definition: GOAD. Jud 3:31. This was a rod or pole about 8 feet long, armed at the larger end with a piece of iron, with which the plough-share was freed from clods and earth, and at the smaller with a sharp spike, by which the oxen were urged on in their labor. In the hands of a powerful man like Shamgar, Jud 3:31, it would be a formidable instrument. The goad is used to this day in Palestine.
entries.definition_ko: 길이 약 8피트의 막대로, 굵은 쪽 끝에는 쇳조각을 달아 보습에서 흙덩이를 떼어 내고, 가는 쪽 끝에는 날카로운 침을 박아 소를 몰았다(삿 3:31). 삼갈 같은 장사의 손에서는 무서운 무기가 되었다. 지금도 팔레스타인에서 쓰인다.

entries.definition: GOAT. Lev 3:12. Goats were among the chief possessions of the Syrian Goat (After Tristam) wealthy in the early ages of the world. Gen 27:9; 1 Sam 25:2;2 Chr 17:11. Resembling the sheep in its general structure and appearance, it is covered with hair instead of wool, and is much more active, bold, and wandering in its habits. It feeds on bark and tender twigs, and its feet are formed for leaping and climbing among rocks and mountains. Its milk is valuable for food, Prov 27:27, the hair for manufactures of various kinds, Ex 25:4; Num 31:20; Heb 11:37, and the skin for vessels or bottles, Josh 9:4; Ps 119:83; Matt 9:17, and in modern times for leather. There are several species of goat in Palestine, but the common kind (Capra mambrica) has enormous hanging ears a foot long, often reaching lower than its nose and its stout recurved horns. Comp.Am 3:12. It was a clean animal by the Jewish law, Deut 14:4, and was much used in sacrifices. Lev 3:12; Num 15:27; Ezr 6:17. The peculiar qualities of goats occasion frequent figurative allusions to them. The boldness and strength of the leaders of the flocks are alluded to, Prov 30:31; Zech 10:3, and they are made to represent oppressors and wicked men generally. Eze 34:17; Eze 39:18; Matt 25:33. Goat, Wild (the climber). This animal is quite distinct from the domestic goat. The high hills of Palestine and Arabia are still a refuge for this very shy and wary creature, the ibex or mountain-goat (beden of the Arabs, Capra beden). Tristram says: "In the neighborhood of En-gedi, while encamped by the Dead Sea shore, we obtained several fine specimens, and very interesting it was to find this graceful creature by the very fountain to which it gave name (En-gedi — i.e. 'Fountain of the Kid'), and in the spot where it roamed of old while David wandered to escape the persecutions of Saul "upon the rocks of the wild goats. 1 Sam 24:2. The flesh of these animals is nearly of the flavor of venison. The Bedouins make bags or bottles of their skins and rings of their horns. When they are found among the rocks they usually elude the pursuit of the hunter, sometimes leaping even 20 feet, but in the plains they are often taken. Their habits are alluded to in Job 39:1; Ps 104:18. Goat, Scape, Lev 16:26, one of the two goats offered on the day of atonement. The ceremony which the high priest performed over the scape-goat is very mysterious and very significant. The priest laid his hands upon the head of the goat and confessed over it the sins of Israel. Lev 16:21. The animal was then let go and driven off into the uninhabited wilderness. The significance of this event is beyond dispute. It represents the culmination of the Mosaic sacrifice for sin, and is at the same time a most perfect representation of vicarious atonement. The iniquities of the nation were considered as having been transferred to the goat, the priest having put them upon its head. It was then driven off, in its uncleanness and pollution, to suffer for crimes it had not committed, in the desolate wilderness. This is a beautiful type of the atonement of Christ, upon whom was laid "the iniquity of us all,"who suffered for our redemption, Isa 53. "Scape-goat" is the A.V. translation of "Azazel." Lev 16:26. The old interpretation, which applied the word to the goat, is now abandoned, the best scholars agreeing in regarding it as expressive of the person to whom the goat was sent. It probably comes from a root, used in Arabic, but not in Hebrew, meaning to "separate." But who is the person? The best opinion is that "the devil" is meant. Both goats were parts of the same sin-offering, both belonged to Jehovah. Hence both were typical of the atonement of Christ. The goat that was slain made an atonement for the holy place. The goat that was sent away typified the removing of the guilt of the people. See the valuable and interesting excursus upon "Azazel" in Bible Commentary, Lev. 16.
entries.definition_ko: 염소는 세상 초기에 부유한 이들의 주요 재산이었다(레 3:12, 창 27:9, 삼상 25:2). 전체 구조와 겉모습이 양과 비슷하나 털이 양털이 아니고, 훨씬 활발하고 대담하며 돌아다니기를 좋아한다. 나무껍질과 연한 가지를 먹으며 발이 바위와 산을 뛰고 오르기에 알맞다. 젖은 양식으로 값지고(잠 27:27) 털은 여러 제품에(출 25:4, 민 31:20, 히 11:37), 가죽은 그릇이나 부대(수 9:4, 시 119:83, 마 9:17)와 오늘날의 가죽 제품에 쓰인다. 유대 율법에서 정결한 짐승이었고(신 14:4) 제사에 많이 쓰였다.

entries.definition: GO'ATH (lowing), a place probably near Jerusalem, Jer 31:39; location not known.
entries.definition_ko: 예루살렘 근처로 추정되는 곳이나 위치는 알려져 있지 않다(렘 31:39).

entries.definition: GOB (ditch, or cistern). 2 Sam 21:18-19. The Greek version reads Goth, while in the account of this encounter of David's men in 1 Chr 20:4 the name is Gezer,
entries.definition_ko: 삼하 21:18-19의 지명이다. 헬라어 역본은 '곳'으로 읽고, 대상 20:4에서 다윗의 용사들의 같은 싸움을 전할 때는 '게셀'이라 한다.

entries.definition: GOB'LET. See Cup.
entries.definition_ko: 잔 참조.

entries.definition: GOD (good). The name of the Creator of all things and the supreme Governor of the universe and the Giver of all good gifts. He is "a Spirit, infinite, eternal, and unchangeable in his being, wisdom, power, holiness, justice, goodness, and truth." He is revealed to us in an endless variety of ways in his works and providential government, Rom 1:20, but more fully in the Holy Scriptures and in the person and work of his only begotten Son, our Lord. Names. — There are three principal designations of God in the O.T. — Elohim, Jehovah, and Adonai. The first is used exclusively in the first chapter of Genesis; it predominates in the second book of Psalms (Ps 42-72, called the Elohim Psalms), and occurs alternately with the other names in the other parts of the O.T. It expresses his character as the almighty Maker and his relation to the whole world, the Gentiles as well as the Jews. The second is especially used of him in his relation to Israel as the (God of the covenant, the God of revelaition and redemption. "Adonai" (i.e. say Lord) is used where God is reverently addressed, and is always substituted by the Jews for "Jehovah," which they never pronounce. These three words are indiscriminately translated, in the English Version, God, Lord, and Jehovah. The Nature of God. — God is revealed to us as a trinity consisting of three Persons who are of one essence, Matt 28:19; 2 Cor 13:14;John 1:1-3— God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Ghost. To the Father is ascribed the work of creation, to the Son the redemption, to the Holy Spirit the sanctification; but all three Persons take part in all the divine works. Although this idea of God is not brought out as prominently in the O.T. as in the New, it is nevertheless there. It is intimated in Gen 1, where God, the Word ("God spake," etc., compare Ps 33:6; John 1:1, John 1:3), and the Spirit of God are mentioned in the work of creation. The "divine Wisdom" of Prov 8 is personified, and corresponds to the "Word" in John 1, and refers to the second Person of the Trinity. To each of these Persons of the Trinity are ascribed the essential attributes of the supreme God. Thus, the Son is represented as the Mediator of the creation. John 1:3; Col 1:16; Heb 1:4. The unity of the Godhead is emphasized in the O.T., while the trinity is only shadowed forth, or at best faintly brought out. The grand reason for the emphasis of the unity of the Godhead was to show the fallacy of polytheism and to discourage idolatry, which the heathen practised. God is denominated "one Lord," Deut 6:4. Over against the false deities of the heathen, he is designated the "living" God. This belief in God as one was a chief mark of the Jewish religion. The attributes of God are those of the most perfect being. He is holy, Josh 24:19; eternal, 1 Tim 1:17; everywhere present, Ps 139:7; Acts 17:24; almighty, Gen 17:1; immutable, Ps 102:20. God is, moreover, just, Jer 9:24, wise, Job 12:13, and above all he is Love, 1 John 4:16.
entries.definition_ko: 만물의 창조주이자 우주의 지존한 통치자, 모든 좋은 선물을 주시는 분의 이름이다. 그분은 '영이시니 그 존재와 지혜와 권능과 거룩하심과 공의와 선하심과 진실하심이 무한하시고 영원하시며 불변하시다.' 그 지으신 것과 섭리로 다스리심 가운데 끝없이 다양하게(롬 1:20), 더 온전하게는 성경과 그 독생자이신 우리 주님의 인격과 사역으로 우리에게 계시되셨다. 구약에 하나님을 가리키는 주요 명칭이 셋 있다 — 엘로힘, 여호와, 아도나이다. 첫째는 창세기 1장에 오로지 쓰이고 시편 제2권(42-72편)에 주로 나오며, 전능한 창조주로서의 성품과 유대인뿐 아니라 온 세상과의 관계를 나타낸다. 둘째는 언약의 하나님, 계시의 하나님으로서 이스라엘과의 관계에서 특히 쓰인다.

entries.definition: GOD'HEAD. Col 2:9. The nature or essential being of God. Acts 17:29; Rom 1:20.
entries.definition_ko: 하나님의 본성 또는 본질적 존재를 뜻한다(골 2:9, 행 17:29, 롬 1:20).

entries.definition: GOD'LINESS, piety resulting from the knowledge and love of God, and leading to the cheerful and constant obedience of his commands. 2 Pet 3:11. In 1 Tim 3:16 it imports the substance of revealed religion.
entries.definition_ko: 하나님을 알고 사랑함에서 비롯되어 그 명령에 기쁘고 한결같이 순종하게 하는 경건이다(벧후 3:11). 딤전 3:16에서는 계시된 신앙의 실체를 뜻한다.

entries.definition: GODS. Rulers and judges are so called in Ex 22:28; Ps 82:6; John 10:34 because they represent God.
entries.definition_ko: 통치자와 재판장이 하나님을 대표하므로 이렇게 불린다(출 22:28, 시 82:6, 요 10:34).

entries.definition: GOG and MA'GOG. Eze 38:2. Magog was the name of one of Japheth's sons. Gen 10:2. It was also a general name of a country north of the Caucasus or Mount Taurus, or for the people of that district. Gog was the king of the country. This people seems to have sustained relations of hostility to Israel, and is associated with Antichrist. Rev 20:8.
entries.definition_ko: 곡과 마곡(겔 38:2). 마곡은 야벳의 아들 중 하나의 이름이며(창 10:2), 또한 코카서스나 다우로스 산 북쪽 나라, 또는 그 지역 백성을 두루 가리키는 이름이었다. 곡은 그 나라의 왕이었다. 이 백성은 이스라엘과 적대 관계였던 듯하며 적그리스도와 결부된다(계 20:8).

entries.definition: GO'LAN (circle), one of the six cities of refuge in Manasseh given to the Levites. It was in Bashan, and the most northerly of the three cities of refuge east of the Jordan. Deut 4:43; Josh 20:8; Josh 21:27; 1 Chr 6:71. It was possibly 10 or 12 miles north-east of the Sea of Galilee, in the centre of Gaulanitis; some suggest Nawa as the site of Golan.
entries.definition_ko: 므낫세에 있어 레위인에게 준 여섯 도피성 중 하나다. 바산에 있었고 요단 동편 세 도피성 중 가장 북쪽이었다(신 4:43, 수 20:8, 21:27, 대상 6:71). 갈릴리 바다 북동쪽 10~12마일, 가울라니티스 한복판에 있었을 것이다.

entries.definition: GOLD. Gen 2:11. This heaviest and most malleable of metals is found at the present day chiefly in California and Australia. Several places are mentioned by the sacred writers as abounding in gold; such as Ophir, Job 28:16, Parvaim, 2 Chr 3:6, Sheba, and Raamah. Eze 27:22. Until after the time of David gold was never coined, but was sold by weight as a precious article of commerce. The use of gold was very common among the Hebrews. Several parts of the temple, its furniture and utensils, were overlaid with this precious metal. Ex 36:34-38; 1 Kgs 7:48-50. And many of the vessels of the wealthy, as well as their personal ornaments and insignia of office, were of gold. Gen 41:42; 1 Kgs 10:17-22; Esth 1:6-7; Dan 5:29; Luke 15:22; Jas 2:2.
entries.definition_ko: 가장 무겁고 가장 잘 펴지는 이 금속은 오늘날 주로 캘리포니아와 오스트레일리아에서 난다(창 2:11). 성경 기자들은 오빌(욥 28:16), 바르와임(대하 3:6), 스바와 라아마(겔 27:22) 등 금이 많이 나는 곳을 언급한다. 다윗 시대 이후까지 금은 주조되지 않고 값진 교역품으로 무게를 달아 팔렸다. 히브리인 사이에 금의 사용이 매우 흔해 성전의 여러 부분과 기물과 그릇을 이 귀금속으로 입혔다(출 36:34-38, 왕상 7:48-50). 부자들의 그릇과 장신구, 직인의 표도 금으로 만들었다(창 41:42, 왕상 10:17-22, 단 5:29, 눅 15:22).

entries.definition: GOLD'EN CAN'DLESTICK. See Candlestick.
entries.definition_ko: 촛대 참조.

entries.definition: GOL'GOTHA (skull), the Hebrew name of the spot where Jesus was crucified. Matt 27:33. See Calvary.
entries.definition_ko: '해골'이라는 뜻으로 예수께서 십자가에 못 박히신 곳의 히브리어 이름이다(마 27:33). 갈보리 참조.

entries.definition: GOLI'ATH (splendor), a renowned champion of the Philistines from Gath. 1 Sam 17:4. He was more than 9 feet in height. Conscious of his superior stature and strength, he defied the armies of Israel to produce a rival. But he was met and slain by David, who, although a pygmy in the eyes of the giant, was mighty through the assistance of God. In 2 Sam 21:19 another Goliath of Gath, "the staff of whose spear was like a weaver's beam," is mentioned as being slain by Elhanan. He may have been a son of David's antagonist. 2 Sam 21:22.
entries.definition_ko: 가드 출신의 이름난 블레셋 용사다(삼상 17:4). 키가 9피트가 넘었다. 자기 체구와 힘을 믿고 이스라엘 군대에 맞설 자를 내라고 조롱했으나, 거인의 눈에는 난쟁이였으되 하나님의 도우심으로 강했던 다윗을 만나 죽임을 당했다. 삼하 21:19에는 '베틀채 같은 창자루'를 가진 또 다른 가드 사람 골리앗이 엘하난에게 죽임을 당했다고 나오는데, 다윗의 적수의 아들이었을 수 있다.

entries.definition: GO'MER (perfect). The eldest son of Japheth, progenitor of the ancient Cimmerians, and of the present Celtic peoples of Europe. Gen 10:2-3; 1 Chr 1:5-6. The wife of Hosea. Hos 1:3.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 야벳의 맏아들로 고대 킴메르인과 오늘날 유럽 켈트 민족의 조상(창 10:2-3, 대상 1:5-6). 2) 호세아의 아내(호 1:3).

entries.definition: GOMOR'RAH (submersion), one of the five cities in the vale of Siddim, Gen 14:1-11; destroyed for its wickedness, Gen 18:20; Gen 19:24, Gen 19:28; made a warning by Moses, Deut 29:23; Deut 32:32; referred to by Isaiah 1:9-10; by Jeremiah 23:14; Jeremiah 49:18; Jeremiah 50:40; by Amos 4:11; by Zephaniah 2:9; by our Saviour, Matt 10:15; Mark 6:11; by Paul, quoting Isaiah, Rom 9:29; by Peter and Jude, 2 Pet 2:6. Its site is disputed. Some place it at the southern, others at the northern, end of the Dead Sea. The name Wady ?'Amriyek?, at the north-west side of the Dead Sea, is like the Hebrew for Gomorrah. See Sodom and Salt Sea.
entries.definition_ko: 싯딤 골짜기의 다섯 성읍 중 하나로(창 14:1-11) 그 악함 때문에 멸망했다(창 18:20, 19:24,28). 모세가 이를 경고로 삼았고(신 29:23, 32:32) 이사야, 예레미야, 아모스, 스바냐가 언급했으며, 구주와 바울, 베드로와 유다도 언급한다(마 10:15, 롬 9:29, 벧후 2:6). 그 위치는 논란이 있어 사해 남쪽 끝으로 보는 이도, 북쪽 끝으로 보는 이도 있다.

entries.definition: GOODMAN OF THE HOUSE is the master of the house, irrespective of moral character. The term was in common use when the A.V. was made. Matt 20:11.
entries.definition_ko: 도덕적 성품과 무관하게 집주인을 뜻한다(마 20:11). 흠정역이 만들어질 당시 흔히 쓰이던 말이다.

entries.definition: GO'PHER-WOOD. The ark was constructed of this material. Gen 6:14. There are many theories as to what gopher-wood was. One is that it was some resinous wood, such as cedar, pine, or fir. Still more probable is the opinion that it was cypress, which was considered by the ancients as the most durable wood, and least exposed to worms and natural decay. It abounded in Syria, was used very commonly for shipbuilding, and was almost the only wood which could furnish suitable timber for so large a vessel as the ark.
entries.definition_ko: 방주가 이 재료로 지어졌다(창 6:14). 무엇인지에 대해 여러 설이 있는데, 백향목이나 소나무, 전나무 같은 수지성 목재라는 설이 하나다. 더 유력한 견해는 사이프러스로, 고대인이 가장 오래가고 벌레와 자연 부패에 가장 강하다고 여긴 나무다. 수리아에 많이 자랐고 배를 만드는 데 흔히 쓰였으며, 방주만큼 큰 배에 알맞은 목재를 댈 수 있는 거의 유일한 나무였다.

entries.definition: GO'SHEN. The portion of Egypt assigned to Israel. Gen 45:5, Gen 45:10; Gen 46:28; Gen 47:27-50:8. It probably bordered on the Tanitic branch of the Nile, hence called Zoan or Tauis, Ps 78:12, and reached from the Mediterranean to the Red Sea. It was suited to shepherds, abounded in vegetables. It contained the treasure-cities Rameses and Pithom, Goshen was near the royal capital. Gen 48:1-2; Ex 5:20; appears to have been the starting place of the Israelites in their journey to the Land of Promise. Ex 12:37-38. A district in Palestine, perhaps between Gibeon and Gaza. Josh 10:41; Num 11:16. A city in the hill-country of Judah, Josh 15:51; perhaps now Sekiyeh.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 이스라엘에게 배정된 애굽의 한 지역이다(창 45:10, 46:28, 47:27). 나일의 다니스 지류에 접해 있었을 것이며 지중해에서 홍해까지 이르렀다. 목자에게 알맞고 채소가 풍부했다. 국고성 라암셋과 비돔이 그 안에 있었고 왕도에 가까웠다(창 48:1-2). 약속의 땅으로 가는 여정의 출발지였던 듯하다(출 12:37-38). 2) 팔레스타인의 한 지역으로 아마도 기브온과 가사 사이다(수 10:41). 3) 유다 산지의 한 성읍(수 15:51).

entries.definition: GOS'PEL (from the Anglo-Saxon god-spell, "good tidings") is the English translation of the Greek euangelion, which signifies "good" or "glad tidings." Luke 2:10; Acts 13:32. The same word in the original is rendered in Rom 10:15 by the two equivalents "gospel" and "glad tidings." The term refers to the good news of the new dispensation of redemption ushered in by the life, death, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. The "good news" is denominated either simply the "gospel," Matt 26:13, or else "the gospel of the kingdom," Matt 9:35; of "Jesus Christ," Mark 1:1; of "peace," Rom 10:15; Eph 6:15, of "salvation," Eph 1:12; of "God," 1 Thess 2:9; and of "grace." Acts 20:24. Gospels, the Four Canonical. The word "Gospels" is also employed to designate the four biographies of our Lord by Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. These are the only faithful accounts of his life extant. They are the independent recitals of well-informed men; and there is no evidence that either Evangelist got his facts from another. But the Gospel by John, while it is complete on its own peculiar plan, seems to have been composed in part with the object of supplementing what was lacking or only partially given in the narrations of the first three Gospels. In this fourth Gospel, for example, the divinity of our Lord is emphatically asserted and dwelt on at length, and of the opposition he met with from the Pharisees a full account is given, John 6-12. John further gives in detail the discourses of our Lord in the last week, John 13-17, and the account of the resurrection of Lazarus, John 11. On the other hand, he omits the circumstances of our Lord's birth, which had been given so fully by Matthew and Luke, the account of the Lord's Supper, related by all three of the other Evangelists, the institution of baptism, and most of the miracles and all the parables found in the first three accounts. There are differences in the accounts of the same events as given by the various Evangelists, but with a few exceptions they are verbal, and only such as we would naturally expect in different descriptions of the same occurrences. These very differences in details are favorable to the genuineness of the Gospels, because they prove the absence of collusion or secret agreement among the writers. The genuineness of these records of our Lord's life is as strongly supported, to say the least, as that of any other document of antiquity. There is no doubt that they were all written, as we have them, in the first century (the first three before the destruction of Jerusalem, a.d. 70), and were all used and known as "the Four Evangelists" in the Church before the year 200, if not before 150. Upon both these points the concurrent evidence is so strong that the opponents must resort to the wildest theories and hypotheses, which refute themselves by their contradictions. There is good evidence scattered all through the second century that they were in general use. Justin Martyr used them about 140. His pupil, Tatian, wrote a Harmony of the Gospels about 170, and quite recently a commentary of Ephraem Syrus on Tatian's Diatessaron has been published at Venice (1876), which settles the vexed question as to the character of this work. The arguments for the genuineness, as varied as they are convincing, are such as these:(1) The direct testimonies of writers in the second century and later; (2) the quotations found in the writings of the authors known as the Fathers; (3) ancient translations, as the Itala and Peshito, dating from the second century; (4) the attitude of heretic and heathen opponents, who, like Celsus (180), did not call in question the genuineness of the records, although they denied the credibility of a part of their contents. Basilides, a Gnostic heretic, knew the Gospel of John as early as 125, and Marcion, another Gnostic, about 150, made use of a mutilated Gospel of Luke. The language in which the Gospels were written was the Greek, with the probable exception of Matthew written in Hebrew, and there can be little doubt that we now have, with the exception of a few readings, the documents as they left the hands of the writers. Gospels, Apocryphal. These are the spurious accounts of our Lord's life. There are many of them; as, for example, the Gospel according to James, according to Nicodemns, etc. The earliest was probably composed sometime in the second century. They indulge in puerile accounts of the parents of our Lord, of the pretended miracles of his childhood, and of his experience in Hades. These stories were invented to satisfy a prurient curiosity, and were accepted by the credulous. The circumstances related carry their own refutation with them, as being entirely out of harmony with the spirit of our Lord's life. They tend to confirm the canonical Gospels as the counterfeit presupposes the genuine coin. A "harmony" of the Gospels is an arrangement of these four biographies which displays the chronology of the events narrated, the variety of events, and the diversity of details. The object is to present a full account of our Lord's life in the chronological sequence of its events. For the several Gospels see Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John.
entries.definition_ko: 고대 영어 '좋은 소식'에서 온 말로, '좋은 소식' 또는 '기쁜 소식'을 뜻하는 헬라어 유앙겔리온의 번역어다(눅 2:10, 행 13:32). 롬 10:15에서는 같은 원어가 '복음'과 '좋은 소식' 두 말로 옮겨졌다. 예수 그리스도의 삶과 죽음과 부활로 열린 새로운 구속의 경륜에 관한 좋은 소식을 가리킨다. 그냥 '복음'(마 26:13)이라 하거나 '천국 복음'(마 9:35), '예수 그리스도의 복음'(막 1:1), '화평의 복음'(롬 10:15), '구원의 복음'(엡 1:13), '하나님의 복음'(살전 2:9), '은혜의 복음'(행 20:24)이라 불린다. 또한 마태·마가·누가·요한이 쓴 주님의 네 전기를 가리키는 데도 쓰인다.

entries.definition: GOURD. Jon 4:6. Probably the plant which shaded the prophet was either the castor-oil plant (Ricinus communis), which in the East grows rapidly to the height of even 15 feet, or, according to rapidly-prevailing opinion, it was a vine of the cucumber family (Cucurbita pepo), similar to our gourd, and still used for shade in Palestine. " In the gardens about Sidon many an arbor Castor-Oil Plant. (Ricinus communis) of gourds may be seen. But the plant withers as rapidly as it shoots, and after a storm or any injury to the stem its fruit may be seen hanging to the leafless tendrils which so lately concealed it-a type of melancholy desolation."-Tristram. Some have regarded the expression, "It came up in a night and perished in a night," as literal, others as indicating merely rapid growth. The declaration that the Lord prepared a gourd, and prepared a worm, and prepared an east wind, indicates the direct and special interposition of his providence to teach the prophet a lesson of submission to the divine will. Gourd, Wild. The wild gourds eaten by the sons of the prophets, 2 Kgs 4:38-41, were doubtless the handsome yet poisonous fruit of the colocynth (Citrullus colocynthis), from which the medicine of that name is obtained. This vine is not common in Palestine, yet may be found about Gilgal, and bears a fruit resembling an orange in size and shape, but very hard and having its yellow rind marbled with green and Colocynthus, or Wild Gourd. (Citrullus colocynthis. After Tristram.) white. The plant resembles the watermelon, and belongs to the same family. For various reasons it is thought that the "knops" used in the ornamental work of Solomon's temple were imitations of the colocynth. 1 Kgs 6:18.
entries.definition_ko: 선지자에게 그늘을 준 식물은 아마도 동방에서 15피트 높이까지 빠르게 자라는 아주까리이거나, 오늘날 널리 지지받는 견해대로 우리의 박과 비슷하며 지금도 팔레스타인에서 그늘용으로 쓰이는 박과 덩굴이었을 것이다(욘 4:6). 시돈 주변 동산에 박 그늘이 여럿 보이나, 이 식물은 자란 만큼 빨리 시들어 폭풍이나 줄기가 상하면 잎 진 덩굴에 열매만 매달린 쓸쓸한 모습이 된다. 여호와께서 박을 예비하시고 벌레를 예비하시고 동풍을 예비하셨다는 말은 선지자에게 순복의 교훈을 주시려는 특별한 섭리의 개입을 나타낸다.

entries.definition: GOVERNOR. Matt 27:2. After Judaea became a province of the Roman empire, governors or procurators were appointed and sent thither from Rome. This was the office held by Pontius Pilate at the time of our Saviour's crucifixion. Sometimes the word "governor" is used as a general title for a ruler or presiding officer. Gen 42:6. See Feast.
entries.definition_ko: 유대가 로마 제국의 속주가 된 후 총독 또는 procurator가 로마에서 임명되어 파견되었다(마 27:2). 구주께서 십자가에 못 박히실 당시 본디오 빌라도가 맡았던 직분이다. 때로 '치리자'라는 일반적 칭호로도 쓰인다(창 42:6).

entries.definition: GO'ZAN, a district of Mesopotamia, 2 Kgs 17:6; 2 Kgs 18:11; 2 Kgs 19:12; 1 Chr 5:26; Isa 37:12; probably identical with Gauzanitis of Ptolemy, and Mygdonia of other writers. It was watered by the Habor, the modern Khabour, a large branch of the Euphrates in Mesopotamia.
entries.definition_ko: 메소보다미아의 한 지역이다(왕하 17:6, 18:11, 19:12, 대상 5:26, 사 37:12). 유브라데의 큰 지류인 오늘날의 하부르인 하볼 강이 그 땅을 적셨다.

entries.definition: GRACE denotes the love of God as displayed in his free favor toward men as sinners and destitute of all claim upon him. 1 Tim 1:2. Hence the N.T., which reveals the plan by which this grace is bestowed, is called "the gospel of the grace of God." Acts 20:24. The apostolic Epistles begin with the salutation, "Grace and peace be with you."
entries.definition_ko: 죄인이며 그분께 아무 자격도 없는 사람들을 향해 값없이 베푸시는 하나님의 사랑을 뜻한다(딤전 1:2). 그래서 이 은혜가 어떻게 주어지는지 그 계획을 밝히는 신약을 '하나님의 은혜의 복음'이라 부른다(행 20:24). 사도들의 서신은 '은혜와 평강이 너희에게 있을지어다'라는 인사로 시작한다.

entries.definition: GRAIN. See Corn.
entries.definition_ko: 곡식 참조.

entries.definition: GRAPES, the fruit of the vine. Gen 49:11. When fully ripe and dried they are called "raisins." 1 Sam 25:18; 1 Sam 30:12; 2 Sam 16:1; 1 Chr 12:40. The soil and climate of Palestine are pre-eminently well suited to the growth of the vine, and it has always been among the principal productions of the country. In Judaea especially particular districts were famed for the excellency of their grapes; as En-gedi and the vales of Eshcol and Sorek. The word "Sorek" is not only the name of a region in the tribe of Judah, but also signifies the noblest variety of the vine and its clusters, which there abounded. This grape was white, with delicious juice, and with seeds so small and soft as to be almost imperceptible. In Persia the best raisins are made of this grape. It is of this that the celebrated Kishmich wine of Shiraz is made. Very fine grapes were in old times, as at present, produced on Mount Lebanon and at Helbon or Aleppo. Travellers agree in relating that Palestine, even in its present state of subjugation to the Mussulmans, who are forbidden to use wine, produces clusters of 12 pounds' weight each, the single grapes of which are as large as plums. They tell us that the clusters of Judaea, a few miles westward from Jerusalem, are larger than any in Europe, and that they have often seen clusters of such size that it was impossible for a single man to carry one of them uninjured for any distance. Brocard informs us in his Travels that the best vines grow in the environs of Bethlehem, in the vale of Rephaim (between Bethlehem and Jerusalem), and in the traditional vale of Eshcol, near Hebron. The grapes of the Holy Land, with the exception of the Sorek, above mentioned, are mostly red or black. Hence the juice is called "the blood of the grape," translated, in our version, "red wine." Isa 27:2. Besides wine and raisins, there is made from grapes a syrup called dibs, which "is obtained by boiling down the juice of the ripe grapes to a third of its bulk, when it becomes as thick as treacle, but is of a lighter color. The Moslems are very fond of dibs, which they eat with bread, drink with water, and use largely in confectionery. The Hebrew name debash ('honey') is identical, and it is this syrup, and not bees' honey, which is understood to be meant by the honey which Jacob sent down as a present to the governor of Egypt, Gen 43:11, and in which the men of Tyre traded from the land of Israel. Eze 27:17." — Tristram. The Jews were expressly required by their law not to gather the grapes until the vine was three years old, Lev 19:23, and to leave some on the vines and some on the ground. Lev 19:10; and it was the privilege of the poor and dependent to gather these for their own use, provided they were eaten on the ground. They were not allowed to take any away. Deut 23:24; Deut 24:21. The grapes thus left were called "the gleanings," and as they hung, here and there one, on the vines or lay scattered on the ground, they were strikingly emblematical of the depopulation of a city or country, Isa 17:6; Isa 24:13; Jer 6:9; Jer 49:9; Ob. 5. See Vine, Vineyard, Wine, Winepress,
entries.definition_ko: 포도나무의 열매다(창 49:11). 완전히 익어 말린 것을 '건포도'라 한다(삼상 25:18, 30:12). 팔레스타인의 토양과 기후는 포도 재배에 매우 알맞아 언제나 그 땅의 주요 산물이었다. 특히 유대에서는 엔게디와 에스골, 소렉 골짜기가 좋은 포도로 이름났다. '소렉'은 유다 지파의 한 지역 이름일 뿐 아니라 그곳에 많던 가장 뛰어난 포도 품종과 그 송이를 뜻하기도 한다. 이 포도는 희고 즙이 맛있으며 씨가 작고 물러 거의 느껴지지 않는다.

entries.definition: GRASS. Isa 51:12. This word is frequently applied in the Scriptures to herbage generally, Isa 15:6, though sometimes distinction is made between such herbs as are used by man as grain and vegetables, and such as are used chiefly by cattle. Ps 104:14. The quick growth and tenderness of this species of vegetation furnish several of the most striking illustrations of the Scriptures. Ps 90:5-6; Ps 92:7; Ps 103:15-16; Isa 40:6-8; Jer 51:12; Jas 1:10; 1 Pet 1:24. The passage in Prov 27:25 would be more accurately rendered thus: "The grass (hay) appeareth, and the green herb (tender grass) showeth itself, and the plants (herbs) of the mountains are gathered." So in Isa 15:6: "The grass (hay) withereth, the green herb (grass) faileth, there is no green thing." Nothing can exceed in beauty and appropriateness the gradation of images employed by the prophet, 2 Kgs 19:26; the weakness and tenderness of the first shoots of any green herb; the frailty of the few spires of grass that sometimes spring up in the vegetable mould or shallow earth upon the housetop, or the withered blade of corn (grain) blasted before it rises into a stalk. Coarse herbage was often dried, as it is still, for the purpose of heating ovens. Under the fierce rays of a Syrian sun, joined to parching winds, it often happens that "the grass of the field which to-day is, . . . to-morrow is cast into the oven." Matt 6:30; Matt 13:30; Luke 12:28.
entries.definition_ko: 성경에서 이 말은 흔히 풀 종류 전반에 쓰이나(사 51:12, 15:6), 때로 사람이 곡식과 채소로 쓰는 것과 주로 가축이 먹는 것을 구별한다(시 104:14). 이 부류 식물이 빨리 자라고 연약한 것이 성경의 가장 인상적인 비유 여럿을 이룬다(시 90:5-6, 103:15-16, 사 40:6-8, 약 1:10, 벧전 1:24).

entries.definition: GRASS'HOPPER, an insect of the locust species, often mentioned in the sacred writings. Eccl 12:5. The word rendered "grasshopper" in the above-cited passage is rendered "locust" in 2 Chr 7:13. Grasshoppers were allowable food under the Jewish law. Lev 11:22. Their timidity is proverbial. Job 39:20. They are often found in great multitudes (hence the figurative language, Jud 6:5 and Num 7:12; Jer 46:23), and prove destructive to vegetation, especially in its early stages. Am 7:1. The allusion in Nah 3:15-17 is to a common habit of these insects. When benumbed with the cold, they assemble in vast numbers upon the hedges or other shrubbery; and such is their multitude that the places they occupy are darkened, and resemble the encamping-ground of a great army. As soon, however, as they are revived by the warmth of the sun, they fly away, no one knows whither. The grasshopper is used to illustrate comparative insignificance. Num 13:33; Isa 40:22; and in the passage from Ecclesiastes first cited, reference is probably made to that degree of weakness and infirmity in old age which makes the weight, or even the chirping, of a grasshopper burdensome.
entries.definition_ko: 성경에 자주 언급되는 메뚜기류의 곤충이다(전 12:5). 위 구절에서 '메뚜기'로 옮긴 말이 대하 7:13에서는 '황충'으로 번역된다. 유대 율법에서 먹을 수 있는 것이었다(레 11:22). 그 겁 많음은 속담이 되었다(욥 39:20). 흔히 큰 무리로 나타나(삿 6:5, 렘 46:23) 식물, 특히 어린 싹에 큰 피해를 준다(암 7:1). 나 3:15-17은 이 곤충의 흔한 습성을 가리킨다 — 추위에 마비되면 엄청난 수로 울타리나 덤불에 모여드는데, 그 수가 많아 앉은 자리가 어두워지고 대군의 진지 같아 보인다. 그러나 햇볕에 되살아나면 어디론지 날아가 버린다.

entries.definition: GRATE, BRA'ZEN. See Altar.
entries.definition_ko: 제단 참조.

entries.definition: GRAVE. See Burial, Engrave, Hell.
entries.definition_ko: 장례, 새김, 지옥 참조.

entries.definition: GREAT SEA. Num 34:6. The Mediterranean Sea; called also "utmost sea" and "the hinder sea." Joel 2:20; Zech 14:8. See Sea.
entries.definition_ko: 지중해를 가리키며 '서해', '뒤쪽 바다'라고도 불린다(민 34:6, 욜 2:20, 슥 14:8).

entries.definition: GREAVES. See Armor.
entries.definition_ko: 병기 참조.

entries.definition: GRE'CIA. See Greece.
entries.definition_ko: 헬라 참조.

entries.definition: GREECE, or HELLAS, the well-known country in the south-east of Europe. It is named four times in the O.T. as Greece or Grecia, Zech 9:13; Dan 8:21; Num 10:20; Matt 11:2, and once in the N.T., Acts 20:2. It or its people are referred to in Hebrew history as Javan, Isa 66:19; Eze 27:13, Eze 27:19, and in apostolic history as Achaia. Its cities noticed in Scripture are Atliens, Corinth, and Cenchrea. See Greeks, and for further notice of the country, see Achaia and Macedonia.
entries.definition_ko: 유럽 남동부의 잘 알려진 나라다. 구약에 네 번 '헬라'로 언급되고(슥 9:13, 단 8:21, 10:20, 11:2) 신약에 한 번 나온다(행 20:2). 히브리 역사에서는 야완으로(사 66:19, 겔 27:13,19), 사도 시대 역사에서는 아가야로 언급된다. 성경에 나오는 그 성읍은 아덴, 고린도, 겐그레아다.

entries.definition: GREEKS, GRECIANS. These terms should be more distinguished. The "Greeks" were the Greeks by race. Acts 16:1, Acts 16:3; Josh 18:17, or else Gentiles as opposed to Jews. Rom 2:9-10, marg. But "Grecians" were foreign Jews as distinct from those in Palestine, who were called "Hebrews." Acts 11:20. The Greeks and Hebrews first met when the Tyrians sold the Jews to the Greeks. Joel 3:6. "Prophetical notice of Greece occurs in Dan 8:21, etc., where the history of Alexander and his successors is rapidly sketched. Zechariah 9:13, foretells the triumphs of the Maccabees over the Graeco-Syrian empire, while Isaiah looks forward to the conversion of the Greeks, amongst other Gentiles, through the instrumentality of Jewish missionaries. Is 66:19."After the complete subjugation of the Greeks by the Romans, and the absorption into the Roman empire of the kingdoms which were formed out of the dominions of Alexander, Sketch-Map of Greece. the political connection between the Greeks and the Jews as two independent nations no longer existed." — Smith:Dictionary of the Bible.
entries.definition_ko: 이 두 말은 더 뚜렷이 구별해야 한다. '헬라인'은 혈통상 헬라 사람이거나(행 16:1,3) 유대인과 대비되는 이방인을 뜻한다(롬 2:9-10 난외주). 그러나 '헬라파 유대인'은 팔레스타인의 유대인('히브리인')과 구별되는 외국 출신 유대인이다(행 11:20). 헬라인과 히브리인이 처음 만난 것은 두로 사람들이 유대인을 헬라인에게 팔았을 때다(욜 3:6). 단 8:21에는 알렉산더와 그 후계자들의 역사가 빠르게 그려진 헬라에 대한 예언적 언급이 있다.

entries.definition: GREY'HOUND is the A.V. translation for the Hebrew words, meaning "one girt about the loins." Prov 30:31. That a "greyhound" does not answer to the meaning of the Hebrew is generally agreed. The most probable rendering yet suggested is that of a "wrestler" girded for the fight; others explain it of the war-horse, which is so poetically described in the book of Job 39:19-25.
entries.definition_ko: '허리를 동인 자'를 뜻하는 히브리어를 흠정역이 이렇게 옮겼다(잠 30:31). '그레이하운드'가 히브리어의 뜻에 맞지 않는다는 데는 대체로 견해가 일치한다. 지금까지 제시된 가장 유력한 번역은 싸움을 위해 띠를 두른 '씨름꾼'이며, 욥 39:19-25에 시적으로 묘사된 군마로 보는 이도 있다.

entries.definition: GRIND. See Mills.
entries.definition_ko: 맷돌 참조.

entries.definition: GRIND'ERS, in Eccl 12:3, represent the double teeth used in mastication.
entries.definition_ko: 전 12:3의 '맷돌질하는 자들'은 씹는 데 쓰는 어금니를 나타낸다.

entries.definition: GRIZ'ZLED, black and white intermingled in small spots. Gen 31:10; Zech 6:3, 1 Kgs 6:6.
entries.definition_ko: 검은빛과 흰빛이 작은 점으로 뒤섞인 것을 뜻한다(창 31:10, 슥 6:3,6).

entries.definition: GROVE. The translation, except in Gen 21:33, of the Hebrew word asherah; but since asherah is regarded by the best interpreters to be an "idol" or an idolatrous pillar (an image of Astarte, and not a "grove,") the translation is misleading, as in 1 Kgs 18:19; 2 Kgs 13:6, and other places. See Ashtoreth. But it is likely that this asherah was often set up in a grove, because thus would be given that seclusion necessary to the cruel and indecent rites which marked, among Oriental nations, the worship of false divinities.
entries.definition_ko: 창 21:33을 제외하면 히브리어 '아세라'를 옮긴 말이다. 그러나 최고의 주석가들은 아세라를 '우상' 또는 우상숭배의 기둥(아스다롯의 형상)으로 보지 '수풀'로 보지 않으므로 이 번역은 오해를 부른다(왕상 18:19, 왕하 13:6). 다만 이 아세라가 흔히 수풀에 세워졌을 가능성은 높으니, 동방 민족들의 거짓 신 숭배를 특징짓던 잔혹하고 음란한 의식에 필요한 은밀함이 그렇게 얻어졌기 때문이다.

entries.definition: GUARD -CHAM'BER, the apartment occupied by the king's guard. 1 Kgs 14:28.
entries.definition_ko: 왕의 호위병이 머물던 방(왕상 14:28).

entries.definition: GUD'GODAH. Deut 10:7. See Hor-Hagidgad.
entries.definition_ko: 홀하깃갓 참조(신 10:7).

entries.definition: GUEST. See Hospitality.
entries.definition_ko: 환대 참조.

entries.definition: GUESTS-CHAMBER. See Chamber.
entries.definition_ko: 객실 참조.

entries.definition: GUIL'TY OF BLOOD, Num 35:27, Num 35:31; GUILTY OF DEATH, Matt 26:66; Mark 14:64. This phrase in the last two passages means "deserving of death ;" in the former it means simply "guilty of blood-shedding."
entries.definition_ko: 민 35:27,31의 '피 흘린 죄'와 마 26:66, 막 14:64의 '사형에 해당한 자'를 가리킨다. 뒤의 두 구절에서는 '죽어 마땅하다'는 뜻이고, 앞의 것은 단순히 '피를 흘린 죄가 있다'는 뜻이다.

entries.definition: GU'NI (painted). A son of Naphtali. Gen 46:24; Num 26:48; 1 Chr 7:13. One of Gad's posterity. 1 Chr 6:15.
GUR (whelp, or abode), an ascent from the plain of Jezreel. 2 Kgs 9:27. Drake suggests Keft Kud, near Jenin, as its site.
entries.definition_ko: 이스르엘 평야에서 올라가는 비탈이다(왕하 9:27).

entries.definition: GUR-BA'AL (abode of Baal), a place in the desert, south-east of Judah. 2 Chr 26:7.
entries.definition_ko: '바알의 거처'라는 뜻으로 유다 남동쪽 광야의 한 곳이다(대하 26:7).

entries.definition: HAAHASH'TARI (the courier), a Judite. 1 Chr 4:6.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 사람(대상 4:6).

entries.definition: HABA'IAH (whom Jehovah hides), a priest, the ancestor of some who returned from exile. Ezr 2:61; Neh 7:3.
entries.definition_ko: 제사장으로, 포로에서 돌아온 이들의 조상이다(스 2:61, 느 7:63).

entries.definition: HAB'AKKUK, or HABBAK'KUK (embrace), one of the twelve minor prophets, of whose birth we know neither the time nor the place. He lived in the reign of Jehoiakim or of Josiah. Prophecy of, relates chiefly to the invasion of Judaea by the Chalditans, Hab 1, and the subsequent punishment of the Chaldajans themselves, ch. Hab 2. The passage Hab 2:4, "the just shall live by his faith," furnished to Paul the text for his Epistle to the Romans. Rom 1:17; comp. Gal 3:11. The third chapter is an eloquent and sublime psalm upon the majesty of God. Bishop Lowth says, "This anthem is unequalled in majesty and splendor of language and imagery."
entries.definition_ko: 열두 소선지자 중 하나로 태어난 때와 곳을 알 수 없다. 여호야김이나 요시야 때 살았다. 그 예언은 주로 갈대아의 유대 침공(1장)과 그 후 갈대아 자신이 받을 형벌(2장)을 다룬다. '의인은 그의 믿음으로 말미암아 살리라'(합 2:4)는 구절이 바울에게 로마서의 주제를 제공했다(롬 1:17, 갈 3:11). 셋째 장은 하나님의 위엄을 노래하는 유창하고 장엄한 시편이다. 로우스 주교는 '이 노래는 언어와 심상의 장엄함과 화려함에서 견줄 데가 없다'고 말한다.

entries.definition: HABAZINI'AH (light of Jehovah), a Rechabite. Jer 35:3.
entries.definition_ko: 레갑 사람(렘 35:3).

entries.definition: HABERGEON. See Armor.
entries.definition_ko: 병기 참조.

entries.definition: HA'BOR (perhaps rich in vegetation), a river of Gozan, 2 Kgs 17:6; 1 Chr 5:26; probably identical with the modern Khabour, the Aborrhas and Chaboras of ancient writers, and a branch of the Euphrates.
entries.definition_ko: 고산의 강이다(왕하 17:6, 대상 5:26). 유브라데의 지류인 오늘날의 하부르와 같은 강일 것이다.

entries.definition: HACHALI'AH (whom Jehovah afflicts), the father of Nehemiah. Neh 1:1; Dan 10:1.
entries.definition_ko: 느헤미야의 아버지(느 1:1, 10:1).

entries.definition: HACH'ILAH, HILL OF (the darksome hill), a place in Judah near Ziph, and where David with his 600 followers hid. 1 Sam 23:19; comp. 1 Sam 23:14-15, 1 Sam 23:18; 1 Sam 26:3. Conder was inclined to locate it at the ruins now called Yekin: "The hill Yekin is a bold promontory standing just at the edge of the plateau. It looks over the whole desert; the cliffs of En-gedi, the Dead Sea, and the heights of Moab are in full view. Just beneath the crest of the hill is a hollow, with another knoll beyond. It is the head of a great valley, which soon becomes precipitous, running down into the desert. In this hollow are a spring and a cave. This I imagine is what is meant by the 'trench.' 1 Sam 26:5. David is said to have crossed over to the other side, and we may imagine him standing on one or other of the hill-tops and looking down on the king and his sleeping party in the hollow."
entries.definition_ko: 십 근처 유다의 한 곳으로, 다윗이 육백 명과 함께 숨었던 곳이다(삼상 23:19, 26:3). 콘더는 지금 예킨이라 불리는 폐허로 보았는데, 고원 가장자리에 우뚝 선 곶으로 온 광야와 엔게디의 절벽, 사해, 모압의 고지가 한눈에 들어온다.

entries.definition: HACH'MONI, SON OF. The Hachmonites Jehiel and Jashobeam are so spoken of 1 Chr 27:32; 1 Chr 11:11. Hachmon was their ancestor.
entries.definition_ko: 학몬 사람 여히엘과 야소브암이 이렇게 불린다(대상 27:32, 11:11). 학모니는 그들의 조상이다.

entries.definition:
HA'DAD (sharpness), one of the sons of Ishmael, 1 Chr 1:30; he is called Hadar in Gen 25:15.

HA'DAD (a different name in Hebrew, meaning brave). King of Edom, who won a great victory over the Midianites on the field of Moab. His capital was Avith, which see. Gen 36:35; 1 Chr 1:46. Another king of Edom, with Pau for his capital, 1 Chr 1:50; called Hadar in Gen 36:39. A member of the royal house of Edom. In the general massacre of the males of Edom by Joab, 1 Kgs 11:15, he escaped, and fled into Egypt. Pharaoh received him with peculiar marks of favor, giving him his daughter in marriage. Subsequently, Hadad returned to Edom, and won for himself the reputation of an "adversary" of Solomon by the border-warfare he carried on against Israel. 1 Kgs 11:14, 1 Kgs 11:25.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 이스마엘의 아들 중 하나(대상 1:30). 창 25:15에서는 하달이라 불린다. 2) 에돔 왕으로 모압 들에서 미디안을 크게 무찔렀다. 수도는 아윗이었다(창 36:35, 대상 1:46). 3) 바우를 수도로 한 또 다른 에돔 왕(대상 1:50). 창 36:39에서는 하달이라 불린다. 4) 에돔 왕가의 한 사람으로, 요압이 에돔의 남자들을 도륙할 때(왕상 11:15) 살아남아 애굽으로 도망했다. 바로가 각별한 호의로 맞아 자기 처제를 아내로 주었다. 후에 에돔으로 돌아와 이스라엘과 국경 전쟁을 벌여 솔로몬의 '대적'이라는 이름을 얻었다(왕상 11:14,25).

entries.definition: HA'DAD - RIM'MON, a place probably named from two Syrian idols, Hadad, the sun-god, and Rimmon. It was in the valley of Megiddo, Zech 12:11, and the scene of a great lamentation over the death of Josiah. 2 Kgs 23:29; 2 Chr 35:20-25. It is identified by Van de Velde with Rummaneh, 4 miles south of Lejun. Conder favors this.
entries.definition_ko: 수리아의 두 우상, 곧 태양신 하닷과 림몬에서 이름을 딴 것으로 보이는 곳이다. 므깃도 골짜기에 있었고(슥 12:11) 요시야의 죽음을 크게 애곡한 무대다(왕하 23:29, 대하 35:20-25).

entries.definition: HADADE'ZER, or HADARE'ZER (Hadad's help), a king of Zobah. He was twice defeated bv King David's armies. 2 Sam 8:3; 2 Sam 10:16. On the first occasion 20,000 of the enemy were slain and 1000 chariots were taken. Amongst the spoil were shields of gold, 1 Chr 18:7, which David took to Jerusalem. Some years afterward. Hadadezer and three other Syrian princes formed an alliance to assist the Ammonites against David; but the whole Syrian army was defeated on the east bank of the Jordan by the Israelites under the command of Joab. Between 40,000 and 50,000 of the enemy were killed, including their principal general, and they thenceforth became tributary to David. 1 Chr 19:16-19.
entries.definition_ko: 소바 왕으로, 다윗의 군대에게 두 번 패했다(삼하 8:3, 10:16). 첫 번째에 적군 2만이 죽고 병거 천 대를 빼앗겼으며, 전리품 중 금 방패가 있어 다윗이 예루살렘으로 가져갔다(대상 18:7). 몇 해 후 하닷에셀과 다른 세 시리아 제후가 동맹해 암몬을 도와 다윗을 치려 했으나, 요압이 이끄는 이스라엘군에게 요단 동편에서 전 시리아군이 패했다. 사령관을 포함해 4~5만이 죽었고 그 후로 다윗에게 조공을 바쳤다(대상 19:16-19).

entries.definition: HA'DAR (room). Gen 25:15. See Hadad. Gen 36:39. See Hadad, 2.
HADARE'ZER. See Hadadezer.
entries.definition_ko: 하닷에셀 참조.

entries.definition: HAD'ASHAH, or HADA'SHAH (new), a town in the plain of Judah, Josh 15:37; probably the Adasa of the Maccabaean history, and corresponding well in name and position to modern Abdas.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 평지의 한 성읍이다(수 15:37).

entries.definition: HADAS'SAH (myrtle). See Esther.
entries.definition_ko: 에스더 참조.

entries.definition: HADAT'TAH(new), a town named as in the extreme south of Judah. Josh 15:25. Fuerst proposes to read Hazorhadattah (New Hazor), as distinct from the Hazor in v. Acts 15:23; Wilton would identify it with an imposing ruin called Kaer el-Adadah.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 최남단의 성읍으로 언급된다(수 15:25).

entries.definition: HA'DES (the unseen world, the spirit-world) occurs eleven times in the Greek Testament (Matt 11:23; 1 Cor 16:18; Acts 2:31; Rev 1:18, etc.), and ought to have been retained in the English Version (as it probably will be in the Revision) to distinguish it from Gehenna ("hell"). The word is used in Homer as a proper noun for Pluto, the god of the unseen or lower world, next brother to Zeus (Jupiter). In later writers it signifies a place, viz., the unseen spiritworld, the realm of the departed, the abode of the dead. The Greek view of Hades and the Roman view of Orcun is that of a place for all the dead in the depths of the earth -dark, dreary, cheerless and shut up, inaccessible to prayers and sacrifices, ruled over by Pluto. The Hebrew Sheol is the equivalent for the Greek Hades, and is so translated in the Septuagint. It is likewise the subterranean abode of all the dead, but only their temporary abode till the advent of the Messiah or the final judgment, and is divided into two departments, called paradise or Abraham's bosom for the good, and Gehenna or hell for the bad. The N.T. Hades does not differ essentially from the Hebrew Sheol, but Christ has broken the power of death, dispelled the darkness of Hades, and revealed to believers the idea of heaven as the state and abode of bliss in immediate prospect after a holy life. The English Version translates Hades and Gehenna by the same word ("hell"), except in 1 Cor 15:55 ("grave"), and thus obliterates the important distinction between the realm of the dead or spiritworld and the place of torment. Hades is a temporary jail or prison-house; heaven and hell are permanent and final. Since Christ's descent into Hades, or the unseen, the spirit world, believers need not fear to enter this realm through death. Christ declares, "I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell [Hades] and of death." Rev 1:18.
entries.definition_ko: '보이지 않는 세계', 곧 영들의 세계를 뜻하며 헬라어 신약에 열한 번 나온다(마 11:23, 행 2:31, 계 1:18 등). 게헨나('지옥')와 구별하기 위해 영어 성경에도 그대로 두었어야 했다. 호메로스에서는 보이지 않는 하계의 신 플루톤을 가리키는 고유명사로 쓰인다. 후대 저자들에게는 장소, 곧 보이지 않는 영들의 세계이자 떠난 자들의 영역, 죽은 자의 거처를 뜻한다. 헬라의 하데스와 로마의 오르쿠스는 땅속 깊은 곳에 있는 모든 죽은 자의 처소로 어둡고 음산하며 닫혀 있다는 관념이다. 히브리어 스올이 헬라어 하데스에 해당하며 칠십인역이 그렇게 옮긴다. 마찬가지로 모든 죽은 자의 지하 거처이나, 메시아가 오시거나 최후 심판이 있기까지의 임시 처소이며 두 부분으로 나뉜다.

entries.definition: HA'DID (sharp), a place near Lod or Lydda. Ezr 2:33; Neh 7:37; Neh 11:34. Its site is probably that of the modern village el-Haditheh, 3 miles east of Lydda. See Adida.
entries.definition_ko: 롯 또는 룻다 근처의 한 곳이다(스 2:33, 느 7:37, 11:34). 룻다 동쪽 3마일의 오늘날 마을 엘하디데 자리로 추정된다.

entries.definition: HAD'LAI (resting), an Ephraimite, father of the chief of a tribe in the reign of Pekah. 2 Chr 28:12.
entries.definition_ko: 에브라임 사람으로, 베가 때 한 지파의 우두머리의 아버지다(대하 28:12).

entries.definition: HADO'RAM (fire-worshippers ?). 1. The fifth son of Joktan. Gen 10:27; 1 Chr 1:21. The tribe which sprang from him were probably the Adramitae, who lived on the south coast of Arabia. The son of Tou or Toi, king of Hamath, 1 Chr 18:10; called Joram in 2 Sam 8:10. The tax-collector stoned after Jeroboam's rebellion, 2 Chr 10:18; called Adoniram, 1 Kgs 4:6, and Adoram, 2 Sam 20:24.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 욕단의 다섯째 아들(창 10:27, 대상 1:21). 그에게서 난 부족은 아라비아 남해안에 살던 아드라미타이였을 것이다. 2) 하맛 왕 도우의 아들(대상 18:10). 삼하 8:10에서는 요람이라 불린다. 3) 여로보암의 반역 후 돌에 맞아 죽은 조세 감독관(대하 10:18). 왕상 4:6에서는 아도니람, 삼하 20:24에서는 아도람이라 불린다.

entries.definition: HA'DRACH, LAND OF (perhaps enclosure), a country of Syria, Zech 9:1-2, and conjectured to be the region about Damascus, including, perhaps, all of Coelo-Syria; or it may refer to the region around Hamath.
entries.definition_ko: 수리아의 한 나라로(슥 9:1-2), 다메섹 일대, 어쩌면 코엘레시리아 전체를 포함하는 지역으로 추측되며 하맛 주변을 가리킬 수도 있다.

entries.definition: HA'GAB (locust), one whose descendants returned from Babylon under Zerubbabel. Ezr 2:46.
entries.definition_ko: 스룹바벨 아래 바벨론에서 그 후손이 돌아온 사람(스 2:46).

entries.definition: HAG'ABA (locust), one whose sons were among the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel, Neh 7:48; called Hagabah in Ezr 2:45.
entries.definition_ko: 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 느디님 사람 중에 그 아들들이 있던 사람으로(느 7:48), 스 2:45에서는 하가바라 불린다.

entries.definition: HA'GAR (flight), an Egyptian woman who lived in the family of Abraham as bond-woman. At Sarah's own suggestion, she became the concubine of Abraham. When she conceived, her mistress was "despised in her eyes." Gen 16:4. In consequence of it, Hagar was harshly treated and fled away from the house of Abraham. She made her way toward Egypt, her native country, through the wilderness of Shur, and while resting herself near a fountain by the wayside she was visited by an angel, who promised her an innumerable seed and a son whose name was to be Ishmael. The angel at the same time directed her to return home and submit herself to her mistress. The place of this manifestation was afterward known as Beer-lahai-roi, "well of the living and seeing [God]." Gen 16:14. We lose sight of Hagar entirely from this time on till the festival of Isaac's weaning. On that occasion Sarah saw Ishmael mocking or making sport of her child. She immediately demanded the banishment of Ishmael and his mother from their home. Abraham was pained by the demand; but being divinely admonished to comply, he rose up early in the morning, and supplying Hagar with bread and a bottle of water sent her and her child away. She found her way to the wilderness of Beer-sheba; but her supply of water was exhausted. Placing the child under one of the shrubs that she might not see it die, she mingled her prayers with its cries. God heard the prayer, and disclosed to her a fountain. She at the same time received again the promise (fulfilled in the Arabs) that Ishmael would be the father of a great nation. Gen 21:9-21. Paul refers to Hagar, Gal 4:25, as a type of the Law and its bondage.
entries.definition_ko: 아브라함의 집에 여종으로 살던 애굽 여인이다. 사라 자신의 제안으로 아브라함의 첩이 되었다. 임신하자 여주인이 '그 눈에 멸시받는지라'(창 16:4) 하여 학대를 받고 아브라함의 집에서 도망쳤다. 고향 애굽을 향해 술 광야를 지나다가 길가 샘 곁에서 쉬던 중 천사의 방문을 받았는데, 천사는 셀 수 없는 자손과 이스마엘이라 이름할 아들을 약속하며 집으로 돌아가 여주인에게 복종하라 일렀다. 이 나타나심의 장소가 후에 브엘라해로이, 곧 '나를 살피시는 살아 계신 이의 우물'이라 알려졌다(창 16:14). 이후 이삭의 젖 떼는 잔치까지 하갈은 시야에서 사라진다. 그때 사라가 이스마엘이 자기 아이를 놀리는 것을 보고 즉시 이스마엘과 그 어미를 내쫓으라 요구했다.

entries.definition: HAGARENES', or HA'GARITES (Flight), a people dwelling east of the Jordan. 1 Chr 5:10, 1 Chr 5:19-20; 1 Chr 27:31. They seem to be distinguished from the Ishmaelites, Ps 83, but are usually regarded as having been named after Hagar, though some identify them with the Agrei. in the north-east of Arabia.
entries.definition_ko: 요단 동편에 살던 백성이다(대상 5:10,19-20, 27:31). 이스마엘 자손과 구별되는 듯하나(시 83:6) 대개 하갈에게서 이름을 딴 것으로 여겨진다.

entries.definition: HAG'GAI (festive), a prophet whose prophetic activity fell after the Captivity, in the second year of Darius Hystaspes, or b.c. 520, Hag 1:1. Nothing is known of his life. The Prophecy of, which is prosaic in style, concerns the repair of the temple, Hag 1:1-12; Hag 2:10-20, the glory of the second temple, Hag 2:1-9, and the triumph of Zerubbabel over his enemies. Hag 2:20-23. The prophet severely rebukes the people for their neglect to build the house of the Lord, and for their selfishness in living in the luxury of ceiled (or panelled) houses, while the temple was neglected. Hag 1:4. The people obeyed the prophet, and received the promise of God's presence. Am 1:13. The second chapter contains a Messianic reference, and alludes to Christ as the "Desire of all nations," Hag 2:7, or, as others render the passage, "the desirable things of all nations." The Hebrew reads, "They shall come, the desire of all nations, and I will fill this house with glory, saith the Lord of hosts."
entries.definition_ko: 포로기 이후, 다리오 히스타스페스 2년 곧 BC 520년에 활동한 선지자다(학 1:1). 그 생애에 대해서는 알려진 바가 없다. 그 예언은 산문체로, 성전 보수(1:1-12, 2:10-19), 둘째 성전의 영광(2:1-9), 스룹바벨이 원수들을 이길 것(2:20-23)을 다룬다. 선지자는 백성이 여호와의 집 짓기를 소홀히 하고 성전이 방치된 동안 판벽한 집의 호사를 누리는 이기심을 엄히 책망한다(학 1:4). 백성이 선지자에게 순종하자 하나님의 임재의 약속을 받았다(학 1:13). 둘째 장에는 메시아적 언급이 있어 그리스도를 '모든 나라의 보배'라 가리킨다(학 2:7).

entries.definition: HAG'GERI (wanderer), one of David's mighty men. 1 Chr 11:38.
entries.definition_ko: 다윗의 용사 중 하나(대상 11:38).

entries.definition: HAG'GI (festive), the second son of Gad, Gen 46:16; Num 26:15; founder of the Haggites.
entries.definition_ko: 갓의 둘째 아들이자(창 46:16, 민 26:15) 학기 족속의 조상이다.

entries.definition: HAGGI'AH (festival of Jehovah), a Merarite Levite, 1 Chr 6:30.
entries.definition_ko: 므라리 자손 레위인(대상 6:30).

entries.definition: HAG'GITH (a dancer), one of David's wives, and the mother of Adonijah. 2 Sam 3:4; 1 Kgs 1:5, etc.
entries.definition_ko: 다윗의 아내 중 하나이자 아도니야의 어머니(삼하 3:4, 왕상 1:5).

entries.definition: HAI (heap of ruins). See Ai.
entries.definition_ko: '폐허 무더기'라는 뜻. 아이 참조.

entries.definition: HAIL. When a very cold current of air encounters a hot and humid one, the vapor of the latter is suddenly condensed into drops, and sometimes these are frozen into irregular spheroids of porous ice, which fall to the earth as hail. This phenomenon is more frequent in temperate than in tropical regions, and usually occurs in summer and at the hottest hour of the day. Hail rarely falls except during thunderstorms; and hence the Bible commonly mentions it in connection with fire (lightning), as in Ps 148:8. As rain was always rare in Egypt, the fall of hail mentioned as the seventh plague, Ex 9, must have been singularly frightful, as it was greatly destructive to man, beast, and herb. God used a storm of hailstones to utterly rout and destroy the Amorites who fought with Joshua at Gibeon, Josh 10. In modern times stones of ice have been known to fall of half a pound in weight, and even eighteen ounces; and were it not that hail-storms are exceedingly local and rarely continue more than five or ten minutes, incalculable destruction would result. The largest hail falls in hot countries, where hail is less frequent. Inspiration often uses this agency figuratively to picture the awful judgments of God. In Rev 16:21 hail-stones are mentioned of a talent in weight, or, if the language were literal, of 55, and perhaps 11 1/2, pounds, according as the Attic or Jewish talent be intended; in all probability the former.
entries.definition_ko: 몹시 찬 기류가 뜨겁고 습한 기류를 만나면 후자의 수증기가 갑자기 응결해 물방울이 되고, 때로 이것이 얼어 성긴 얼음 덩이가 되어 우박으로 떨어진다. 이 현상은 열대보다 온대에서 잦고 대개 여름, 하루 중 가장 더운 때에 일어난다. 우박은 대개 뇌우 중에 떨어지므로 성경은 흔히 불(번개)과 함께 언급한다(시 148:8). 애굽에는 비가 늘 드물었으므로 일곱째 재앙으로 언급된 우박은(출 9장) 유난히 무서웠을 것이며 사람과 짐승과 초목에 큰 피해를 주었다. 하나님은 여호수아와 기브온에서 싸운 아모리 사람들을 우박으로 완전히 무찌르셨다(수 10장).

entries.definition: HAIR. The difference between the Hebrews and their neighbors, the Egyptians, in the matter of wearing their hair is early, though incidentally, alluded to in the Bible. Thus Joseph, on being summoned into the presence of Pharaoh, "shaved himself," while in most other countries it would have been sufficient to comb his hair and trim his beard. But the Egyptian men -out of notions of cleanliness perhaps- shaved their heads; the priests shaved their whole bodies every third day. The women, however, wore their natural hair long and plaited. In place of the Egyptian mode of wearing the hair. (From a painting. British Museum.) natural hair, wigs were worn by the men; and these were so constructed as to afford more protection against the sun than the more modern turbans. The Assyrians, and the Asiatics generally, the neighbors of the Hebrews on the east, had opposite customs in regard to the hair of men. On the Assyrian sculptures the hair appears long and combed closely down upon the head; the beard is also full length. False hair seems to have been plaited in to make the greater show.
