Much care was given to the hair. The Greeks were great admirers of long hair in both men and women. Their manner of wearing it varied. The Roman men at the time of Christ wore their hair short. Shaving was also customary, and a long beard was regarded as slovenly. The Hebrews were accustomed to cut the hair very much as we do, and must have used a kind of scissors, 2 Sam 14:26. But in the case of a vow or religious obligation they let it grow, as in the case of the Nazarites. Num 6:5; Jud 13:5. See Nazarites. The precept to the priests, Eze 44:20, requires an avoidance of extremes; so that the "Israelites" should neither resemble the priests of the heathen gods, who shaved their hair close, nor yet the Nazarites, who did not cut the hair at all. It was prohibited, Lev 19:27, to round the corners of the head -that is (as it is generally understood), to shave off the hair about the temples. The hair (especially black or dark hair) was considered an ornament, and it was anointed with aromatic oil, particularly on festivals and other joyous occasions. Ruth 3:3; 2 Sam 14:2; Ps 23:5; 92:10: Eccl 9:8; Luke 7:46. Combs and hair-pins are mentioned in the Talmud as in use among the Jews. The hair is spoken of by the apostle as a natural veil or covering to women, which it is a shame to put off, 1 Cor 11:15. It was plaited or braided, as is the custom at this day among the Asiatic women. The excessive care bestowed upon the head-dress led to the apostolic rebuke. 1 Tim 2:9; 1 Pet 3:3. See Head-dress. The practice of shaving the head in token of great affliction and humiliation for sin was common among the Hebrews even as early as Job's day, Job 1:20. So that the exhortation to cut off the hair is equivalent to an exhortation to begin a course of deep mourning and sorrow, Jer 7:29. A change in the color of the hair was one of the earliest indications of the leprosy, and hence, after recovery, the removal of the hair as the seat of disease was particularly enjoined. Lev 13:4, Num 13:10, Lev 13:31-32; Lev 14:8-9. See Leprosy. Baldness disqualified for the priesthood; artificial baldness was forbidden, Lev 21:5. See Baldness. Hair was employed by the Hebrews as an image of what was least valuable in man's person, 1 Sam 14:45:2 Sam 14:11; Matt 10:30; Luke 13:7; Acts 27:34, as well as of what was innumerable Ps 40:12; Ps 69:4, or particularly fine. Jud 20:16).
entries.definition_ko: 히브리인과 이웃 애굽인이 머리털을 다루는 방식의 차이가 성경에 일찍이 스치듯 언급된다. 요셉이 바로 앞에 불려 갈 때 '수염을 깎았다' 하는데, 다른 대부분의 나라에서는 머리를 빗고 수염을 다듬는 것으로 충분했을 것이다. 애굽 남자들은 아마도 청결의 관념에서 머리를 밀었고 제사장은 사흘마다 온몸을 밀었다. 다만 여자들은 긴 머리를 땋아 길렀다. 남자들은 자연모 대신 가발을 썼는데, 오늘날의 터번보다 햇볕을 더 잘 가려 주었다. 동쪽 이웃인 앗수르인과 아시아인 일반은 남자의 머리에 관해 정반대 관습을 지녀, 앗수르 조각에는 머리털이 길고 머리에 바싹 빗어 붙인 모습으로 나타난다.

entries.definition: HAK'KATAN (the small, or young), the father or chief of the sons of Azgad, Ezr 8:12.
entries.definition_ko: 아스갓 자손의 아버지 또는 우두머리(스 8:12).

entries.definition: HAK'KOZ (the thorn), the head of the seventh course of priests. 1 Chr 24:10.
entries.definition_ko: 제사장 일곱째 반차의 우두머리(대상 24:10).

entries.definition: HAKU'PHA (bent), one mentioned Ezr 2:51; Neh 7:53.
entries.definition_ko: 스 2:51과 느 7:53에 언급된 사람.

entries.definition: HA'LAH, a place in Assyria to which the ten tribes were carried captive. 2 Kgs 17:6; 2 Kgs 18:11; 1 Chr 5:26. It is now identified, with great probability, as the Chalcitis of Ptolemy, and in the north-west of Gauzanitis. Layard found a remarkable mound near the Khabour called Gla or Kalah, "castle," which covers the site of an ancient fortress or town. The Septuagint and Vulgate versions appear to regard Halah as a river, and it may have been the name of a river and of a town. The river was perhaps the Nahr al Huali, which is a branch of the Khabour.
entries.definition_ko: 열 지파가 사로잡혀 간 앗수르의 한 곳이다(왕하 17:6, 18:11, 대상 5:26). 프톨레마이오스의 칼키티스, 가우자니티스 북서쪽으로 상당히 유력하게 비정된다. 레이어드가 하부르 근처에서 글라 또는 칼라('요새')라 불리는 큰 흙무더기를 발견했는데 옛 요새나 성읍의 터를 덮고 있다.

entries.definition: HA'LAK, THE MOUNT (the smooth or the bald mountain), the name of a mountain marking the southern limit of Joshua's conquests. Josh 11:17; Acts 12:7. It has been variously identified with the range of hills parallel with Beer-sheba, with the modern Jebel el-Mukrek, 60 miles south of the Dead Sea, and with the range of white hills 8 miles south of the Dead Sea, and which divides the Ghor, to the north, from the Arabah, to the south.
entries.definition_ko: '매끈한' 또는 '민둥한 산'이라는 뜻으로, 여호수아의 정복 남쪽 경계를 표시하는 산의 이름이다(수 11:17, 12:7).

entries.definition: HALE means to haul, to drag by force, before magistrates. Luke 12:58; Acts 8:3.
entries.definition_ko: 관원 앞으로 억지로 끌고 가는 것을 뜻한다(눅 12:58, 행 8:3).

entries.definition: HAL'HUL (trembling), a town in the mountains of Judah, Josh 15:58. Its ruins, having the same name, Halhul, are found on the eastern slope of a hill 4 miles north of Hebron, where is also an old mosque dedicated to Neby Yunas, the prophet Jonah.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 산지의 성읍이다(수 15:58). 같은 이름 할훌의 폐허가 헤브론 북쪽 4마일 언덕 동쪽 비탈에 있으며, 선지자 요나에게 바쳐진 옛 회당도 있다.

entries.definition: HA'LI (necklace), a town in Asher, Josh 19:25; now 'Alia.
entries.definition_ko: 아셀의 성읍이다(수 19:25).

entries.definition: HALL, in Luke 22:55, was the court of the high priest's palace.
entries.definition_ko: 눅 22:55의 이 말은 대제사장 관저의 뜰이었다.

entries.definition: HALLELU'JAH. See Alleluia.
entries.definition_ko: 할렐루야 참조.

entries.definition: HALLO'HESH (the enchanter),one who sealed the covenant, Neh 10:24.
entries.definition_ko: 언약에 인친 사람(느 10:24).

entries.definition: HAL'LOW means to make holy, to consecrate.
entries.definition_ko: 거룩하게 하다, 구별하다라는 뜻이다.

entries.definition: HALO'HESH (the enchanter), one who helped repair the wall, Neh 3:12.
entries.definition_ko: 성벽 수축을 도운 사람(느 3:12).

entries.definition: HAM (hot, or multitude), the son of Noah. He is known for his irreverence to his father. Gen 9:22, and as the parent of Gush, Mizraim, Phut, and Canaan, Gen 10:6, who became the founders of large nations. Cush seems to have been the father of the peoples dwelling in Babylonia, southern Arabia, and Ethiopia; Nimrod was his son. Gen 10:8. Mizraim, the Hebrew word for Egypt, was the ancestor of the Egyptians. Phut was also the ancestor of an African people, as appears from the association of his name with the descendants of Cush and the Lydians, Jer 46:9; see margin. Canaan was the ancestor of the Phoenicians and other tribes inhabiting Palestine. Egypt is called "the land of Ham," Ps 78:51; Ps 105:23-27; Ps 106:22.
entries.definition_ko: 노아의 아들이다. 아버지에게 불경한 일로 알려져 있고(창 9:22) 구스, 미스라임, 붓, 가나안의 아버지로(창 10:6) 이들이 큰 민족의 조상이 되었다. 구스는 바벨로니아와 남부 아라비아, 에티오피아에 살던 민족들의 조상인 듯하며 니므롯이 그 아들이다(창 10:8). 히브리어로 애굽을 뜻하는 미스라임은 애굽인의 조상이다. 붓도 아프리카 민족의 조상이었고, 가나안은 베니게인과 팔레스타인에 살던 여러 부족의 조상이다. 애굽을 '함의 땅'이라 부른다(시 78:51, 105:23-27, 106:22).

entries.definition: HA'MAN (celebrated), prime minister of Ahasuerus, the Persian monarch. Esth 3:1. His pride being hurt because Mordecai, the Jew, refused to bow and do him reverence, Esth 3:2, he secured a royal decree for the extermination of all Jews in the Persian dominions. He was, however, thwarted through the influence of Esther, and executed on the very gallows he had prepared for Mordecai. Esth 7:10. The Jews, on the mention of his name on the day of Purim, hiss. Like Sejanus in Roman history, his name will always suggest the contrast of power and disgrace.
entries.definition_ko: 페르시아 왕 아하수에로의 총리다(에 3:1). 유대인 모르드개가 절하며 경의를 표하지 않아 자존심이 상하자(에 3:2), 페르시아 전역의 모든 유대인을 진멸하라는 조서를 얻어 냈다. 그러나 에스더의 영향으로 저지되었고, 모르드개를 위해 준비한 바로 그 나무에 매달려 죽었다(에 7:10). 유대인은 부림절에 그 이름이 나올 때 야유한다. 로마 역사의 세야누스처럼 그 이름은 언제나 권세와 몰락의 대비를 떠올리게 한다.

entries.definition: HA'MATH (fortress, citadel), one of the most important cities of Syria, and one of the oldest in the world. It was founded by a son of Canaan, Gen 10:18; Num 34:8, and was situated in the valley of the Orontes, between its source and the site of the city of Antioch. It thus commanded the route to the Euphrates from Phoenicia, and may be called the "key" of northern Palestine. It was 165 miles in a straight line north of Jerusalem, and was the capital of a kingdom or province of which little is known. It was visited by the spies, Num 13:21, and it is frequently noticed as the northern boundary of Palestine. Num 34:8; Josh 13:5. Its king, Toi, blessed David for his victory over Zobah, 2 Sam 8:9-12; Solomon extended his kingdom to Hamath, 1 Kgs 8:6; 2 Chr 8:4, and built store-cities in that region; afterward the city and country became independent, but were again subdued by Jeroboam II., 2 Kgs 14:25, 2 Kgs 14:28. It was taken by the Assyrians, 2 Kgs 18:34; Isa 10:9; Amos calls it "Hamath the great," and speaks of its desolation. Am 6:2. Later History-The name of Hamath was changed by Antiochus Epiphanes to Epiphania, though the old name does not appear to have been lost, since it was known as Hamath in the time of Jerome. The place was taken by the Moslems, a.d. 639; by the Franks, a.d. 1108; by the Turks, a.d. 1115; was destroyed by an earthquake in which 15,000 persons perished, a.d. 1157; and taken by Saladin, a.d. 1178. Its modern name is Hamah, and it is now a place of 30,000 inhabitants. Porter regards it as a town where life has been at a standstill for 30 centuries. It, how Inscription discovered at Hamath. (From a report of the Am, Palestine Exploration Society.) ever, has large bazaars, baths, mosques, and hydraulic works, and carries on an active trade with Aleppo and other towns of Asia and Africa. The Persian water-wheels, which creak and groan as they raise the water for the supply of the city, are great curiosities. The Hamath inscriptions, which have in late years excited the attention of scholars, were first seen by Burckhardt, but attracted little notice until 1870. The stones are four in number, and are inscribed in hieroglyphics of a very ancient character; they have not yet been satisfactorilv deciphered.
entries.definition_ko: 수리아의 가장 중요한 성읍 중 하나이자 세상에서 가장 오래된 성읍 중 하나다. 가나안의 아들이 세웠고(창 10:18) 오론테스 골짜기, 그 수원과 안디옥 사이에 있었다. 베니게에서 유브라데로 가는 길목을 지켜 북부 팔레스타인의 '열쇠'라 할 수 있다. 예루살렘 북쪽 직선거리 165마일에 있으며 알려진 바 적은 한 왕국 또는 속주의 수도였다. 정탐꾼들이 들렀고(민 13:21) 흔히 팔레스타인 북쪽 경계로 언급된다(민 34:8, 수 13:5). 그 왕 도이가 소바를 이긴 다윗을 축복했고(삼하 8:9-12), 솔로몬이 나라를 하맛까지 넓혔다(왕상 8:65, 대하 8:4). 후에 독립했다가 여로보암 2세에게 다시 정복되었고(왕하 14:25,28) 앗수르에게 함락되었다(왕하 18:34, 사 10:9).

entries.definition: HAMATH-ZOBAH (fortress of Zohah), a city which Solomon conquered, 2 Chr 8:3, which cannot have been Hamath, "the great," but must have been another Hamath, not yet identified.
entries.definition_ko: 솔로몬이 정복한 성읍으로(대하 8:3) '큰' 하맛일 수는 없고 아직 확인되지 않은 다른 하맛이었을 것이다.

entries.definition: HAM'MATH (warm springs), a fortified city in Naphtali, Josh 19:35, and probably identical with Hummam, or "Warm Springs," about 1 mile south of Tiberias. It is still noted for its hot, sulphurous waters, which are too nauseous to drink, but are used for bathing and are regarded as possessing great medicinal qualities. The walls of an old town can be traced near the baths. Hammath is probably Ihe same as Hammon, No. 2, and as Hammothdor.
entries.definition_ko: '더운 샘'이라는 뜻으로 납달리의 견고한 성읍이다(수 19:35). 디베랴 남쪽 약 1마일의 후맘, 곧 '더운 샘'과 같은 곳으로 추정된다. 지금도 뜨거운 유황수로 유명한데 마시기에는 역겨우나 목욕에 쓰이며 약효가 뛰어난 것으로 여겨진다. 함못과 함몬(2), 함못도르가 같은 곳일 것이다.

entries.definition: HAMMED'ATHA (double ?), Haman's father, Esth 3:1.
entries.definition_ko: 하만의 아버지(에 3:1).

entries.definition: HAM'MELECH (the king), the father of Jerahmeel and Malchiah. Jer 36:26; Eze 38:6.
entries.definition_ko: 여라므엘과 말기야의 아버지(렘 36:26, 38:6).

entries.definition: HAM'MER, the English translation of four different Hebrew words. The hammers mentioned by Isaiah, Is 44:12 "seem to have been the heaviest instruments of the kind for hard blows." Jael's hammer, Jud 4:21, was properly a mallet, such as the Bedouin use at the present day to drive the wooden tent-pins into the ground. The "battle-axe," Jer 51:20, and the "maul," Prov 25:18, were species of hammers used for warlike purposes. The tool probably resembled that of the present day. The word "hammer" is also used symbolically for mighty force. Jer 23:29; Jer 50:23.
entries.definition_ko: 네 가지 다른 히브리어를 옮긴 말이다. 이사야가 말한 망치(사 44:12)는 '센 타격을 위한 가장 무거운 연장'이었던 듯하다. 야엘의 망치(삿 4:21)는 정확히는 나무 장막 말뚝을 땅에 박는 데 오늘날 베두인이 쓰는 것과 같은 나무망치였다. '싸움 도끼'(렘 51:20)와 '방망이'(잠 25:18)는 전쟁에 쓰인 망치의 일종이다. 이 말은 큰 힘을 나타내는 상징으로도 쓰인다(렘 23:29, 50:23).

entries.definition: HAMMOL'EKETH (the queen), the sister of Gilead, 1 Chr 7:17-18.
entries.definition_ko: '여왕'이라는 뜻으로 길르앗의 누이다(대상 7:17-18).

entries.definition: HAM'MON (warm springs). A place in Asher, near Zidon, Josh 19:28. It is identified with 'Ain Hamul, 10 miles below Tyre. A Levitical city in Naphtali, 1 Chr 6:76; probably the same as Hammath and Hammoth-dor; now el ?Hummdm?.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 시돈 근처 아셀의 한 곳(수 19:28). 2) 납달리의 레위인 성읍(대상 6:76)으로 함맛, 함못도르와 같은 곳일 것이다.

entries.definition: 'HAM'MOTH-DOR(warm springs, dwelling), a Levitical city and a city of refuge in Naphtali, Josh 21:32. See Hammath and Hammon, No. 2.
entries.definition_ko: 납달리에 있는 레위인 성읍이자 도피성이다(수 21:32). 함맛, 함몬(2) 참조.

entries.definition: HA'MON-GOG (multitude of Gog), a name given to a ravine or valley in which multitudes of the slain of Gog were to be buried, Eze 39:11, Eze 39:15. The Targums regard it as near the Sea of Galilee, and probably on the great road from Syria and the East to Egypt.
entries.definition_ko: '곡의 무리'라는 뜻으로 곡의 죽은 무리를 묻을 골짜기에 붙인 이름이다(겔 39:11,15). 탈굼은 갈릴리 바다 근처, 아마도 수리아와 동방에서 애굽으로 가는 큰길에 있었다고 본다.

entries.definition: HAM'ONAH, or HAMO'NAH (multitude), a city apparently near where the multitudes of Gog should be buried, Eze 39:16.
entries.definition_ko: 곡의 무리를 묻을 곳 근처로 보이는 성읍이다(겔 39:16).

entries.definition: HA'MOR (ass), the father of Shechem, who ravished Dinah, Gen 33:19. He was killed by Jacob's sons, Gen 34:26. He is called Emmor in Acts 7:16.
entries.definition_ko: 디나를 욕보인 세겜의 아버지다(창 33:19). 야곱의 아들들에게 죽임을 당했다(창 34:26). 행 7:16에서는 에모르라 불린다.

entries.definition: HAMU'EL (wrath of God), a Simeonite, 1 Chr 4:26.
entries.definition_ko: 시므온 사람(대상 4:26).

entries.definition: HA'MUL (pitied), the younger son of Pharez, and ancestor of the Hamulites. Gen 46:12; 1 Chr 2:5; Num 26:21.
entries.definition_ko: 베레스의 작은아들이자 하물 족속의 조상(창 46:12, 대상 2:5, 민 26:21).

entries.definition: HAMU'TAL (akin to the dew), daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, a wife to King Josiah, and mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah. 2 Kgs 23:31; 2 Kgs 24:18; Jer 52:1.
entries.definition_ko: 립나 사람 예레미야의 딸로, 요시야 왕의 아내이자 여호아하스와 시드기야의 어머니다(왕하 23:31, 24:18, 렘 52:1).

entries.definition: HANAM'EEL (whom God has given), son of Shallum, and Jeremiah's cousin, Jer 32:6-12.
entries.definition_ko: 살룸의 아들이자 예레미야의 사촌(렘 32:6-12).

entries.definition: HA'NAN (merciful). A prominent Benjamite, 1 Chr 8:23. A descendant of Saul. 1 Chr 8:38; 1 Chr 9:44. One of David's guard, 1 Chr 11:43. One of the ancestors of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel. Ezr 2:46; Neh 7:49. A Levite who assisted Ezra in explaining the Law, Neh 8:7, and sealed the covenant, Jud 10:10. A chief who sealed the covenant, Neh 10:22. Another sealer, Neh 10:26. The tithe-keeper appointed by Nehemiah to represent the laity, Neh 13:13. The four storekeepers represented the four classes of the people — priests, scribes, Levites, and the laity. One whose sons had a chamber in the temple, Jer 35:4.
entries.definition_ko: 베냐민의 유력자(대상 8:23), 사울의 후손(대상 8:38), 다윗의 호위병 중 하나(대상 11:43), 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 느디님 사람의 조상(스 2:46), 에스라를 도와 율법을 해석한 레위인(느 8:7), 언약에 인친 지도자들(느 10:22,26), 느헤미야가 평신도를 대표하도록 세운 십일조 관리인(느 13:13) 등을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: HANAN'EEL (graciously given of God), a tower which formed a part of the wall of Jerusalem. Neh 3:1; Neh 12:39; Jer 31:38; Zech 14:10. It appears to have been between the fishgate and the sheep-gate, but can scarcely be identified with the tower of Meah, as some have proposed. Dr. Barclay suggested that in the projection at the northeast corner of the harem enclosure are to be found the remains of the tower of Hananeel.
entries.definition_ko: 예루살렘 성벽의 일부를 이루던 망대다(느 3:1, 12:39, 렘 31:38, 슥 14:10). 어문과 양문 사이에 있었던 것으로 보인다.

entries.definition: HANA'NI (gracious). A son of Heman, appointed by David to share with his eleven kinsmen the charge of the eighteenth division of the Levitical musicians, 1 Chr 25:4, 1 Chr 25:25, A seer who rebuked King Asa for neglect to trust in God. He was imprisoned for his boldness, 2 Chr 16:7-10. He was probably the father of Jehu the prophet, 1 Kgs 16:1-2; 2 Chr 19:2. A brother of Nehemiah, who brought him the melancholy report of the condition of Jerusalem which induced Nehemiah to make his journey thither, Neh 1:2. Hanani was afterward appointed by Nehemiah to have charge of the city gates, b.c. 446, Neh 7:2. A priest who had a foreign wife, Ezr 10:20.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 헤만의 아들로, 다윗이 열한 형제와 함께 레위인 악사 열여덟째 반차를 맡게 했다(대상 25:4,25). 2) 아사 왕이 하나님을 의지하지 않은 것을 책망한 선견자로, 그 담대함 때문에 갇혔다(대하 16:7-10). 아마도 선지자 예후의 아버지일 것이다(왕상 16:1). 3) 느헤미야의 형제로 예루살렘의 참담한 형편을 알려 느헤미야가 그리로 가게 했고(느 1:2), 후에 성문을 맡게 되었다(느 7:2). 4) 이방 여인을 아내로 둔 제사장(스 10:20).

entries.definition: HANANI'AH (whom God hath given). A false prophet and contemporary with Jeremiah. He prophesied that the vessels of the Lord's house would be brought back from Babylon two years after the date of the prophecy, Jer 28:3. In token of deliverance from the bondage of Babylon, he broke the wooden yoke which Jeremiah wore in accordance with the divine command. Jeremiah was deceived by his pretensions, but subsequently called him a deceiver to his face, and prophesied his early death. He died that year, Jer 28:17. Hananiah's case is an instance of the false prophets with whom the true prophets came into conflict. A Benjamite chief, 1 Chr 8:24. One of the sons of Heman, 1 Chr 25:4, 1 Chr 25:23. One of Uzziah's captains, 2 Chr 26:11. One who had a foreign wife, Ezr 10:28. 6, 7. Two repairers of the wall of Jerusalem, Neh 3:8, Neh 3:30. 8, The "ruler of the palace," whom Nehemiah appointed to share with his brother the charge of the gates of Jerusalem, Neh 7:2. 9, One who signed the covenant, Neh 10:23. 10, 11, Two priests, Neh 12:12, Ex 12:41. 12, A son of Zerubabbel, 1 Chr 3:19, 1 Chr 3:21. 13, The father of one of Jehoiakim's princes, Jer 36:12. 14, Grandfather of the captain who arrested Jeremiah, Jer 37:13. 15, Original Hebrew name of Shadrach, Dan 1:6-7.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 예레미야와 동시대의 거짓 선지자다. 예언한 날로부터 2년 후 여호와의 성전 기구가 바벨론에서 돌아오리라 예언했고(렘 28:3), 바벨론의 속박에서 벗어남의 표로 예레미야가 하나님의 명대로 메고 있던 나무 멍에를 꺾었다. 예레미야가 처음에는 속았으나 후에 그를 면전에서 속이는 자라 부르고 그해에 죽으리라 예언했으며 실제로 그해에 죽었다(렘 28:17). 참 선지자들이 맞선 거짓 선지자들의 한 예다. 그 외에도 베냐민 지도자(대상 8:24), 헤만의 아들(대상 25:4,23), 웃시야의 지휘관(대하 26:11), 성벽 수축자들(느 3:8,30), 느헤미야가 예루살렘 성문을 맡긴 '영문의 관원'(느 7:2) 등이 있다.

entries.definition: HAND is a symbol of human action; "pure hands" are pure actions; "unjust hands" are deeds of injustice; "hands full of blood," actions stained with cruelty; and the like. Ps 24:4; Eze 23:37. It is likewise a term for the vengeance of God exercised upon any one, 1 Sam 5:6-7. "To pour water on any one's hands" was to serve him. So Elisha is said to have done for Elijah, 2 Kgs 3:11. "To wash one's hands" in public was a way of expressing innocency, Deut 21:6-7; Matt 27:24; "to kiss one's hand" is an act of adoration, Job 31:27; "to lift up one's hands" is to take an oath. Gen 14:22. Also it is a posture in blessing, Lev 9:22; also, to rebel, 2 Sam 20:21. "To stretch out the hand" is sometimes a gesture that denotes mercy, Isa 65:2; "to put it forth unto anything" is to steal, Ex 22:8, Ex 22:11. "To smite the hands together over the head" was a gesture of despairing grief. 2 Sam 13:19; Jer 2:37. Hand in general is the symbol of power and strength — the right hand particularly so. "To be on one's right hand" is to be in one's favor. The Hebrews, in reckoning the four quarters, faced the east; consequently to "the right hand" signified to the south, the southern quarter; "to the left hand" signified to the north, the northern quarter. Job 23:9; 1 Sam 23:19, see margin; 2 Sam 24:5. These are a few out of the many uses of the word hand. One more use will be given: "To lay the hands upon any one," or the imposition of hands, was at an early period "a part of the ceremonial observed on the appointment and consecration of persons to high and holy undertakings." In Num 27:18 we read that Moses was commanded to lay his hand upon Joshua. This act did not confer any new grace upon Joshua, but merely gave formal and public confirmation of Jehovah's choice, and confirmed and strengthened the spiritual gifts already bestowed. Comp. Deut 34:9. The phrase is not used in the N.T. in exactly the same sense. Acts 8:15-17; 1 Tim 4:14; 2 Tim 1:6. The apostles confirmed the grace the convert had received, as in the case of Cornelius, Acts 10:44-48, and in other cases conferred spiritual gifts and qualifications.
entries.definition_ko: 손은 인간 행위의 상징이다. '깨끗한 손'은 깨끗한 행위요, '불의한 손'은 불의한 행실이며, '피 묻은 손'은 잔혹함에 물든 행위다(시 24:4, 겔 23:37). 또한 누군가에게 행하시는 하나님의 보응을 가리키기도 한다(삼상 5:6-7). '누구의 손에 물을 붓다'는 그를 섬긴다는 뜻으로, 엘리사가 엘리야에게 그리했다 한다(왕하 3:11). 공중 앞에서 '손을 씻는' 것은 무죄를 나타내는 방식이었고(신 21:6-7, 마 27:24), '손에 입 맞추는' 것은 경배의 행위이며(욥 31:27), '손을 드는' 것은 맹세하는 것이다(창 14:22). 축복할 때의 자세이기도 하고(레 9:22) 반역을 뜻하기도 한다(삼하 20:21). 손은 대체로 권세와 힘의 상징이며 특히 오른손이 그러하다.

entries.definition: HAND-BREADTH, the palm; used as a measure of four fingers, equal to about 4 inches. Ex 25:25; 1 Kgs 7:26. In Ps 39:5 the expression "Thou hast made my days as an hand-breadth" means "very short."
entries.definition_ko: 손바닥 너비로, 손가락 넷에 해당하며 약 4인치다(출 25:25, 왕상 7:26). 시 39:5의 '주께서 나의 날을 한 뼘 길이만큼 되게 하셨사오매'는 '매우 짧다'는 뜻이다.

entries.definition: HANDICRAFT. The following is in the main a condensation of the article in Ayre's Treasury of Bible Knowledge: The primitive condition of man being that of agriculturists, his wants were few and easily supplied. Yet even he would want some tools, and as the race became older and extended itself its necessities would stimulate it to greater inventiveness. Hence we find that the Cainites, who were more progressive than the Sethites, early possessed iron articles, Gen 4:22. See Tubal-cain. From this incidental biblical notice we are able to form an idea of that early mode of life. Our notices are, however, extremely scanty. Still, by putting them together, we get this enumeration of tradesmen among the Hebrews and the other peoples mentioned in the Bible. Apothecaries, or, rather, perfumers. Ex 30:25, Ex 25:35; 2 Chr 16:14; Neh 3:8; Eccl 10:1. Bakers. See Bake, Bread, Oven. Barbers. Eze 5:1; Num 6:5, Gen 6:19. Carpenters. The building of Noah's ark implies considerable knowledge of this trade. The various structures ordered by the Lord for his service, such as the tabernacle and its contents, Ex 25:10, etc., and the houses of the people, prove that this useful trade was early practised and afterward maintained among the Hebrews. But when particularly fine work had to be done, foreign artists were employed. 2 Sam 5:11; 1 Kgs 5:6. Yet it is doubtless true that many of the Hebrew carpenters were good and skilful workmen. Isa 44:13-17; Ezr 3:7. Among the carpenters' tools are mentioned in the Bible the rule, the measuring-line, the plane, the compass, the hammer, nails, the saw, the axe, Isa 10:15, the awl, Ex 21:6. Our Lord's reputed father, Joseph, and our Lord himself were carpenters. See Carpenter. Carvers in wood and stone. Bezaleel and Aholiah, who were proficient therein, are individually mentioned in Exodus as leading in the building of the tabernacle in the wilderness, Ex 31:5. So a man sent by Huram is credited with the superintendence of the carved work of the temple, 2 Chr 2:13, etc. Dyers were also known. This fact is easily inferred from the prevalent use of colored fabrics on the part of the early Hebrews. Engravers, both upon stone and metal, Ex 28:9-11. See Engrave. Fullers were probably numerous, in consequence of the prevalence of white in dress. See Fuller. Masons. Cities antedate the Flood, Gen 4:17. The Israelites built cities for their Egyptian master (Rameses), Ex 1:11. It is reasonable to conjecture that the Phoenician masons mentioned as building Solomon's temple were the master-masons, but that Hebrew workmen were also employed, 1 Kgs 5:17-18. The skill of these masons is shown in so exactly fitting the stones of the. temple that the building rose without the sound of a hammer, 1 Kgs 6:7. Plastering was customary within and without, mortar being used. Lev 14:40-42; Matt 23:27. The untempered mortar was perhaps mere mud, Eze 13:10-15. Mining must have been early practised, Job 28:1-6. See Metals. Potters are frequently spoken of; e.g. Jer 18:2-6. See Potter. Ship-builders. This trade was perhaps only carried on for a short period. The Tyrians were the prominent ship-builders, and were the teachers of other nations. 1 Kgs 10:22; 1 Kgs 22:48-49. See Commerce. Smiths or workers in metal were of various kinds, from the diggers or smelters of ore to the skilled artificers in gold and silver. They existed before the Flood, Gen 4:22. Much work of this sort was done in the wilderness. Ex 25:11-13; Gen 26:6,Ex 26:21. Bronze was the metal most employed — iron much less so. The jewelry worn so commonly, the vessels of the tabernacle, the gold and silver utensils, the ornamentation so profusely used, — all show that the smiths of the various sorts were much employed by the Hebrews. Tanners and dressers of leather were found in all parts of the land. It was at a tanner's house that Peter lodged when in Joppa, Acts 9:43. Tent-makers. This trade seems to have been a lucrative one. Paul followed it, and supported himself by it, Acts 18:3. Weavers, particularly women, are mentioned frequently. 2 Kgs 23:7; 1 Chr 4:21; Prov 31:13, Num 31:19. A trade was indispensable to a Jewish citizen after the Captivity, but all trades were not held in equal honor. It is probable that as in the East at the present day, so formerly, each trade had its own special locality. Be it ever remembered to the honor of the Jews that they, almost alone among ancient nations, regarded a trade as a fit occupation of a freeman, that therefore their highest citizens could earn their bread if necessary, and that slaves were not depended upon, as in Greece, for the doing of all manual work. Trades among the Jews were also not necessarily hereditary. It was a saying of the Rabbins: "He who does not teach his son a trade makes out of him a footpad."
entries.definition_ko: 사람의 처음 형편이 농경이었으므로 필요한 것이 적고 쉽게 채워졌다. 그러나 그때도 연장은 필요했고, 인류가 오래되고 퍼져 가면서 그 필요가 더 큰 발명을 자극했다. 그래서 셋 자손보다 진취적이던 가인 자손이 일찍이 철 기구를 지녔음을 본다(창 4:22). 성경의 이 스치는 언급으로 그 초기 생활 방식을 짐작할 수 있다. 기록이 매우 적으나 모아 보면 히브리인과 성경에 언급된 다른 민족들의 장인 목록을 얻는다 — 향품 만드는 자(출 30:25, 대하 16:14, 느 3:8), 떡 굽는 자, 이발사(겔 5:1, 민 6:5), 목수(노아의 방주 건조가 상당한 지식을 전제한다) 등이다.

entries.definition: HANDKERCHIEF, NAPKIN, A'PRON, These articles were pretty much alike, differing mainly in use. See Clothes.
entries.definition_ko: 이 물건들은 거의 같고 쓰임새만 주로 달랐다. 의복 참조.

entries.definition: HANDS, LAYING ON OF. See Hand.
entries.definition_ko: 손 참조.

entries.definition: HAND'STAVES, darts or javelins. Eze 39:9.
entries.definition_ko: 손 창 또는 단창을 뜻한다(겔 39:9).

entries.definition: HA'NES, a city of Egypt, Isa 30:4, and generally identified with Heracleopolis, "Hercules' city," in middle Egypt, on the west of the Nile; but the Chaldee paraphrast reads Tahpanhes, thus identifying it with that city.
entries.definition_ko: 애굽의 한 성읍으로(사 30:4), 대개 나일 서편 중부 애굽의 헤라클레오폴리스, 곧 '헤라클레스의 도시'로 비정된다. 다만 갈대아 역본은 다바네스로 읽어 그 성읍과 동일시한다.

entries.definition: HANGING, HANGINGS. The words are not the singular and plural of the same word in the Hebrew, but are translations of quite different words. The "hanging" — literally, "a cover" — is the word for the curtain before the door of the tabernacle, Ex 26:36-37; Ex 39:38, and for the curtain before the entrance of the court. Ex 27:16; Ex 38:18; Num 4:26. The same Hebrew word is several times translated correctly in the expression, "veil of the covering." Ex 35:12; Ex 39:34; Ex 40:21; Num 4:5. The "hangings"—literally, "that which is in motion" — were the coverings upon the walls of the court of the tabernacle. Ex 27:9; Ps 35:17; Ex 38:9; Num 3:26; Song 4:6, Num 4:26. The word "hangings" is used in 2 Kgs 23:7, but the Hebrew word may more properly be translated "tents," such as were used in the impure rites of Ashtoreth.
entries.definition_ko: 이 두 말은 같은 히브리어의 단수·복수가 아니라 전혀 다른 말을 옮긴 것이다. '휘장'은 문자적으로 '덮개'로, 성막 문의 휘장(출 26:36-37, 39:38)과 뜰 입구의 휘장(출 27:16, 38:18, 민 4:26)을 가리키는 말이다. 같은 히브리어가 여러 번 '가리는 휘장'으로 바르게 번역된다(출 35:12, 40:21, 민 4:5). '포장'은 문자적으로 '움직이는 것'으로 성막 뜰의 벽에 두른 휘장이다(출 27:9, 38:9, 민 3:26). 왕하 23:7의 '휘장'에 해당하는 히브리어는 아스다롯의 부정한 의식에 쓰인 '장막'으로 옮기는 편이 더 적절하다.

entries.definition: HANG'ING. According to Jewish law, the criminal was first strangled and then hanged. Num 25:4; Deut 21:22. The body was to be taken down before sunset. It was a special mark of infamy and a curse, Deut 21:23. Jesus is said to have been "hanged on a tree;" literally, "on a beam of wood." Acts 5:30; Gal 3:13. But the expression refers to his crucifixion.
entries.definition_ko: 유대 율법에 따르면 죄인을 먼저 목 졸라 죽인 후 매달았다(민 25:4, 신 21:22). 시체는 해 지기 전에 내려야 했다. 특별한 수치와 저주의 표였다(신 21:23). 예수께서 '나무에 달려' 죽으셨다 하는데(행 5:30, 갈 3:13) 문자적으로는 '나무 기둥에'이며 십자가에 못 박히심을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: HAN'IEL (grace of God), a son of Ulla, and a prince of Asher, 1 Chr 7:39.
entries.definition_ko: 울라의 아들이자 아셀의 지도자(대상 7:39).

entries.definition: HAN'NAH (grace), one of the wives of Elkanah, and the mother of Samuel, whom she received in answer to prayer. Her song of praise on this occasion, 1 Sam 2:1-10, is a magnificent hymn to the holiness and justice of Jehovah, and has been compared with the song of Mary. Luke 1:46-55.
entries.definition_ko: 엘가나의 아내 중 하나이자 사무엘의 어머니로, 기도의 응답으로 그를 얻었다. 그때 부른 찬송(삼상 2:1-10)은 여호와의 거룩하심과 공의를 노래한 장엄한 찬가로 마리아의 노래(눅 1:46-55)와 비교되어 왔다.

entries.definition: HAN'NATHON (graciously regarded), a place on the north-eastern border of Zebulon, Josh 19:14. Conder proposes to identify it with Kefe Anan, the Caphar Hananiah of the Talmud.
entries.definition_ko: 스불론 북동쪽 경계의 한 곳(수 19:14).

entries.definition: HA'NOCH (initiated). A son of Midian, Gen 25:4; called Henoch. 1 Chr 1:33. Eldest son of Reuben; founder of the family of the Hanochites. Gen 46:9; Ex 6:14; Num 26:5.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 미디안의 아들(창 25:4). 대상 1:33에서는 하녹이라 불린다. 2) 르우벤의 맏아들이자 하녹 족속의 조상(창 46:9, 출 6:14, 민 26:5).

entries.definition: HANOCHITES, THE, the descendants of Hanoch, Num 26:5.
entries.definition_ko: 하녹의 후손을 가리킨다(민 26:5).

entries.definition: HA'NUN (gracious). A king of Ammon who is known for the indignities he showed to the messengers sent to him by David to comfort him at the death of his father, 2 Sam 10:1-6. A man of Jerusalem. Neh 3:13. Another repairer of the wall. Neh 3:30.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 암몬 왕으로, 아버지의 죽음을 위로하려 다윗이 보낸 사신들을 모욕한 일로 알려져 있다(삼하 10:1-6). 2) 예루살렘 사람(느 3:13). 3) 또 다른 성벽 수축자(느 3:30).

entries.definition: HAPHRA'IM (two pits), a city of Issachar, apparently near Shunem. Josh 19:19. Eusebius and Jerome place it 6 miles north of Legio. About 6 miles northeast of Lejun and 2 miles west of Solam (Shunem) is the modern village of el-Afuleh, which may represent Haphraim.
entries.definition_ko: 잇사갈의 성읍으로 수넴 근처로 보인다(수 19:19).

entries.definition: HAR' SHA (deaf), ancestor of some who returned with Zerubbabel. Ezr 2:52; Neh 7:54.
entries.definition_ko: 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 이들의 조상(스 2:52, 느 7:54).

entries.definition: HA'RA (mountain-land), a place, evidently in western Assyria, to which the Israelites east of the Jordan were carried captive, 1 Chr 5:26. It is generally regarded as a variation of Haran. From the connection in which it is named, it must have been on or near the Khabour River.
entries.definition_ko: 요단 동편 이스라엘 사람들이 사로잡혀 간 곳으로 서부 앗수르에 있었던 것이 분명하다(대상 5:26). 대개 하란의 변형으로 여겨지며, 함께 언급된 지명들로 보아 하부르 강가나 그 근처였을 것이다.

entries.definition: HAR'ADAH (fear), a desert-station of the Israelites, Num 33:24-25, and may be identical with Jehel-Aradah, in Wadi el-'Ain, a day's march from 'Ain Huderah.
entries.definition_ko: 광야에서 이스라엘이 진 친 곳(민 33:24-25).

entries.definition:
HA'RAN (a mountaineer). The brother of Abraham, and the father of Lot, Gen 11:26. A Levite, 1 Chr 23:9.

HA'RAN (parched), a son of Caleb by his concubine Ephah, 1 Chr 2:46.

HA'RAN (parched, dry), called also CHAR'RAN, Acts 7:2, Acts 7:4, the place to which Terah removed from Ur of the Chaldees, taking with him his two sons, Abram and Nahor, and his grandson, Lot. Terah died there, Gen 11:31-32; Abram and Lot moved to Canaan, Gen 12:4, while Nahor remained at Haran, which was called the city of Nahor, Gen 24:10. It was the early home of Rebekah, and Jacob afterward resided there with Laban, Gen 27:43. The city was in Mesopotamia, and more definitely in Padan-aram, Gen 24:10; Gen 25:20, and also in western Assyria. It is generally identified with the modern Haran, the Roman Carras, situated on the river Belik (the ancient Bilichus), about 50 miles above its entrance into the Euphrates. It is now a small Arab village, containing within its ruined walls the traditional tomb of Terah, the father of Abraham. About 20 miles distant is Orfak, which some claim to be Ur of the Chaldees. There is a Harran on the border of Lake Antcibeh east of Damascus, which Dr. Beke would identify with Haran of Abram, but his view is not accepted by biblical scholars.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 아브라함의 형제이자 롯의 아버지(창 11:26). 2) 레위인(대상 23:9). 3) 갈렙이 첩 에바에게서 얻은 아들(대상 2:46). 4) 하란은 또한 데라가 갈대아 우르에서 두 아들 아브람과 나홀, 손자 롯을 데리고 옮겨 간 곳의 이름이다(행 7:2,4). 데라가 거기서 죽었고(창 11:31-32) 아브람과 롯은 가나안으로 옮겼으며(창 12:4) 나홀은 하란에 남아 그곳이 나홀의 성이라 불렸다(창 24:10). 리브가의 옛 고향이며 야곱이 후에 라반과 함께 지낸 곳이다(창 27:43). 메소보다미아, 더 정확히는 밧단아람에 있었다.

entries.definition: HA'RARITE, THE (the mountaineer), the designation of three persons in connection with David's guard. Agee, 2 Sam 23:11. Shammah, 2 Sam 23:33. Sharar, 2 Sam 23:33; called Sacar, 1 Chr 11:35.
entries.definition_ko: '산지 사람'이라는 뜻으로 다윗의 호위대와 관련된 세 사람에게 붙은 칭호다 — 아게(삼하 23:11), 삼마와 사랄(삼하 23:33).

entries.definition: HARBO'NA (ass-driver), a eunuch of Ahasuerus, Esth 1:10.
entries.definition_ko: 아하수에로의 내시(에 1:10).

entries.definition: HARBO'NAH, the same person as above, Esth 7:9.
entries.definition_ko: 위와 같은 인물이다(에 7:9).

entries.definition: HARDNESS, 1 Kgs 20:11. In this passage and some others the word denotes armor. The phrase "made ready his chariot," Ex 14:6, literally means, in modern phraseology, "tackled," or "put to, his horses." That bridles with bits were very early known as part of the harness of a horse is obvious from Isa 37:29; Prov 26:3; Ps 32:9. The ancient harness was often very elaborate, as the monuments testify.
entries.definition_ko: 왕상 20:11 등에서 이 말은 갑옷을 뜻한다. '병거를 갖추고'(출 14:6)는 오늘날 말로 하면 '말을 메웠다'는 뜻이다. 재갈 물린 굴레가 아주 이른 시기부터 말 장구의 일부로 알려졌음이 사 37:29, 잠 26:3, 시 32:9에서 분명하다. 고대의 마구는 유적이 증언하듯 흔히 매우 정교했다.

entries.definition: HARE, Deut 14:7. Of the hare, which resembles the rabbit, five species or varieties are found in Palestine. This animal was declared unclean by the Jewish law, Lev 11:6, "because he cheweth the cud, but divideth not the hoof." For popular guidance this description was better than a more scientific one, and is explained under Coney.
entries.definition_ko: 토끼와 비슷하며 팔레스타인에 다섯 종 또는 변종이 있다(신 14:7). 유대 율법은 '새김질은 하되 굽이 갈라지지 아니하였으므로' 부정한 짐승으로 선언했다(레 11:6). 대중이 알아보기에는 더 학문적인 설명보다 이 서술이 나았다.

entries.definition: HA'REPH (plucking off), a son of Caleb. 1 Chr 2:51.
entries.definition_ko: 갈렙의 아들(대상 2:51).

entries.definition: HA'RETH (thicket?), a forest of Judah to which David fled from Saul, 1 Sam 22:5. Conder supposes that by a transposition of letters it should read "the city of Hareth" (?), as in Josephus and in two important manuscripts, and finds the site of the place in the small modern village of Kharas, on the north side of Wady Arneba, near Kilch (Keilah).
entries.definition_ko: 다윗이 사울을 피해 도망한 유다의 수풀이다(삼상 22:5).

entries.definition: HARHAI'AH (Jehovah is angry), father of a repairer of the wall, Neh 3:8.
entries.definition_ko: 성벽 수축자의 아버지(느 3:8).

entries.definition: HAR'HAS (very poor), an ancestor of Shallum, 2 Kgs 22:14; called Hasrah in 2 Chr 34:22.
entries.definition_ko: 살룸의 조상(왕하 22:14). 대하 34:22에서는 하스라라 불린다.

entries.definition: HAR'HUR (inflammation), one whose descendants returned with Zerubbabel. Ezr 2:51; Neh 7:53.
entries.definition_ko: 스룹바벨과 함께 그 후손이 돌아온 사람(스 2:51, 느 7:53).

entries.definition: HA'RIM (flat-nosed), a priest who headed the third course of priests. 1 Chr 24:8. His descendants returned with Zerubbabel. Ezr 2:39; Neh 7:42. Some of them had foreign wives, Ezr 10:21. The name was signed to the covenant, Neh 10:27. The name occurs again Neh 12:15. One whose son repaired part of the wall of Jerusalem, Neh 3:11. A non-priestly ancestor of others who returned, and whose strange wives were discarded. His sons signed the covenant. Ezr 2:32; Neh 7:35; Ezr 10:31; Neh 10:27.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 제사장 셋째 반차를 이끈 제사장이다(대상 24:8). 그 후손이 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아왔고(스 2:39, 느 7:42) 그중 일부는 이방 여인을 아내로 두었으며(스 10:21) 그 이름이 언약에 서명되었다(느 10:5). 2) 그 아들이 예루살렘 성벽 일부를 수축한 사람(느 3:11). 3) 제사장이 아닌 다른 사람으로, 돌아온 이들의 조상이며 그 자손이 이방인 아내를 내보냈다(스 2:32, 10:31).

entries.definition: HA'RIPH (plucking off), ancestor of some who returned with Zerubbabel, Neh 7:24.
entries.definition_ko: 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 이들의 조상(느 7:24).

entries.definition: HAR'LOT. The first mention of harlots is in the case of Tamar, Gen 38:15, but we frequently meet with them later in the books of the Bible. The Mosaic Hare of Mt. Sinai. Law forbade fathers to hire out their daughters as harlots, Lev 19:29, and the severe punishment by burning was ordained for the priest's daughter guilty of fornication, Lev 21:9. The harlot was regarded as unclean, and is mentioned in the same breath with the dog, Deut 23:18. The book of Proverbs compares the harlot to a deep ditch and a narrow pit, Prov 23:27, and represents in strong language the perils attending an association with her, Prov 7:10-27. The term is also used of wicked cities; as Nineveh, Nah 3:4, and Jerusalem, Isa 1:21; of Israel, to represent her alienation from God. The marriage relation is looked upon as subsisting between it and God, The nation became a harlot when she practised idolatry. Jer 2:20; Dan 3:1; Eze 16:15; Hos 2:2; Gal 4:15. In the N.T. harlots are classed with publicans. Matt 21:32, and Paul admonishes against the sin of fornication, especially in his Epistle to the Corinthians. 1 Cor 5:1; 2 Cor 12:21. In the book of Revelation, (heathen) Rome, under the mystic name of Babylon, is called "the mother of harlots," Rev 17:5.
entries.definition_ko: 창녀에 대한 첫 언급은 다말의 경우다(창 38:15). 모세 율법은 아버지가 딸을 창녀로 내놓는 것을 금했고(레 19:29), 음행한 제사장의 딸에게는 불사르는 중벌을 정했다(레 21:9). 창녀는 부정하게 여겨져 개와 나란히 언급된다(신 23:18). 잠언은 창녀를 깊은 구덩이와 좁은 함정에 비기며(잠 23:27) 그와 어울리는 위험을 강한 말로 그린다(잠 7:10-27). 이 말은 니느웨(나 3:4)나 예루살렘(사 1:21) 같은 악한 성읍에도 쓰이고, 하나님을 떠난 이스라엘을 나타내는 데도 쓰인다. 하나님과 이스라엘 사이는 혼인 관계로 여겨져, 백성이 우상숭배를 행할 때 창녀가 된 것이다(렘 2:20, 겔 16:15, 호 2:2).

entries.definition: HAR'NEPHER (panting ?), an Asherite chieftain, 1 Chr 7:36.
entries.definition_ko: 아셀 지파의 지도자(대상 7:36).

entries.definition: HA'ROD (trembling), a well or spring by which Gideon and his army encamped before the battle with the Midianites, and apparently where the Lord caused to be applied the test of the warriors by their mode of drinking. Jud 7:1. Saul may have encamped there. 1 Sam 28:4; 1 Sam 29:1. Stanley located it at 'Ain Jalud, a spring 2 miles south-east of Jezreel; Conder at 'Ain Jendin, a copious spring from a rock, 3 miles west of Scythopolis (Beisdn). The name Jendin means "Two companies."
entries.definition_ko: 기드온과 그 군대가 미디안과 싸우기 전 진 쳤던 우물 또는 샘으로, 여기서 주님이 물 마시는 방식으로 군사를 시험하게 하신 듯하다(삿 7:1). 사울도 여기 진 쳤을 수 있다(삼상 29:1). 스탠리는 이스르엘 남동쪽 2마일의 아인 잘루드로, 콘더는 스구도볼리 서쪽 3마일의 아인 젠딘으로 본다.

entries.definition: HAR'OEH (the seer), or REAI'AH, a name, 1 Chr 2:52.
entries.definition_ko: 대상 2:52의 이름으로 르아야라고도 한다.

entries.definition: HA'RORITE, 1 Chr 11:27. See Hakodite.
entries.definition_ko: 대상 11:27. 하롯 사람 참조.

entries.definition: HARO'SHETH (working in wood, etc.) OF THE GENTILES, so called from the mixed people who dwelt there. A place in the north of Palestine, the home of Sisera, Jud 4:2, Jud 4:13, Jud 4:16, and the place of assembling of Jabin's army. Dr. W. M. Thomson locates Harosheth in the pass between the plain of Esdraelon and Acre, at the base of Mount Carmel, where the Kishon flows through the ravine. A village and mound covering ruins, both bearing a name very similar to Harosheth, are found in this vicinity. Conder proposes with greater probability to identity it with El-Harothieh, a miserable mud hamlet about 11 miles west of Nazareth.
entries.definition_ko: '이방의 하로셋'으로, 거기 살던 잡족 때문에 그렇게 불렸다. 팔레스타인 북부의 한 곳으로 시스라의 거처이며(삿 4:2,13,16) 야빈의 군대가 모인 곳이다. 콘더는 나사렛 서쪽 약 11마일의 초라한 흙집 마을 엘하로시에로 보는 것이 더 유력하다고 한다.

entries.definition: HARP, a musical instrument invented by Jubal, and used by the Jews in seasons of thanksgiving to God, mirth, and joy. Gen 4:21; Gen 31:27; Ps 81:2; Isa 24:8. The instrument suggested any other thought than mourning and sorrow. In the hour of captivity the harp is hung upon the willows, Ps 137:2. David was particularly skilful in the use of it, 1 Sam 16:16,1 Sam 16:23. See Psaltery. The harp was played with the fingers, 1 Sam 16:23, but perhaps also with a; key, as Josephus suggests. The same Egyptian Harp. author ascribes ten strings to the harp, which would lead us to infer its identity with the "instrument of ten strings," Ps 92:3. Sometimes it had only eight strings, and was called "the harp on the Sheminith." 1 Chr 15:21; Ps 6:12, title. Harps were of different sizes, for some played on them while walking, 1 Sam 10:5, David played before Saul. 1 Sam 16:23; 1 Sam 18:10. There are different accounts of the shape of the harp. The preceding cut is found represented on Egyptian monuments.
entries.definition_ko: 유발이 만든 악기로, 유대인이 하나님께 감사하고 즐거워하며 기뻐할 때 썼다(창 4:21, 31:27, 시 81:2, 사 24:8). 이 악기는 애곡과 슬픔과는 전혀 다른 것을 떠올리게 한다. 포로 된 때에는 수금을 버드나무에 걸었다(시 137:2). 다윗이 특히 이를 잘 탔다(삼상 16:16,23). 손가락으로 탔으나(삼상 16:23) 요세푸스가 시사하듯 채로도 탔을 것이다. 같은 저자는 줄이 열이라 하는데, 그렇다면 '열 줄 비파'(시 92:3)와 같을 것이다. 때로 여덟 줄뿐인 것도 있어 '스미닛에 맞춘 수금'이라 불렸다(대상 15:21).

entries.definition: HAR'ROW. The verb meaning "to break the clods" is employed in Job 39:10; Isa 28:24; and Hos 10:11, and is believed to indicate the use, occasionally at least, of an instrument analogous to our harrow. This may have been a plank or log of wood, upon which stones were heaped and the laborer sat, and which was drawn over the ground by oxen, to break in pieces the clods and level the surface; or the present custom may have been employed: "In modern Palestine oxen are sometimes turned in to trample the clods, and in some parts of Asia a brush of thorn is dragged over the surface, but all these processes, if used, occur (not after, but) before the seed is committed to the soil." -Smith: Bib. Diet. The word rendered "harrow" in 2 Sam 12:31; 1 Chr 20:3, means a Threshing-instrument, which see.
entries.definition_ko: '흙덩이를 부수다'라는 동사가 욥 39:10, 사 28:24, 호 10:11에 쓰이며, 적어도 때때로 우리의 써레와 비슷한 도구가 쓰였음을 나타내는 것으로 여겨진다. 널빤지나 통나무에 돌을 쌓고 일꾼이 앉아 소가 땅 위로 끌어 흙덩이를 부수고 표면을 고르는 것이었거나, 오늘날처럼 소를 몰아 흙덩이를 밟게 하거나 가시나무 다발을 끌었을 수 있다. 삼하 12:31과 대상 20:3의 '써레'로 옮긴 말은 타작 기구를 뜻한다.

entries.definition: HART, HIND, Ps 42:1. The former is the male stag, one of the most graceful and beautiful of all animals. It was clean by the Levitical law, Deut 12:15; Deut 14:5, and the grace and agility of its motions are alluded to in Song 2:9; Isa 35:6. The stag lolls or pants like the dog, and is soon exhausted by hunger. Jer 14:5; Lam 1:6. It is uncertain whether this word denotes the true fallow-deer, the red deer, or the Barbary deer, or whether it embraces all of them. These three species doubtless formerly lived in Palestine or adjoining districts. The fallow-deer alone is still seen, and that rarely, in the wooded districts of the country. The hind is the female stag. She is smaller and weaker than her mate, the hart, and has no horns. She is sure and swift of foot, and leaps fearlessly among the rocks and precipices. 2 Sam 22:34; Ps 18:33; Hab 3:19. The instinctive affection of the hart and hind is alluded to Prov 5:18-19, and Song 2:7; Song 3:5. The figurative prediction of Jacob respecting Naphtali, Gen 49:21, would be more appropriately rendered, "Naphtali is a deer roaming at large; he shooteth forth noble antlers." The antlers or horns indicate the strength and health of the stag, and the whole metaphor expresses the increase of the tribe and the fertility of their portion in Judaea. See Fallow-deer, Roe.
entries.definition_ko: '수사슴'과 '암사슴'이다(시 42:1). 앞의 것은 수사슴으로 모든 짐승 가운데 가장 우아하고 아름다운 것 중 하나다. 레위기 율법에서 정결했고(신 12:15, 14:5) 그 몸짓의 우아함과 민첩함이 언급된다(아 2:9, 사 35:6). 수사슴은 개처럼 헐떡이며 굶주리면 이내 지친다(렘 14:5, 애 1:6). 암사슴은 수사슴보다 작고 약하며 뿔이 없다. 발이 든든하고 빨라 바위와 벼랑 사이를 겁 없이 뛰어다닌다(삼하 22:34, 시 18:33, 합 3:19).

entries.definition: HA'RUM (lofty), a Judite, 1 Chr 4:8.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 사람(대상 4:8).

entries.definition: HARU'MAPH (slit-nosed), one whose son helped to repair the wall, Neh 3:10.
entries.definition_ko: 그 아들이 성벽 수축을 도운 사람(느 3:10).

entries.definition: HAR'UPHITE, THE, a name of Shephatiah, 1 Chr 12:5.
entries.definition_ko: 스바댜의 별칭(대상 12:5).

entries.definition: HA'RUZ (zealous), the maternal grandfather of King Amon, 2 Kgs 21:19.
entries.definition_ko: 아몬 왕의 외조부(왕하 21:19).

entries.definition: HAR'VEST occurred in the months of March and April, and the term is frequently employed to designate this season of the year. Josh 3:15; Prov 6:8. The harvests of the different grains happened in regular succession, and are known as the "wheat-harvest," 1 Sam 12:17, and the "barley-harvest," Ruth 1:22. The grain was reaped with sickles, Jer 50:16, gathered in handfuls, Ruth 2:16, and done up into sheaves. Ps 129:7. It was then conveyed to the barns or threshing-floors, sometimes in carts. Am 2:13, where it was threshed or winnowed. One mode of threshing was by the treading of oxen, which it was forbidden to muzzle, Deut 25:4. Harvest was a season of great joy and merriment, Isa 9:3. In the book of Ruth we pass through it as in a panoramic vision. In the N.T. our Lord refers to the end of the world under the term of harvest. Matt 13:39, whose reapers will be the angels. The angel is represented figuratively as at that time thrusting in his sickle, "for the harvest of the earth is ripe," Rev 14:15. Feast of. See Pentecost.
entries.definition_ko: 추수는 3~4월에 있었고, 이 말이 흔히 그 계절을 가리키는 데 쓰인다(수 3:15, 잠 6:8). 곡식마다 차례로 추수가 이루어져 '밀 추수'(삼상 12:17), '보리 추수'(룻 1:22)라 불린다. 낫으로 베고(렘 50:16) 한 움큼씩 모아(룻 2:16) 단으로 묶었다(시 129:7). 그 후 곳간이나 타작 마당으로 때로 수레에 실어 옮겼고(암 2:13) 거기서 떨고 까불렀다. 타작 방법 중 하나는 소로 밟는 것인데 그 입에 망을 씌우지 못하게 했다(신 25:4). 추수는 큰 기쁨과 흥겨움의 계절이었다(사 9:3). 신약에서 주님은 세상 끝을 추수로 말씀하시며(마 13:39) 그 추수꾼은 천사들이라 하신다.

entries.definition: HASADI'AH (whom Jehovah loves), a descendant of the royal line of David, 1 Chr 3:20.
entries.definition_ko: 다윗의 왕가 계보의 후손(대상 3:20).

entries.definition: HASENU'AH (the hated), a Benjaniite, 1 Chr 9:7.
entries.definition_ko: 베냐민 사람(대상 9:7).

entries.definition: HASHABI'AH (whom Jehovah regards). 1, 2, Merarite Levites. 1 Chr 6:45; 1 Chr 9:14. 3, The head of the twelfth course of Levitical musicians, 1 Chr 25:3, 1 Chr 25:19. 4, A Hebronite Levite, 1 Chr 26:30, 5. Prince of the tribe of Levi in David's time, 1 Chr 27:17. A chief Levite in Josiah's time, 2 Chr 35:9. A Merarite Levite who accompanied Ezra from Babylon, Ezr 8:19. A priest in the same company, Ezr 8:24, A repairer of the wall, Neh 3:17. A Levite who sealed the covenant, Neh 10:11. A Levite, Neh 11:22, A Levite, Neh 11:15, A priest, Neh 12:24.
entries.definition_ko: 므라리 자손 레위인들(대상 6:45, 9:14), 레위인 악사 열두째 반차의 우두머리(대상 25:3,19), 헤브론 사람 레위인(대상 26:30), 다윗 때 레위 지파의 지도자(대상 27:17), 요시야 때의 레위인 지도자(대하 35:9), 에스라와 함께 바벨론에서 온 레위인(스 8:19), 성벽 수축자(느 3:17), 언약에 인친 레위인(느 10:11) 등 여러 사람을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: HASHAB'NAH (whom Jehovah regards), one who sealed the covenant, Neh 10:25.
entries.definition_ko: 언약에 인친 사람(느 10:25).

entries.definition: HASHABNI'AH (whom Jehovah regards). One whose son repaired the wall, Neh 3:10. A Levite, Neh 9:5.
entries.definition_ko: 그 아들이 성벽을 수축한 사람(느 3:10), 레위인(느 9:5).

entries.definition: HASHBAD'ANA (considerate judge?), one who stood on Ezra's left while he read the Law to the people, Neh 8:4.
entries.definition_ko: 에스라가 백성에게 율법을 읽을 때 그 왼편에 섰던 사람(느 8:4).

entries.definition: HA'SHEM (fat), father of some in David's guard, 1 Chr 11:34, or Jashen, 2 Sam 23:32-33.
entries.definition_ko: 다윗의 호위대에 속한 이들의 아버지(대상 11:34). 삼하 23:32-33에서는 야센이라 한다.

entries.definition: HASHMO'NAH, a station of the Israelites near Mount Hor, Num 33:29, and probably identical with Heshmon, which see.
entries.definition_ko: 호르산 근처 이스라엘의 진 친 곳으로(민 33:29), 헤스몬과 같은 곳으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: HA'SHUB (intelligent). 1, 2, Two of the repairers of the wall, Neh 3:11, Neh 3:23. One who sealed the covenant, Neh 10:23. A Merarite Levite, Neh 11:15; called Hasshub 1 Chr 9:14,
entries.definition_ko: 성벽 수축자 두 사람(느 3:11,23), 언약에 인친 사람(느 10:23), 므라리 자손 레위인(느 11:15) 등을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: HASHU'BAH (intelligent), a descendant of David, 1 Chr 3:20,
entries.definition_ko: 다윗의 후손(대상 3:20).

entries.definition: HA'SHUM (rich). One whose descendants returned with Zerubbabel. Ezr 2:19; Neh 7:22. Several of these descendants had married foreign women, Ezr 10:33. Representatives of them sealed the covenant, Neh 10:18. One who stood on Ezra's left hand while he publicly read the Law, Neh 8:4.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 스룹바벨과 함께 그 후손이 돌아온 사람(스 2:19, 느 7:22). 그 후손 여럿이 이방 여인과 결혼했다(스 10:33). 2) 에스라가 율법을 낭독할 때 그 왼편에 섰던 사람(느 8:4).

entries.definition: HASHU'PHA (stripped), one of the ancestors of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel. Neh 7:46, In Ezr 2:43 more accurately Hasupha.
entries.definition_ko: 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 느디님 사람의 조상 중 하나다(느 7:46). 스 2:43에서는 더 정확히 하수바라 표기된다.

entries.definition: HAS'RAH (very poor). See Habhas,
entries.definition_ko: 하르하스 참조.

entries.definition: HASSENA'AH (thorn-edge), Neh 3:3, one whose sons built the fish-gate. If the name of a town, which is not certain, it must be identical with Senaah. See Senaah.
entries.definition_ko: 그 아들들이 어문을 세운 사람이다(느 3:3). 성읍 이름이라면(확실하지는 않다) 스나아와 같은 곳일 것이다.

entries.definition: HAS'SHUB. See Hashub, No, 4.
entries.definition_ko: 하숩(4) 참조.

entries.definition: HASU'PHA. See Hashupha.
entries.definition_ko: 하수바 참조.

entries.definition: HAT. See Head-dress.
entries.definition_ko: 머리 장식 참조.

entries.definition: HA'TACH, a Persian eunuch, Esth 4:5-6, Ruth 4:9-10.

HATE, Gen 24:60. To hate is to regard with a passion contrary to love, Jer 44:4. God's hatred is toward all sinful thoughts and ways. It is a feeling of which all holy beings are conscious in view of sin, and is wholly unlike the hatred which is mentioned in the Scripture among the works of the flesh, Gal 5:20. We must hate the evil, but love and bless our enemy, Matt 5:43. To hate sometimes means to love in a less degree. When our Saviour says that he who would follow him must hate father and mother, he means that even these dearest earthly friends must be loved in a subordinate degree; and in the same sense the follower of Christ is to hate his own life, or be willing to sacrifice it for the love and service of the Redeemer. A careful examination of the passages and the connection in which these words occur will best show their true force and meaning.
entries.definition_ko: 미워함은 사랑과 반대되는 감정으로 대하는 것이다(창 24:60, 렘 44:4). 하나님의 미워하심은 모든 죄된 생각과 길을 향한다. 거룩한 존재라면 누구나 죄를 볼 때 느끼는 감정이며, 육체의 일로 언급되는 미움과는 전혀 다르다(갈 5:20). 우리는 악을 미워하되 원수를 사랑하고 축복해야 한다(마 5:43-44). '미워하다'는 때로 덜 사랑한다는 뜻이다. 구주께서 자기를 따르려는 자는 부모를 미워해야 한다 하신 것은, 이 지극히 사랑하는 이들조차 그보다 낮은 자리에서 사랑해야 한다는 뜻이다. 같은 뜻에서 그리스도를 따르는 자는 자기 목숨을 미워해야, 곧 구속자를 사랑하고 섬기기 위해 기꺼이 버릴 각오를 해야 한다.

entries.definition: HA'THATH (fearful), a son of Othniel, 1 Chr 4:13.
entries.definition_ko: 옷니엘의 아들(대상 4:13).

entries.definition: HAT'IPHA (captive), one of the ancestors of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel. Ezr 2:54; Neh 7:56.
entries.definition_ko: 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 느디님 사람의 조상 중 하나(스 2:54, 느 7:56).

entries.definition: HAT'ITA (exploring), one of the ancestors of temple-porters who returned. Ezr 2:42; Neh 7:45.
entries.definition_ko: 돌아온 성전 문지기들의 조상 중 하나(스 2:42, 느 7:45).

entries.definition: HATRODITE, THE, the designation of two of David's warriors, 2 Sam 23:25.
entries.definition_ko: 다윗의 용사 두 사람에게 붙은 칭호(삼하 23:25).

entries.definition: HAT'TII, (wavering), one of the ancestors of the Nethinim who returned, Ezr 2:57; Neh 7:59.
entries.definition_ko: 돌아온 느디님 사람의 조상 중 하나(스 2:57, 느 7:59).

entries.definition: HAT'TUSH (assembled). One of David's descendants, and another descendant who returned with Zerubbabel. 1 Chr 3:22; Ezr 8:2. A repairer of the wall, Neh 3:10. A priest who accompanied Zerubbabel and afterward sealed the covenant, Neh 10:4; 1 Kgs 12:2.
entries.definition_ko: 다윗의 후손이며 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아온 또 다른 후손(대상 3:22, 스 8:2), 성벽 수축자(느 3:10), 스룹바벨과 함께 온 후 언약에 인친 제사장(느 10:4, 12:2) 등을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: HAU'RAN (caves, caverns), a country east of the Jordan; the north-eastern boundary of Palestine, Eze 47:16, Eze 47:18, and the Auranitis of the Greeks, and now known as the Hauran. For situation of the country see Map at end of this volume. History. — Little was known of the Hauran previous to 1854. The works of Porter, 1855, Graham, 1858, Wetzstein, 1860, Burton and Drake, 1872, and Selah Merrill of the Am. Pal. Explor. Soc., 1877, have thrown much light on its extent, nature, and history, but a thorough exploration of the country yet remains to be made. When the Israelites conquered the land, the whole of this region appears to have been subject to Og, the king of Bashan, Num 21:33-35; Deut 3:1-5, and a large portion of it was allotted to Manasseh. The district would then include the Argob, the slope of the Hauran Mountains, where the Israelites found 60 fortified cities with walls and gates and a fertile tract. See Bashan. In the Roman period the country was divided into 5 provinces, Ituraea, Gaulanitis, Batanaea (applied also to the whole region), Trachonitis, and Auranitis. The ruins scattered over the region are very extensive and remarkable; those built in the caverns are regarded by Wetzstein as the most ancient, and possibly reaching back to the times of the Rephaim, Gen 14:5; Gen 15:20, and Deut 3:11. The villages are chiefly of stone houses, having gates and doors of large slabs of dolerite; the gateways of the larger buildings are ornamented with sculptured vines and inscriptions. The Arabs, according to Wetzstein, from near Yemen settled in the Hauran at about the beginning of the Christian era; later, a second immigration from south Arabia took place, and these controlled the country for five centuries, and they probably erected most of the stone buildings now in so good a state of preservation. A large number of inscriptions in various characters are yet to be deciphered, which will throw much light, no doubt, upon the ancient history of this wild region. Wetzstein states that the eastern section of the Lejah and the slopes of the Hauran Mountains contain at least 300 ruined cities and towns. Selah Merrill says that an important ruin is found in every half hour of travel, and that among these ruins he has himself visited and examined 60 ruined churches, and eleven of thirteen theatres, including one vast naumachia where mock sea-fights were held. And he concludes a paper read before the American Geographical Society in New York, Nov. 8, 1877 (Bulletin, No. 5), with the following remarks: "In every age previous to the Moslem conquest in a.d. 635 — running clear back to the time of the giants — this land has been thickly inhabited, generally by intelligent and wealthy people. Churches, theatres, palaces, temples, castles, baths, porticos, splendid roads, a multitude of inscriptions, remains of a perfect system of irrigation, historical notices of cathedrals, bishops, and a widespread Christian influence, notices of conquests and vast spoils falling into the hands of the victors, authentic notices of many successive and powerful races that have flourished here, and the surface of the whole country dotted with ruined towns, cities, and villages, — are convincing proofs that the statements found in the O.T. respecting the numbers of their armies and people may be accepted, so far as the capacities of the soil for supporting such a population are concerned, as the literal truth." See also Argob, Bashan, and Gilead.
entries.definition_ko: '굴들'이라는 뜻으로 요단 동편의 나라이며 팔레스타인의 북동쪽 경계다(겔 47:16,18). 헬라인의 아우라니티스이며 지금도 하우란으로 알려져 있다. 1854년 이전에는 이 지역에 대해 알려진 바가 적었다. 이스라엘이 그 땅을 정복할 때 이 지역 전체가 바산 왕 옥에게 속했던 것으로 보이며(민 21:33-35, 신 3:1-5) 상당 부분이 므낫세에게 배정되었다. 여기에 아르곱과 하우란 산지 비탈이 포함되는데, 이스라엘 사람들은 거기서 성벽과 성문을 갖춘 견고한 성읍 60개와 비옥한 땅을 발견했다.

entries.definition: HAV'ILAH, or HAVI'LAH (circle, district), a country abounding in gold, bdellium, and onyx-stone, Gen 2:11. Havilah is mentioned as a boundary of the children of Ishmael, Gen 25:18. Kalisch supposes that it was a country between the Persian and the Arabian gulfs; others hold that the "country of Havilah" in 1 Sam 15:7 refers to the region about Mount Seir, and that it was not probably identical with the Havilah of Gen 2:11. See Eden.
entries.definition_ko: 금과 베델리엄과 호마노가 많이 나는 땅이다(창 2:11). 이스마엘 자손의 경계로 언급된다(창 25:18). 페르시아 만과 아라비아 만 사이의 지역으로 보는 견해가 있고, 삼상 15:7의 '하윌라 땅'은 세일산 일대를 가리키며 창 2:11의 하윌라와는 같지 않을 것으로 보는 견해도 있다.

entries.definition: HAV'ILAH. A son of Cush, Gen 10:7. A son of Joktan, Gen 10:29.
entries.definition_ko: 구스의 아들(창 10:7), 욕단의 아들(창 10:29).

entries.definition: HA'VOTH-JA'IR(villages of Jair), a title applied to certain villages east of the Jordan which Jair captured and held. Num 32:41; Jud 10:4. The towns of Jair are included with the 60 cities given to Manasseh, Josh 13:30; 1 Chr 2:23; but the word rendered "villages" usually means a small collection of hovels in a country place. These towns were a part of one of the revenue-districts of Solomon, 1 Kgs 4:13.
entries.definition_ko: '야일의 마을들'이라는 뜻으로, 야일이 점령해 차지한 요단 동편의 어떤 마을들에 붙은 이름이다(민 32:41, 삿 10:4). 야일의 성읍들은 므낫세에게 준 60성읍에 포함되나(수 13:30, 대상 2:23) '마을'로 옮긴 말은 대개 시골의 작은 오두막 무리를 뜻한다. 이 성읍들은 솔로몬의 관할 구역 중 하나에 속했다(왕상 4:13).

entries.definition: HAWK, a general name for a well known group of fierce and rapacious birds, unclean by the Levitical law, Lev 11:16; Deut 14:15, but so sacred among the Greeks and Egyptians that to kill one, even unintentionally, was a capital crime. Of the ten or twelve species of these falcons found in Palestine most are migratory, Job 39:26. Kestrel, or Hawk. (Tinnunculus alaudarius. After Tristram.)
entries.definition_ko: 사납고 탐욕스러운 잘 알려진 새 무리를 두루 가리키는 이름으로 레위기 율법에서 부정하다(레 11:16, 신 14:15). 그러나 헬라인과 애굽인에게는 매우 신성하여 뜻하지 않게라도 죽이면 사형에 처해졌다. 팔레스타인에 있는 열 종 남짓의 매 중 대부분이 철새다(욥 39:26).

entries.definition: HAY, Prov 27:25. We are not to suppose that this word, as used in the Bible, denotes dried grass, as it does with us. The management of grass by the Hebrews as food for cattle was entirely different from ours. It was never dried and stored for winter use, but was cut green as it was wanted; and the phrase "mown grass," Ps 72:6, would be more properly rendered "grass that has just been fed off." So in Prov 27:25 the word translated "hay" means the first shoots of the grass; and the whole passage might properly be rendered, "The grass appeareth, and the green herb showeth itself, and the plants of the mountains are gathered." And in Isa 15:6 "hay" is put for "grass," and "grass" is put for the "green herb." The tenderness of grass, the rapidity of its growth, and the early period at which it is cut down and consumed afford the sacred writers some striking and beautiful illustrations. Ps 103:15; Isa 40:6; Jas 1:11. See Mowings.
entries.definition_ko: 성경에서 이 말은 우리처럼 말린 풀을 뜻하지 않는다(잠 27:25). 히브리인이 가축의 먹이로 풀을 다루는 방식은 우리와 전혀 달랐다. 말려서 겨울용으로 저장하지 않고 필요할 때 푸른 채로 베었다. 시 72:6의 '벤 풀'은 '방금 뜯어 먹은 풀'로 옮기는 편이 더 적절하다. 잠 27:25에서 '풀'로 옮긴 말은 풀의 첫 싹을 뜻한다. 풀의 연약함과 빨리 자람, 이른 시기에 베여 사라짐이 성경 기자들에게 인상적이고 아름다운 비유가 된다(시 103:15, 사 40:6, 약 1:11).

entries.definition: HAZ'AEL, (God sees), an officer in the court of Syria, and subsequently its powerful king. Elijah was commanded to anoint him king but left this duty to Elisha; and so when Hazael was despatched by his king, Benhadad, to Elisha to inquire about the results of the disease with which he was afflicted, the prophet predicted the elevation of Hazael to the throne of Syria, and a series of the most horrible cruelties of which he would be guilty toward the children of Israel,1 Kgs 19:15. Hazael expressed the utmost abhorrence of such conduct, but on the next day he smothered Benhadad to death and ascended the throne, 2 Kgs 8:7-16. He warred against the kingdom of Israel, 2 Kgs 10:32, and against Judah. He took Gath, and was averted from entering Jerusalem only by a rich bribe,2 Kgs 12:17-18. He reigned forty-six years, and was succeeded by his son, Benhadad. The conquests of Hazael's reign were lost during that of his son and successor, 2 Kgs 13:25.
entries.definition_ko: 수리아 궁정의 관리였다가 후에 강력한 왕이 되었다. 엘리야가 그에게 기름 부으라는 명을 받았으나 그 임무를 엘리사에게 남겼다. 왕 벤하닷이 자기 병의 결과를 물으려 하사엘을 엘리사에게 보냈을 때, 선지자는 하사엘이 수리아 왕위에 오를 것과 이스라엘 자손에게 저지를 끔찍한 잔학을 예언했다(왕상 19:15). 하사엘은 그런 짓에 극도의 혐오를 표했으나, 이튿날 벤하닷을 질식시켜 죽이고 왕위에 올랐다(왕하 8:7-15). 이스라엘과 유다를 쳤고 가드를 빼앗았으며, 많은 뇌물을 받고서야 예루살렘 진입을 그쳤다(왕하 12:17-18). 46년간 다스렸고 아들 벤하닷이 뒤를 이었다.

entries.definition: HAZAEL, HOUSE OF, either family or palace of Hazael, Am 1:4.
entries.definition_ko: 하사엘의 집안 또는 궁전을 뜻한다(암 1:4).

entries.definition: HAZA'IAH (whom Jehovah sees), a Judite, Neh 11:5.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 사람(느 11:5).

entries.definition: HA'ZAR-AD'DAR (village of Adar, or greatness), called Adar in Josh 15:3; to the west of Kadesh-barnea, and on a ridge between Canaan and the desert; now 'Ain el-Kudeirat.
entries.definition_ko: '아달의 마을'이라는 뜻으로 수 15:3에서는 아달이라 불린다. 가데스바네아 서쪽, 가나안과 광야 사이의 능선에 있다.

entries.definition: HA'ZAR-E'NAN (fountain, village), a boundary of the Promised Land. Num 34:9-10; Eze 47:17; Eze 48:1. Porter would identify it with Kuryetein, 60 miles east-north-east of Damascus, where are large fountains, fragments of columns, and other ruins, but this is too far north; Canon Cook suggests Ayon ed-Dara, a fountain in the heart of the central chain of Anti-Libanus.

HA'ZAR-GAD'DAH (village of fortune), a town in the south of Judah, Josh 15:27, which Wilton would identify with Wady Mubughik, where are extensive ruins of great antiquity; Grove with el-Ghurrah, about 9 miles east of Beersheba; Conder with Judeideh, the name of a spring near Hebron.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 남부의 한 성읍(수 15:27).

entries.definition: HA'ZAR-HAT'TICON (middle village) , a place on the border of the Hauran, Eze 47:16.
entries.definition_ko: 하우란 경계의 한 곳(겔 47:16).

entries.definition: HA'ZAR-SHU'AL (village or enclosure of jackals), a town in the southern portion of Judah; given afterward to Simeon, Josh 15:28; Josh 19:3; 1 Chr 4:28, and repeopled after the Captivity, Neh 11:27. Wilton suggested Beni Shail, near Gaza, as its site, but Van de Velde and Conder, with greater pi-obability, locate it at Saweh, between Beersheba and Moladah. The ruins are on a high bluff; a wall built of flint blocks surrounds the site, and justifies the name Hazar ("enclosure").
entries.definition_ko: '자칼의 마을'이라는 뜻으로 유다 남부의 성읍이며 후에 시므온에게 주어졌고(수 15:28, 19:3, 대상 4:28) 포로기 이후 다시 사람이 살았다(느 11:27).

entries.definition: HA'ZAR-SU'SAH, and HA'ZAR-SU'SIM (village of horses), a city of Simeon, in the southern border of Judah. Josh 19:5; 1 Chr 4:31. Wilton believes it was in Wady es-Sauiek, near Gaza, but Conder proposes Beit Susia, south of Beit Jibrin.
entries.definition_ko: '말들의 마을'이라는 뜻으로 유다 남쪽 경계에 있는 시므온의 성읍이다(수 19:5, 대상 4:31).

entries.definition: HA'ZARMA'VETH (court of death), the third of Joktan's sons. Gen 10:26; 1 Chr 1:20. He was the progenitor of the inhabitants of modern Hadramaut, a province in South-eastern Arabia. This province abounds in frankincense and myrrh, but the climate is very unhealthy; whence its singular name.
entries.definition_ko: '죽음의 뜰'이라는 뜻으로 욕단의 셋째 아들이다(창 10:26, 대상 1:20). 아라비아 남동부의 지금 하드라마우트 지역 주민의 조상이다. 이 지역은 유향과 몰약이 많이 나나 기후가 매우 나빠 이런 특이한 이름이 붙었다.

entries.definition: HA'ZEL, Gen 30:37. It is generally supposed that the almond tree is intended in this passage. The original word is thought to be susceptible of this rendering.
entries.definition_ko: 창 30:37의 나무로, 대개 살구나무를 뜻하는 것으로 여겨진다.

entries.definition: HAZ'ELELPO'NI (shade coming upon me), a sister to some descendants of Judah, 1 Chr 4:3.
entries.definition_ko: 유다의 후손들의 누이(대상 4:3).

entries.definition: HA'ZER, same as Hazar; used only in composition.
entries.definition_ko: 하살과 같으며 합성어에만 쓰인다.

entries.definition: HAZE'RIM (the villages). In Deut 2:28 we read that the Avim dwelt in Hazerim, even unto Azzeh or Gaza; and the notice of the Avites in Josh 13:3-4, as the most southern of the tribes inhabiting the Canaanitish country clearly identifies their land with the mountains of Azazimeh. See Palmer's Desert of the Exodus (Amer. ed.), p. 360.
entries.definition_ko: '마을들'이라는 뜻이다. 신 2:23에 아위 사람이 하세림, 곧 가사까지 거주했다고 나오며, 수 13:3-4에 아위 사람이 가나안 땅에 살던 부족 중 가장 남쪽이라 한 것이 그 땅을 아자지메 산지와 분명히 연결한다.

entries.definition: HAZE'ROTH (villages, or enclosures), the second station of the Israelites, Num 11:35; Neh 12:16; Num 33:17-18; Deut 1:1, and identified with 'Ain Hudherah, 40 miles north-east of Sinai.
entries.definition_ko: '마을들' 또는 '울타리들'이라는 뜻으로 이스라엘의 둘째 진 친 곳이다(민 11:35, 33:17-18, 신 1:1). 시내산 북동쪽 40마일의 아인 후데라로 확인된다.

entries.definition: HAZ'EZON-TA'MAR, and HAZ'ANON- TA'MAR (felling of palm trees), the old name of En-gedi,Gen 14:7; 2 Chr 20:2; a city as old as the oldest in Syria, the contemporary of Sodom and Gomorrah, and already a city when Hebron was first founded. See Tristram's Land of Israel, p. 285, and also En-gedi.
entries.definition_ko: '종려나무 벰'이라는 뜻으로 엔게디의 옛 이름이다(창 14:7, 대하 20:2). 수리아에서 가장 오래된 성읍만큼 오래되어 소돔·고모라와 같은 시대였고, 헤브론이 처음 세워질 때 이미 성읍이었다.

entries.definition: HA'ZIEL (vision of God), a Levite in the time of David, 1 Chr 23:9.
entries.definition_ko: 다윗 때의 레위인(대상 23:9).

entries.definition: HA'ZO (vision), a son of Nahor, Gen 22:22.
entries.definition_ko: 나홀의 아들(창 22:22).

entries.definition: HA'ZOR (enclosure). The city of King Jabin; destroyed by Joshua, Josh 11:1, Josh 11:10-11; given to Naphtali, Josh 19:36; again possessed by the Canaanites, Jud 4:2, who had for its king Jabin — a generic title, probably, like Pharaoh in Egypt — who reigned in Hazor and whose general was Sisera. It was fortified by Solomon, 1 Kgs 9:15; its people were carried into captivity by Tiglath-pileser. 2 Kgs 15:29. The city appears to have been situated on a hill in the midst of a plain, and was a stronghold. Josh 11:4; Jud 4:3. Several places have been suggested as the site: Tell Khureibeh, a rocky peak near Kedesh, by Robinson, and Conder points out the name Hadireh, the Arabic equivalent of Hazor, near this; modern Hazere, where are ruins, by Thomson; but doubtless it is to be found at Khurbet Hurrah, 2 1/2 miles south-east of Kedesh, as proposed by the Palestine Memoirs. Remains of ancient walls, towers, and a fortress are to be found, and also broken glass and pottery. A city in the south of Judah; probably should be written Hazor-ithman, Josh 15:23. Another town of Judah; called Hazor-hadattah, or New Hazor, Josh 15:25. Robinson proposes el-Hudherah; Conder, el-Hazzdrah, near Beit Jibrin, as its site. Hezron, which is Hazor, Josh 15:25; rendered by Canon Cook "Kerioth Hezron, which is Hazor." He would identify it with el-Kuryetein, where are large ruins seen by De Sauley. It is supposed to have been the home of Judas Iscariot, the man of Kerioth, Matt 10:4; Conder suggested Kheshram, north of Beer-sheba, as the site of this Hazor.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 야빈 왕의 성읍으로 여호수아가 멸했고(수 11:1,10-11) 납달리에게 주어졌으며(수 19:36) 다시 가나안 사람이 차지했다(삿 4:2). 그 왕은 야빈이라 불렸는데(애굽의 바로처럼 통칭이었을 것이다) 하솔에서 다스렸고 그 군대 장관이 시스라였다. 솔로몬이 견고케 했으며(왕상 9:15) 그 백성이 디글랏 빌레셀에게 사로잡혀 갔다(왕하 15:29). 평지 한가운데 언덕 위에 자리한 요새였던 것으로 보인다(수 11:4, 삿 4:3). 2) 남쪽의 한 성읍.

entries.definition: HEAD'-BANDS were perhaps fillets for the hair. Isa 3:20. See Head dress.
entries.definition_ko: 머리에 매는 띠였던 것으로 보인다(사 3:20). 머리 장식 참조.

entries.definition: HEAD'-DRESS, Hats were unknown to the Hebrews. The attempt of Jason to introduce them was regarded as a grievance, 2 Mace. 4:12. "Coverings for the head were not in ordinary use. Thus, it was a token of mourning to cover the head, 2 Sam 15:30; Jer 14:3-4, and the mantle seems to have been employed for the purpose, 1 Kgs 19:13. The head-dresses that were then used Head-dress of Assyrian King and Queen. (From Nineveh Marbles.) were rather for ornament. This was specially the case with the high priest's mitre and the 'bonnets' of the ordinary priests, which are expressly said to have been 'for glory and for beauty.' Ex 28:36-40. And those which were intended by the Hebrew words tzaniph and peer seem to have been worn only by eminent persons or on festive occasions. The former word implies wrapping around, after the fashion of a turban; it is described as used by men, Job 29:14 Syrian Head-dresses. Damascus. (Ayre.) (in our version 'diadem'); by women, Isa 3:23 ('hoods'); as belonging to kings, Isa 62:3 ('diadem'); to the high priest, Zech 3:5 ('mitre'). The latter, peer, conveying the idea of ornament or beauty, is said to have been worn by priests, Ex 39:28; Eze 44:18 ('bonnets'), by females, Isa 3:20, by a bride-groom, Isa 61:10, and by others in gala-dress. Isa 61:3;Eze 24:17, 1 Chr 24:23."— Ayre. The Assyrian head-dress is described in Eze 23:15 as consisting of a high turban. The word rendered "hats" in Dan 3:21 properly applies to a cloak.
entries.definition_ko: 히브리인에게 모자는 알려져 있지 않았다. 머리를 덮는 것은 일상적으로 쓰이지 않았으니, 머리를 가리는 것이 애도의 표시였다(삼하 15:30, 렘 14:3-4). 그때 쓰인 머리 장식은 오히려 장식용이었다. 특히 대제사장의 관과 일반 제사장의 '두건'이 그러해 '영화롭고 아름답게' 하려는 것이라 분명히 말한다(출 28:36-40). '차니프'와 '페에르'로 표현된 것은 지체 높은 이들이나 잔치 때에만 쓰였던 듯하다. 앞의 말은 터번처럼 둘러 감는 것을 함축한다.

entries.definition: HEAP. See Stones.
entries.definition_ko: 돌 참조.

entries.definition: HEART, Acts 16:14. The seat of the affections, desires, hopes, and motives. John 14:1; Esth 1:10. The term is also used by the Bible writers to designate the understanding, 1 Cor 2:9, and intellectual perceptions. It is further a general term for the spiritual nature of man. Isa 1:5; 2 Cor 4:6. In the latter passage the apostle speaks of the light shining in our hearts, teaching us of Christ as the One who reveals God. The heart is declared to be corrupt and full of evil, Eccl 9:3, and deceit, Jer 17:9, the seat of sin and crime. Matt 15:19, as also of faith. Rom 10:10. The Lord "looketh on the heart," 1 Sam 16:7, in contrast to the outward appearance, and we are commanded to cultivate it, as the most important part of our nature, rather than external appearances. Prov 4:4; Joel 2:13. The expression "to speak in the heart," 1 Sam 1:13, is synonymous with "to think."
entries.definition_ko: 감정과 소망과 동기의 자리다(행 16:14, 요 14:1). 성경 기자들은 이 말로 지각(고전 2:9)과 지적 인식을 가리키기도 한다. 나아가 사람의 영적 본성을 두루 가리키는 말이다(사 1:5, 고후 4:6). 마음은 부패하고 악이 가득하며(전 9:3) 속임이 있고(렘 17:9) 죄와 범죄의 자리이나(마 15:19) 또한 믿음의 자리다(롬 10:10). 주님은 외모가 아니라 '중심을 보신다'(삼상 16:7). '마음속으로 말하다'(삼상 1:13)는 '생각하다'와 같은 뜻이다.

entries.definition: HEARTH. The Hebrew words so translated do not, any of them, mean what we call a hearth. Thus, the "hearth" of Gen 18:6 was the heap of ashes covering the hot stones on which the bread was baked, according to the Eastern custom. See Bread. The "hearth" of Ps 102:3 means fagot as fuel; in Isa 30:14, not the hearth, but the burning mass. When we read that King Jehoiakim threw the cut leaves of Jeremiah's prophecy into the fire that was on the hearth, we are to understand that before him was a portable furnace or brazier of charcoal, Jer 36:22-23.
entries.definition_ko: 이렇게 옮긴 히브리어들은 어느 것도 우리가 말하는 화덕을 뜻하지 않는다. 창 18:6의 '화덕'은 동방 관습대로 떡을 굽는 달군 돌을 덮은 재 무더기였다. 시 102:3의 '화덕'은 연료로 쓰는 장작을, 사 30:14에서는 화덕이 아니라 타는 덩어리를 뜻한다. 여호야김이 예레미야의 예언을 오려 불에 던졌다는 대목은 그 앞에 숯을 담은 이동식 화로가 있었음을 뜻한다(렘 36:22-23).

entries.definition: HEATH. Jer 17:6; Jer 48:6. No true heath is found in Palestine. There is great probability that the dwarf juniper or savin (Juniperus sabina), which grows in the most sterile and desolate parts of the desert, is the plant intended. "Its gloomy, stunted appearance, with its scale-like leaves pressed close to its gnarled stems and cropped close by the wild goats, as it clings to the rocks about Petra, gives great force to the contrast suggested by the prophet between him that trusteth in man, naked and destitute, and the man that trusteth in the Lord, flourishing as a tree planted by the waters." — Tristram.
entries.definition_ko: 팔레스타인에는 참 히스가 자라지 않는다(렘 17:6, 48:6). 광야의 가장 메마르고 황량한 곳에서 자라는 난쟁이 향나무일 가능성이 높다. 그 음침하고 왜소한 모습이 페트라 주변 바위에 붙어 자라는 것을 보면, 사람을 의지하는 벌거벗고 궁핍한 자와 여호와를 의지하여 물가에 심긴 나무처럼 번성하는 자의 대비가 더욱 실감난다.

entries.definition: HEA'THEN, Ps 2:1. This term (from heath, one who lives on the heaths or in the woods, like pagans, i.e. villagers) is applied in the English Bible to all idolaters or to all nations except the Jews. See Gentile. It now denotes all nations except Christians, Jews and Mohammedans.
entries.definition_ko: 영어 성경에서 이 말은 모든 우상 숭배자, 곧 유대인을 뺀 모든 민족에게 쓰인다(시 2:1). 지금은 그리스도인과 유대인과 이슬람교도를 뺀 모든 민족을 가리킨다. 이방인 참조.

entries.definition: HEAVE-OFFERING. See Offering.
entries.definition_ko: 제사 참조.

entries.definition: HEAVEN The general idea expressed by the word in the Bible is of a realm different from the earth and hell. Under this general realm are included two realms — the one the material, the other the spiritual heaven. The plural is often used in both cases, most frequently in Matthew, and always in the phrase "the Father in the heavens," "the kingdom of the heavens." The heavens or heaven is contrasted with the earth, Gen 1:1; Ps 115:15; Matt 5:18; Matt 24:35, and is represented as above us. This is the material world of air and the firmament. It is looked upon by the Hebrews as a solid expanse, Gen 1:11, Heb., which has windows, Gen 7:11; 2 Kgs 7:2, 2 Kgs 7:19, and doors. Ps 78:23, The rain descends from it, Jas 5:18; 2 Sam 21:10, and the frost, Job 38:29. The stars are called the "stars of heaven," Nah 3:16, the "host of heaven," Deut 4:19, or the "lights in the firmament," Gen 1:14, and the fowls fly in the midst of it, Rev 19:17. This material and stellar heaven will be dissolved at the final consummation, Rev 6:14; 2 Pet 3:10, and with the earth give place to a new heaven and a new earth. Rev 21:1. The term refers also to a realm beyond this material universe, and different from it — an invisible realm of holiness and bliss. This heaven is the peculiar abode of God, who is described as the God of heaven and the God in heaven. 1 Kgs 8:30; Dan 2:28; Matt 5:45. Christ is said to be the "Lord from heaven," 1 Cor 15:47, and to have "come down from" or to have descended from heaven, John 3:13, etc. Into this heaven he has again ascended. Luke 24:51; Acts 1:9; Eph 4:8; 1 Pet 3:22. Here God has his throne, here the angels dwell. Matt 22:30. It is the place where God's will is done. Matt 6:10, and where joy, Luke 15:7, and peace reign, Acts 19:38. It is here that Christ has prepared the many mansions, John 14:2, and into which Elijah passed, 2 Kgs 2:1. Believers have an inheritance in this realm, 1 Pet 1:4, and may lay up treasures in it. Matt 6:20. Heaven is in this signification contrasted with hell, Ps 139:8, into which Satan fell, Luke 10:18; 2 Pet 2:4. The terms "paradise," Luke 23:43, and "Abraham's bosom," Luke 16:22, designate a state of bliss in the other world, but not the highest and ultimate state. The third heaven, 2 Cor 12:2, into which Paul was rapt in a vision, is probably only another expression for the highest heaven. The later rabbins distinguished seven heavens: the first three belong to the material universe; the other four to the spiritual world, where God, the saints, and angels dwell. That the believer's heaven is not merely a state, but also a world of space, is abundantly testified to not only by many of the above passages, but also by such expressions as "heavenly places," Eph 1:3. The bliss of heaven is beyond our conception. This is indicated by the many forms and figures used to give us an impression of its joys. John 14:2-3; Heb 4 and Heb 11; Rev 3, Rev 21, Rev 22. Heaven, Kingdom of. See Kingdom.
entries.definition_ko: 성경에서 이 말이 나타내는 일반적 관념은 땅이나 지옥과 다른 영역이다. 이 큰 영역 안에 물질적 하늘과 영적 하늘 두 영역이 있다. 하늘은 땅과 대비되며(창 1:1, 시 115:15, 마 5:18) 우리 위에 있는 것으로 그려진다. 이는 공기와 궁창의 물질 세계다. 히브리인은 이를 창이 있고(창 7:11, 왕하 7:2) 문이 있는(시 78:23) 단단한 펼침으로 보았다. 거기서 비가 내리고(약 5:18) 서리가 내린다(욥 38:29). 별들은 '하늘의 별', '하늘의 군대'(신 4:19), '궁창의 광명체'(창 1:14)라 불리고 새들이 그 가운데 난다(계 19:17).

entries.definition: HE'BER (alliance). Grandson of Asher. Gen 46:17; Num 26:45; 1 Chr 7:31. A Judite, 1 Chr 4:18. A Gadite, 1 Chr 5:13. A Benjamite, 1 Chr 8:17. Another Benjamite, 1 Chr 8:22. Heber the Kenite, the husband of Jael, who slew Sisera, Jud 4:22. See Jael, Sisera. Heber appears to have led a life apart from the rest of his tribe. He must have been a person of consequence, from the fact that it is stated that there was peace between him and the powerful king Jabin, Jud 4:17. For Eber, Luke 3:35.

entries.definition: HE'BREWS, EPISTLE TO THE, was written about the years 62 to 64 in Italy, Heb 13:24, and addressed to the believing Jews of Palestine and the East. The design of the author was not, primarily, to make new converts or to console old ones, but to guard them against apostasy and to strengthen their faith by an exhibition of the evidence in favor of the pre-eminence of the religion of Christ over that of Moses, One gets the impression of peculiar temptations to apostasy or a weakening in the faith against which the Hebrew Christians are continually warned in the Epistle, ch. Ruth 2:1; Song of Solomon 4:1, Song 4:14; Ezr 10:23. The Epistle at once exhibits the unity and the characteristic difference of the Old and the New Testament economy and revelation. Both were alike of divine origin, Heb 1:1-2, but the former was imperfect and defective, chs. Heb 8:6-7; Dan 10:1. This is proved by an extended consideration of the character of Christ, the Mediator of the new covenant, and of the mediators (Moses and Aaron) of the old covenant, and by a consideration of the prophecy of Jeremiah concerning a new covenant, ch. Neh 10:16, and its spiritual character, chs. Heb 9-10. In the comparison thus instituted we discover a marked contrast between the old and new covenants, so far as both their nature and their founders are concerned. The Epistle exhibits the person of Christ, the Author of the new covenant, as superior in dignity to the angels, ch. Heb 1, and proves it by the O.T. itself. Christ was the very brightness of God's glory and the express image of his person, ch. John 1:3. Therefore the conclusion is drawn that the revelation made by him is of greater authority than that made by angels, which was accepted, ch. Gen 2:2. He is then represented as of superior dignity to Moses, ch, Heb 3:3, and as our High Priest, ch. Dan 3:1, who belongs to the order of Melchisedek, ch. Heb 5:16; Heb 7:21. In order to perform the high priestly functions, it was necessary for him to endure the sufferings and temptations incident to the humanity he intended to save, Heb 2:17; Gal 4:15; 1 Kgs 12:2, and to assume human nature, ch. Num 2:14. He thus becomes the Author of salvation, ch. Heb 5:9, by the shedding of his blood, Gal 2:9; Heb 9:12. The superiority of his high priesthood is shown not only by his super-angelic nature, but in his freedom from sin, Gal 4:15; Heb 7:27, The Aaronic priests were sinful, Heb 7:28. Christ has thus purchased an eternal salvation for all who believe in him in a View of Hebron fiom the South. (After Photograph by Bonfils.) Mount Hermon, with Ruins of an Ancient Temple.
