entries.definition_ko: '찬양하는'이라는 뜻으로 유다 계열 인물, '에스드모아의 아버지'로 기록된다(역대상 4:17).

entries.definition: ISH'BAK (leaving behind), a son of Abraham by Keturah. Gen 25:2; 1 Chr 1:32. From him sprang the northern Arabians.
entries.definition_ko: '뒤에 남기는'이라는 뜻으로 아브라함이 그두라에게서 얻은 아들이다(창 25:2, 대상 1:32). 그에게서 북방 아라비아인이 나왔다.

entries.definition: ISH'BI-BE'NOB (*dwelling in rest), a son of Kapha, a Philistine giant slain by Abishai. 2 Sam 21:16-17.
entries.definition_ko: '놉에 거하는 자'라는 뜻으로 라파의 아들, 블레셋 거인족 중 하나로 다윗을 전투에서 공격했으나 아비새에게 죽임당했다(사무엘하 21:16).

entries.definition:
I'SHI (saving). 1,2. Judites. 1 Chr 2:31; 1 Chr 4:20. A Simeonite. 1 Chr 4:42. A Manassite. 1 Chr 5:24.

I'SHI, Hos 2:16, signifying my husband, and BAALI, in the same passage, signifying my Lord, are figuratively used to denote that Israel once played the whore in serving idols, but would now serve the living God. The latter having been used in idol-worship, would become obsolete in this sense. Hos 2:17.
entries.definition_ko: 1) '구원'이라는 뜻으로 유다 사람들(대상 2:31, 4:20), 시므온 사람(대상 4:42), 므낫세 사람(대상 5:24)의 이름이다. 2) 호 2:16의 '이시'는 '나의 남편'을, 같은 구절의 '바알리'는 '나의 주'를 뜻하며, 이스라엘이 한때 우상을 섬겨 음행했으나 이제 살아 계신 하나님을 섬기리라는 것을 비유적으로 나타낸다. 뒤의 말은 우상 숭배에 쓰였으므로 이런 뜻으로는 더 이상 쓰이지 않게 될 것이었다(호 2:17).

entries.definition: ISHI'AH (whom Jehovah lends), a chieftain of Issachar. 1 Chr 7:3.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 빌려주신'이라는 뜻으로 다윗 시대 잇사갈 지파 우두머리 중 하나인 이스라히야의 다섯 아들 중 막내이다(역대상 7:3).

entries.definition: ISHI'JAH (whom Jehovah lends), one who had a foreign wife. Ezr 10:31.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 빌려주신'이라는 뜻으로 이방인 아내와 결혼한 브네하림 가문의 평신도 이스라엘인이다(에스라 10:31).

entries.definition: ISH'MA (desolation), a Judite. 1 Chr 4:3.
entries.definition_ko: '황폐'라는 뜻으로 유다 족보에 나오는 이름이다(역대상 4:3).

entries.definition: ISH'MAEL (whom God hears). 1. The son of Abraham by Hagar. Previous to his birth, when his mother, being ill-treated by Sarah, had fled from the house, the angel of the Lord announced to her that her seed should be innumerable, and that her offspring should be of a belligerent and wild disposition: "He will be a wild man; his hand will be against every man's hand, and every man's hand against him." Gen 16:12. Ishmael was circumcised at the age of 13. Gen 17:25. Subsequently, the jealousy of Sarah was aroused by Ishmael's mocking at Isaac, Gen 21:9, and she demanded that the offender and his mother be sent away from the home. Abraham, granting Sarah's request, sent the bondwoman and her son off, after supplying them with water and bread. Departing, they went off into the wilderness of Beer-sheba. The stock of water became exhausted, and the lad, overcome with fatigue and thirst, sunk down, apparently to die. God appeared for their deliverance, directed Hagar to a fountain of water, and renewed his promise to make of him a great nation. Ishmael remained in the wilderness and became a hunter. Gen 21:13-20. At length he married an Egyptian woman, and so rapidly did his progeny multiply that in a few years afterward they are spoken of as a trading nation. Gen 37:25. The last we see of the first-born son of Abraham is at the cave of Machpelah, where he joins with Isaac in interring the remains of his father. Gen 25:9. Ishmael no doubt became a wild man of the desert, the progenitor of the roaming Bedouin tribes of the East, so well known as robbers to this day that travellers through their territory must be well armed and hire a band of robbers to protect them against their fellow-robbers. Ishmael is also the spiritual father of the Mohammedans, who are nothing but bastard Jews. They apply to themselves the promise of a large posterity given to Ishmael. Gen 21:13, Gen 21:18. A descendant of Saul. 1 Chr 8:38; 1 Chr 9:44. A Judite. 2 Chr 19:11. A Judite, one of the captains who assisted Jehoiada to set Joash on the throne, 2 Chr 23:1. A priest who had a foreign wife. Ezr 10:22. Ishmael, "the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed royal "of Judah, murdered, at Mizpah, Gedaliah, the governor of Judyea, appointed by Nebuchadnezzar, who, although warned by Johanan, had unsuspiciously received him. Every circumstance contributed to increase the baseness of the deed — the generous incredulity of Gedaliah, the fact that the murder took place immediately after a feast given by Gedaliah to Ishmael and other prominent Jews who had conspired with him, and the slaughter of all the attendant Jews and also of some Chaldaean soldiers. The secrecy of the deed was so profound that the town knew nothing of it until the second day, when Ishmael hypocritically received eighty devotees who came bearing offering and incense to the house of the Lord, and murdered all but ten of them, who purchased their lives by promise of money. This carnival of blood being over, Ishmael surprised the town and carried away to the Ammonites the inhabitants, including the daughters of Zedokiah. But Johanan followed him, met him in battle at "the great waters" — probably the Pool of Gibeon — defeated him, rescued the prisoners, and compelled Ishmael to flee to the Ammonites. See Jer 41; 2 Kgs 25:23, 2 Kgs 25:25. See also Gedaliah. The motives of Ishmael were partly corrupt, since he had been tampered with by Baalis, king of the Ammonites, and partly mistaken patriotism, bitter hatred, and craven fear of the Chaldaeans.
entries.definition_ko: 아브라함과 하갈의 아들로, 태어나기 전 천사가 '그의 손이 모든 사람을 치겠고'라 예언했다(창 16:12). 13세에 할례를 받았으나 이삭을 조롱하여 어머니와 함께 쫓겨나 브엘세바 광야에서 방황하다 하나님의 돌봄을 받았다(창 21:9-21). 열두 아들의 조상이 되어 아라비아 북부에 거주하며 이집트에서 앗수르까지 퍼졌다(창 25:12-18).

entries.definition: ISH'MAELITES, the descendants of Ishmael. Gen 37:25. The company of Ishmaelites to whom Joseph was sold are elsewhere called Midianites. Gen 37:28. Probably they were Ishmaelites who dwelt in Midian. It is evident, however, that the two names were sometimes applied to the same people, Jud 8:22, Jud 8:24, though we know the descendants of Midian were not Ishmaelites, for Midian was a son of Abraham by Keturah.
entries.definition_ko: 이스마엘의 후손이다(창 37:25). 요셉을 사들인 이스마엘 상인 무리가 다른 곳에서는 미디안 사람이라 불린다(창 37:28). 아마도 미디안에 살던 이스마엘 사람이었을 것이다. 다만 두 이름이 때로 같은 백성에게 쓰였음이 분명하다(삿 8:22,24). 미디안의 후손이 이스마엘 자손이 아님은 미디안이 아브라함과 그두라 사이의 아들이었기에 분명하다.

entries.definition: ISHMAI'AH (Jehovah hears), the ruler of Zebulun during David's reign. 1 Chr 27:19.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 들으셨다'는 뜻. (1.) 시글락에서 다윗과 합류한 기브온 사람, '삼십 용사 가운데, 그리고 삼십 용사 위의 용사'(역대상 12:4). (2.) 오바댜의 아들이며 다윗과 솔로몬 시대 스불론의 부왕(역대상 27:19).

entries.definition: ISH'MEELITE. 1 Chr 2:17. See Ishmaelites.
entries.definition_ko: 이스마엘 자손을 가리키는 흠정역의 다른 표기이다(역대상 2:17).

entries.definition: ISH'MERAI (whom Jehovah keeps), a Benjamite. 1 Chr 8:18.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 지키시는'이라는 뜻으로 베냐민 사람, 엘바알 가문이다(역대상 8:18).

entries.definition: I'SHOD (man of renown), a Manassite. 1 Chr 7:18.
entries.definition_ko: '영광의 사람'이라는 뜻으로 요단 동편 므낫세 지파, 함몰레겟의 아들이다(역대상 7:18).

entries.definition: ISH'PAN (bald), a Benjamite chief. 1 Chr 8:22.
entries.definition_ko: 베냐민 사람, 사삭 가문이다(역대상 8:22).

entries.definition: ISH'TOB (men of Tob), apparently a small kingdom which formed a part of the country of Aram, and named with Zobah, Rehob, and Maachah. 2 Sam 10:6, 2 Sam 10:8. See Tob.
entries.definition_ko: '돕 사람들'이라는 뜻으로 아람 땅의 일부를 이룬 작은 왕국으로 보이며, 소바·르홉·마아가와 함께 언급된다(삼하 10:6,8). 돕 참조.

entries.definition: ISH'UA (quiet). A son of Asher. 1 Chr 7:30.
entries.definition_ko: 아셀의 아들(대상 7:30).

entries.definition: ISH'UAH (quiet), the second son of Asher, Gen 46:17; called Isuah 1 Chr 7:30.
entries.definition_ko: '조용한'이라는 뜻으로 아셀의 둘째 아들이다(창세기 46:17).

entries.definition: ISH'UI (quiet). The third son of Asher, 1 Chr 7:30; called Isui and Jesul Gen 46:17; Num 26:44. A son of Saul, 1 Sam 14:49:not elsewhere mentioned; he probably died young.
entries.definition_ko: '조용한'이라는 뜻. 아셀의 셋째 아들로(대상 7:30) 창 46:17과 민 26:44에서는 이스위, 예수이라 불린다. 또한 사울의 아들로(삼상 14:49) 다른 데는 언급되지 않으며 아마도 일찍 죽었을 것이다.

entries.definition: ISLES OF THE GENTILES. Gen 10:5; Zeph 2:11; Ps 72:10; Eze 26:15. The Hebrew word signifies any land bordering on the sea, and "the isles of the Gentiles" refers to the coasts of the Mediterranean, Black, and Caspian Seas.
entries.definition_ko: 창 10:5, 습 2:11, 시 72:10, 겔 26:15에 나오는 표현이다. 히브리어는 바다에 접한 모든 땅을 뜻하며, '이방의 섬들'은 지중해와 흑해, 카스피해의 해안을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: ISMACHI'AH (whom Jehovah supports), a Levitical overseer of offerings under Hezekiah. 2 Chr 31:13.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 들으신다'는 뜻으로 다윗에게 시글락에서 합류한 기브온 용사 지도자 중 하나였다(역대상 12:4). 별도로 '여호와께서 붙드시는 자'라는 뜻의 동명이인은 히스기야 시대 헌물 감독 레위인 중 하나였다(역대하 31:13).

entries.definition: ISMAI'AH (Jehovah hears), a Gibeonite chief who joined David at Ziklag. 1 Chr 12:4.
entries.definition_ko: 시글락에서 다윗에게 합류한 기브온 지도자(대상 12:4).

entries.definition: IS'PAH (bald), a Benjamite chief. 1 Chr 8:16.
entries.definition_ko: '대머리'라는 뜻으로 브리아 가문 베냐민 사람, 지파 우두머리 중 하나이다(역대상 8:16).

entries.definition: ISRAEL, KING'DOM OF, a term not infrequently applied to the united kingdom before the revolt of the ten tribes, 1 Sam 13:1, 1 Sam 13:4; 1 Sam 15:28; 1 Sam 16:1; 2 Sam 5:12; 2 Sam 7:16; 1 Kgs 2:46; 1 Kgs 4:1; but the term was also used to designate the country of the ten tribes only during the dissensions which followed the death of Saul. After the death of Solomon and the revolt under Rehoboam, 1 Kgs 12:20, 1 Kgs 12:28, 1 Kgs 12:32, it was generally, but not uniformly, applied to the independent kingdom formed by the ten tribes in the north of Palestine; so that thenceforth the kings of the ten tribes were called "kings of Israel," and the descendants of David, who ruled over Judah and Benjamin, were called "kings of Judah." In the prophets "Judah" and "Israel" are often mentioned. Hos 4:15; Ex 5:3, Hos 5:5; Jer 6:10; Zech 7:1;Hos 8:2-3, Isa 8:6, Hos 8:8; Hos 9:1, Hos 9:7; Am 1:1; Am 2:6; Num 3:14; Mic 1:5; Isa 5:7. The two kingdoms are sometimes called "the two houses of Israel." Isa 8:14. The area of the kingdom of Israel is estimated at about 9000 square miles, or about the same as that of the State of New Hampshire, and its population at from 3,000,000 to 4,000,000. The kingdom lasted 254 years, b.c. 975-721. The capitals were Shechem, 1 Kgs 12:25, Tirzah, 1 Kgs 14:17, and Samaria, 1 Kgs 16:24. Jezreel was also a summer residence of some of its kings. Of the 19 kings, not counting Tibni, not one was a godly man. The idolatry introduced by Jeroboam was continued, notwithstanding the partial reformations of Elijah, Elisha, and other faithful prophets. The following admirable summary of the history of the kingdom in four periods is given in Smith's Abridged Dictionary, by W.A. Wright. "(a) b.c. 975-929.— Jerohofim had not sufficient force of character in himself to make a lasting impression on his people. A king, but not a founder of a dynasty, he aimed at nothing beyond securing his present elevation. The army soon learned its power to dictate to the isolated monarch and disunited people. Baasha, in the midst of the army at Gibbethon, slew the son and successor of Jeroboam; Zimri, a captain of chariots, slew the son and successor of Baasha; Omri, the captain of the host, was chosen to punish Zimri; and after a civil war of four years he prevailed over Tibni, the choice of half the people. "(b) b.c. 929-884.— For forty-five years Israel was governed by the house of Omri. That sagacious king pitched on the strong hill of Samaria as the site of his capital. The princes of his house cultivated an alliance with the kings of Judah, which was cemented by the marriage of Jehoram and Athaliah. The adoption of Baal-worship led to a reaction in the nation, to the moral triumph of the prophets in the person of Elijah, and to the extinction of the house of Ahab, in obedience to the bidding of Elisha, "(c) b.c. 884-772.— Unparalleled triumphs, but deeper humiliation, awaited the kingdom of Israel under the dynasty of Jehu. Hazael, the ablest king of Damascus, reduced Jehoahaz to the condition of a vassal, and triumphed for a time over both the disunited Hebrew kingdoms. Almost the first sign of the restoration of their strength was a war between them, and Jehoash, the grandson of Jehu, entered Jerusalem as the conqueror of Amaziah. Jehoash also turned the tide of war against the Syrians, and Jeroboam II., the most powerful of all the kings of Israel, captured Damascus and recovered the whole ancient frontier from Hamath to the Dead Sea. This short-lived greatness expired with the last king of Jehu's line. "(d.) b.c. 772-721.— Military violence, it would seem, broke off the hereditary succession after the obscure and probably convulsed reign of Zachariah. An unsuccessful usurper, Shallum, is followed by the cruel Menahem, who, being unable to make head against the first attack of Assyria under Pul, became the agent of that monarch for the oppressive taxation of his subjects. Yet his power at home was sufficient to ensure for his son and successor, Pekahiah, a ten years' reign, cut short by a bold usurper, Pekah. Abandoning the northern and trans-Jordanic regions to the encroaching power of Assyria under Tiglath-pileser, he was very near subjugating Judah, with the help of Damascus, now the coequal ally of Israel. But Assyria, interposing, summarily put an end to the independence of Damascus, and perhaps was the indirect cause of the assassination of the baffled Pekah. The irresolute Hoshea, the next and last usurper, became tributary to his invader, Shalmaneser, betrayed the Assyrian to the rival monarchy of Egypt, and was punished by the loss of his liberty and by the capture, after a three years' siege, of his strong capital, Samaria. Some gleanings of the ten tribes yet remained in the land after so many years of religious decline, moral debasement, national degradation, anarchy, bloodshed, and deportation. Even these were gathered up by the conqueror and carried to Assyria, never again, as a distinct people, to occupy their portion of that goodly and pleasant land which theirforefathers won under Joshua from the heathen." After the destruction of the kingdom of Israel, b.c. 721, the name "Israel" began again to be applied to the whole surviving people. "Israel" is sometimes put for the true Israelites, the faithful worthy of the name. Ps 73:1; Isa 45:17; Jer 49:3; John 1:47; Rom 9:6; Jud 11:26. See Judah.
entries.definition_ko: 솔로몬 사후 르호보암의 실정으로 열 지파가 여로보암 아래 분리하여 세운 왕국(주전 975-721)으로, 수도는 처음 세겜과 디르사, 후에 사마리아였다. 19명의 왕이 다스렸으나 단 한 왕조도 안정적이지 못했고, 여로보암의 금송아지 우상에서 시작된 배교가 계속되어 결국 앗수르에 의해 멸망하고 주민이 이주당했다(왕하 17:6).

entries.definition: IS'RAEL. Gen 35:10. The surname of Jacob, given to him by the angel at Peniel. Gen 32:28; Hos 12:3. It signifies "the prince that prevails with God." One of the finest hymns of Charles Wesley describes that mysterious wrestling with God in prayer, and begins, We find the name "Israel" soon after used for the whole race of Jacob's posterity, Ex 3:16; also for the kingdom of the ten tribes, as distinguished from Judah, 2 Kgs 14:12; and again, in a spiritual sense, for the whole body of true believers. Rom 9:6; Jud 11:26. Land of. See Canaan.
entries.definition_ko: 브니엘에서의 큰 기도 씨름 이후 야곱에게 주어진 이름(창세기 32:28)으로, '그가 왕자처럼 하나님과 겨루어 이겼다'는 뜻이다(야곱 항목 참조). 야곱의 후손 전체를 가리키는 통상적 이름이다.

entries.definition: IS'RAELITE, a member of Israel.
entries.definition_ko: '이스라엘의 후손'이라는 뜻이다. 사무엘하 17:25에서는 아마사의 아버지 이드라를 '이스라엘 사람'이라 부르나 역대상 2:17에서는 '이스마엘 사람 예델'로 나오는데 후자가 옳은 표기로 여겨진다.

entries.definition: IS'SACHAR (God hath given me my hire). The fifth son of Jacob and Leah. Gen 30:18. The prophetical description of him uttered by his father, Gen 49:14-15, was fulfilled in the fact that the posterity of Issachar were a laborious people and addicted to rural employments, and were subject to the tributes of marauding tribes. See Tribes. A Korhite Levite. 1 Chr 26:5.
entries.definition_ko: '삯 받은'이라는 뜻(창세기 30:18). '하나님이 내게 그 삯을 주셨다'고 레아가 말하며 '그 이름을 잇사갈이라 하였더라'. 야곱의 아홉째 아들로 밧단아람에서 태어났다.

entries.definition: ISSACHAR, THE TERRITORY OF, included the great plain of Esdraelon, or Jezreel, and lay above that of Manasseh; its boundaries are given in Josh 19:17-23. It extended from Mount Carmel to the Jordan, and from Mount Tabor to En-gannim. Zebulun was on the north, Manasseh on the south, and Gilead on the east, across the Jordan. It contained 16 noted cities and their villages. Among them were Megiddo, Jezreel, Shunem, Beth-shan, Endor, Aphek, Taanach; and Jezreel stood almost exactly in the centre of the territory. This region was one of the richest and most fertile in Palestine. Many historical events of great interest took place within the territory. It furnished two kings to Israel — Baasha and Eiah. 1 Kgs 15:27; 1 Kgs 16:6. Their portion of Palestine is still among the most fertile of the whole land. See Jezreel, Plain OF, and Palestine.
entries.definition_ko: 이스르엘, 곧 에스드라엘론 대평야를 포함하며 므낫세 위쪽에 자리했다. 그 경계는 수 19:17-23에 나온다. 갈멜산에서 요단까지, 다볼산에서 엔간님까지 뻗었다. 북쪽은 스불론, 남쪽은 므낫세, 동쪽은 요단 건너 길르앗이었다. 이름난 성읍 16곳과 그 마을들이 있었는데 므깃도, 이스르엘, 수넴, 벧산, 엔돌, 아벡, 다아낙 등이며 이스르엘이 거의 정중앙에 있었다. 팔레스타인에서 가장 부유하고 비옥한 지역 중 하나였다. 이스라엘에 바아사와 엘라 두 왕을 냈다(왕상 15:27, 16:6).

entries.definition: ISSHI'AH (whom Jehovah lends). A descendant of Moses, 1 Chr 24:21; called Jeshahiah 1 Chr 26:25. A Kohathite Levite. 1 Chr 24:25.
entries.definition_ko: 모세의 후손(대상 24:21), 고핫 자손 레위인(대상 24:25).

entries.definition: IS'UAH (quiet), second son of Asher. 1 Chr 7:30.
entries.definition_ko: '조용한'이라는 뜻으로 아셀의 둘째 아들이다(역대상 7:30).

entries.definition: IS'UI (quiet), third son of Asher. Gen 46:17.
entries.definition_ko: '조용한'이라는 뜻으로 아셀의 셋째 아들이며 그 이름을 딴 가문의 시조이다(창세기 46:17).

entries.definition: ITAL'IAN BAND, a cohort, composed of native Italians, stationed at Caesarea. Acts 10:1. Cornelius was their centurion.
entries.definition_ko: 고넬료가 속했던 로마 보병대의 이름(사도행전 10:1)으로, 아마도 이탈리아에서 모집된 사람들로 이루어졌기에 이렇게 불렸을 것이다.

entries.definition: IT'ALY, a well-known country in the south of Europe, and including the whole of the peninsula west of the Adriatic Sea. It has an area of about 100,000 square miles and a population of over 25,000,000. It is named in the N.T. only three times: (1) as the country from which Aquila and Priscilla were expelled. Acts 18:2; (2) Paul sailed for Italy, Acts 27:1; and (3) in the Epistle to the Hebrews some of that country joined in the salutations sent. Heb 13:24.
entries.definition_ko: (사도행전 18:2; 27:1,6; 히브리서 13:24) 대부분의 지리적 명칭처럼 역사의 시기마다 다르게 쓰였다. 로마의 세력이 커지면서 여러 민족이 차례로 정복되어 편입되었다.

entries.definition: ITH'AI (with Jehovah), a Benjamite, one of David's guard, 1 Chr 11:31; called Ittai 2 Sam 23:29.
entries.definition_ko: '주와 함께'라는 뜻으로 기브아 사람 리배의 아들, 베냐민 사람, 다윗의 근위 용사 중 하나이다(역대상 11:31).

entries.definition: ITH'AMAR (land of palms), a son of Aaron. Ex 6:23. After the violent death of Nadab and Abihu for their act of desecration. Lev 10:1-2, he and Eleazar were alone left for the priestly office. Lev 10:6, Eze 10:12. Eli was the only high priest of the line of Ithamar, 1 Chr 24:6, and, in fact, his house does not seem to have exercised as much influence as that of Eleazar. 1 Chr 24:4.
entries.definition_ko: '종려나무 섬'이라는 뜻으로, 아론의 넷째이자 막내아들(역대상 6:3). 형제들과 함께 제사장직에 구별되었고(출애굽기 6:23), 나답과 아비후가 죽은 뒤 엘르아살과 함께 그 직분을 수행했다.

entries.definition: ITH'IEL. (God is with me). A Benjamite. Neh 11:7. A friend of Agur. Prov 30:1.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 나와 함께 계신다'는 뜻. (1) 여사야의 아들, 베냐민 사람(느헤미야 11:7). (2) 아굴 벤야게가 잠언을 전한 두 사람(이디엘과 우갈) 중 하나(잠언 30:1).

entries.definition: ITH'MAH (orphanage), one of David's guard. 1 Chr 11:46.
entries.definition_ko: '상실'이라는 뜻으로 모압 사람, 다윗의 근위 용사 중 하나이다(역대상 11:46).

entries.definition: ITH'NAN (bestowed), one of the towns in the extreme south of Judah, on the borders of the desert. Josh 15:23. Wilton says it is identical with el-Hora, east of Beer-sheba; but this is only conjectural.
entries.definition_ko: '주어진'이라는 뜻으로 광야 경계에 있는 유다 최남단 성읍 중 하나다(수 15:23). 윌턴은 브엘세바 동쪽의 엘호라와 같은 곳이라 하나 추측일 뿐이다.

entries.definition: ITH'RA (abundance), David's brother-in-law. 2 Sam 17:25. See Jether.
entries.definition_ko: '탁월함'이라는 뜻으로 다윗의 누이 아비가일을 통해 아마사를 낳은 이스라엘 사람(또는 이스마엘 사람)이다(사무엘하 17:25).

entries.definition: ITH'RAN (abundance). A Horite. Gen 36:26; 1 Chr 1:41. An Asherite. 1 Chr 7:37.
entries.definition_ko: '탁월함'이라는 뜻. (1) 호리 사람 디손의 아들로 호리 족속의 족장으로 추정(창세기 36:26). (2) 아셀의 후손(역대상 7:30).

entries.definition: ITH'REAM (residue of the people), a son of David, born at Hebron. 2 Sam 3:5; 1 Chr 3:3.
entries.definition_ko: '백성의 풍성함'이라는 뜻으로 다윗이 헤브론에서 아내 에글라를 통해 낳은 여섯째 아들이다(사무엘하 3:5).

entries.definition: ITH'RITE, THE, the designation of two of David's warriors. 2 Sam 23:38; 1 Chr 11:40.
entries.definition_ko: 다윗의 용사 두 사람에게 붙은 칭호(삼하 23:38, 대상 11:40).

entries.definition: IT'TAH-KA'ZIN (time of the judge), one of the landmarks of Zebulun, Josh 19:13.
entries.definition_ko: '재판관의 때'라는 뜻으로 스불론 경계의 지표 중 하나이다(여호수아 19:13). 확인되지 않았다.

entries.definition: IT'TAI (in time). A native of Gath, and high in position in the army of David during the rebellion of Absalom. 2 Sam 18:2. He was sincerely attached to David. 2 Sam 15:19-22. He reminds us of the attachment of Ruth to Naomi, and his words of devotion, 2 Sam 15:21, are only inferior to hers, Ruth 1:16, for pathos. One of David's guard. 2 Sam 23:29.
entries.definition_ko: '가까운; 때맞은; 또는 주와 함께'라는 뜻. (1.) 베냐민 사람으로 다윗의 삼십 용사 중 하나(사무엘하 23:29). (2.) 가드 출신 블레셋 사람으로, 다윗이 유랑하던 시절 그의 무리 육백 용사를 지휘한 것으로 보인다(사무엘하 15장).

entries.definition: ITURAE'A (an enclosed region), a small province on the north-western border of Palestine, and at the southeastern base of Hermon, between Trachonitis and Galilee. It derived its name from "Jetur," a son of Ishmael. Gen 25:15; 1 Chr 1:31; 1 Chr 5:19. This district is now called Jedur, and is about 17 miles from north to south by 20 from east to west. The greater portion is a fine plain, with a rich and well-watered soil; the sub-stratum is black basalt. The district contains 38 villages, 10 of them entirely desolate; the others have a few peasant families living in wretchedness and amid ruins, Philip was "tetrarch of Ituraea and of the region of Trachonitis." Luke 3:1.
entries.definition_ko: '둘러싸인 지역'이라는 뜻으로 팔레스타인 북서쪽 경계, 헤르몬 남동쪽 기슭, 트라코니티스와 갈릴리 사이의 작은 속주다. 이스마엘의 아들 '여둘'에게서 이름이 왔다(창 25:15, 대상 1:31, 5:19). 이 지역은 지금 제두르라 불리며 남북 약 17마일, 동서 20마일이다. 대부분이 좋은 평야로 땅이 기름지고 물이 넉넉하며 기반암은 검은 현무암이다. 38개 마을이 있는데 그중 열은 완전히 황폐하고 나머지에는 몇몇 농가가 폐허 가운데 비참하게 산다. 빌립이 '이두래와 드라고닛 지방의 분봉왕'이었다(눅 3:1).

entries.definition: IV . He is the object of religious worship. Phil 2:10-11; Heb 1:6; Rev 5:11-13. We insert here, as a help in studying the harmony of the four Gospels, the chronological table of the life of Christ, from Schaff's Popular Commentary on the New Testament (New York, 1879), vol. i. p. 18. Outline of the Gospel History. The life of Christ has been of late studied with an eagerness, a keenness, and a wealth of illustration that argue well for the future. The question, "What think ye of Christ?" is asked to-day with peculiar emphasis. This new-born interest in the earthly life of the Founder of the Christian religion will bear fruit in the increased reverence of believers and the increased respect of his foes. Christs, False. Matt 24:24. Our Lord warned his disciples that false Christs should arise. Not less than 24 different persons of such pretensions have appeared, and the defence of their claims to the Messiahship has cost the Jews a great expense of life and treasure. One of them, Coziba, or Barchocheba, lived early in the second century. He put himself at the head of the Jewish nation as their Messiah; they adhered to him. The Romans made war upon him, and the Jews themselves allow that in their defence of this false Messiah they lost between 500,000 and 600,000 souls! In the twelfth century not less than 8 or 10 impostors appeared under the same name, and were followed by great numbers of the Jews. Most of them were punished for their imposture with death, and usually involved a multitude of their deluded followers in persecution and death. The last that gained any considerable number of converts was Mordecai, a Jew of Germany, who lived in 1682. He fled for his life, and his end is not known.
entries.definition_ko: IV. 그분은 종교적 예배의 대상이시다(빌 2:10-11, 히 1:6, 계 5:11-13). 또한 '거짓 그리스도'에 대해, 주님은 거짓 그리스도들이 일어나리라 제자들에게 경고하셨다(마 24:24). 그런 주장을 한 사람이 스물넷이 넘게 나타났다.

entries.definition: I'VAH, or A'VAH, an Assyrian or Babylonian city mentioned with Hena and Sepharvalm, 2 Kgs 18:34; 2 Kgs 19:13; comp. Isa 37:13, and with Babylon and Cutha, 2 Kgs 17:24. Rawlinson identified it with Hit, on the Euphrates.
entries.definition_ko: '뒤집음'이라는 뜻으로, 사마리아로 이주민을 보낸 앗수르의 성읍(열왕기하 18:34; 19:13). 스발와임과 헤나 사이 유프라테스강 변에 있었으며 일부는 에스라 8:15의 아하와와 같은 곳으로 본다.

entries.definition: I'VORY (tooth), the substance of the tusk of the elephant. From the meaning of the Hebrew word, it is seen that the Jews of Solomon's time understood that it was obtained from a tooth, not from a horn. That which is brought from Ceylon is regarded as most valuable. It was among the merchandise of Tyre, Eze 27:15, and Tarshish. 1 Kgs 10:22. Solomon's throne was built of it, 2 Chr 9:17, 2 Chr 9:21; and so lavishly was it used in various kinds of architecture and in cabinet-work as to justify the expressions found in Am 3:15; Am 6:4 and Eze 27:6. "Ivory palaces," Ps 45:8, probably refers to boxes richly wrought or inlaid with ivory, in which perfume was kept.
entries.definition_ko: (히브리어 복수형 '셴합빔', '코끼리의 엄니') 애굽인들이 일찍부터 장식에 사용했고 앗수르인들이 대규모로 교역했다(에스겔 27:6; 요한계시록 18:12). 페니키아인들은 이를 노 젓는 배의 목재 장식에 사용했다.

entries.definition: IZ'EHAR. Num 3:19. See Izhar.
entries.definition_ko: '기름'이라는 뜻으로 민수기 3:19에서만 이스할이 이 형태로 표기된다.

entries.definition: IZ'HAR (oil), a son of Kohath, and grandson of Levi. Ex 6:18, Ex 6:21; Num 3:19; Mark 16:1; 1 Chr 6:2, 1 Chr 6:18.
entries.definition_ko: '기름'이라는 뜻으로 고핫의 아들이자 레위의 손자다(출 6:18,21, 민 3:19, 대상 6:2,18).

entries.definition: IZ'HARITES, descendants of Izhar.
entries.definition_ko: 이스할의 후손을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: IZRAHI'AH (whom Jehovah causes to sparkle), a chieftain of Issachar. 1 Chr 7:3.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 빛나게 하시는 자'라는 뜻으로 잇사갈의 지도자이다(역대상 7:3).

entries.definition: IZ'RAHITE, THE, the designation of one of David's captains, 1 Chr 27:8; probably a Zahrite.
entries.definition_ko: 다윗의 지휘관 중 하나에게 붙은 칭호로(대상 27:8) 아마도 세라 사람일 것이다.

entries.definition: IZ'RI (built), a Levite, leader of the fourth course. 1 Chr 26:11.
entries.definition_ko: '창조자'라는 뜻으로 성전 봉사 넷째 반차의 레위인 지휘자이다(역대상 25:11). 3절에서는 세리로 불린다.

entries.definition: JA'AKAN (he shall adorn, or one sagacious), the son of Seir the Horite. Deut 10:6. See Bene-jaakan. The name is given as Jakan in 1 Chron 1:42.
entries.definition_ko: '그가 꾸밀 것이다' 또는 '지혜로운 자'라는 뜻으로 세일 사람 호리의 아들이다(신 10:6). 브네야아간 참조. 대상 1:42에서는 야간으로 나온다.

entries.definition: JAAK'OBAH (heel catcher, supplanter), a chieftain of Simeon. 1 Chr 4:36.
entries.definition_ko: '발꿈치를 잡는 자'라는 뜻으로, '야곱'이라는 이름의 한 형태이며 시므온의 후손 중 하나(역대상 4:36).

entries.definition: JAA'LA, JAA'LAH (a wild shegoat), one of the descendants of Solomon's slaves who returned with Zerubbabel from Babylon to Jerusalem. Ezr 2:56, Neh 7:58.
entries.definition_ko: 스룹바벨과 함께 바벨론에서 예루살렘으로 돌아온 솔로몬의 종의 후손 중 하나(스 2:56, 느 7:58).

entries.definition: JAA'LAM (whom God. hides), a son of Esau by his wife Aholibamah, and a chief of Edom. Gen 36:5, Gen 36:14, Gen 36:18; 1 Chr 1:35.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 숨기시는 자'라는 뜻으로 에서가 아내 오홀리바마에게서 얻은 아들이며 에돔의 족장이다(창 36:5,14,18, 대상 1:35).

entries.definition: JA'ANAI (whom Jehovah answers), a chief of Gad. 1 Chr 5:12.
entries.definition_ko: '애곡하는 자'라는 뜻으로, 갓 지파의 주요 인물 중 하나(역대상 5:12).

entries.definition: JAAR'E-OR'EGIM (forests of the weavers), the Bethlehemite whose son Elhanan slew the brother of Goliath. 2 Sam 21:19. In 1 Chr 20:5 he appears as Jair.
entries.definition_ko: '직조공들의 숲'이라는 뜻으로(사무엘하 21:19) 베들레헴 사람, 골리앗을 죽인 엘하난의 아버지이다. 병행 기사(역대상 20:5)에서는 야레 대신 야일로 나오고 오레김은 생략된다.

entries.definition: JA'ASAU (whom Jehovah has made), one mentioned, Ezr 10:37, as having a foreign wife.
entries.definition_ko: '만드는 자'라는 뜻으로, 포로 귀환 이후 이방인 아내를 버린 이스라엘 사람(에스라 10:37).

entries.definition: JAA'SIEL (whom God has made), the son of Abner, and chief of the tribe of Benjamin. 1 Chr 27:21.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 지으신 이'라는 뜻으로, 다윗의 호위병 중 하나이며 아브넬의 아들(역대상 27:21); 역대상 11:47에서는 야시엘이라 불린다.

entries.definition: JAAZANI'AH (whom Jehovah hears). A captain who joined Gedaliah at Mizpah, 2 Kgs 25:23, and who subsequently fought against Ishmael, and then later went to Egypt. Comp. Jer 41:11; Jer 43:2. The probable chief of the family of the Rechabites at the time of Jeremiah. Jer 35:3. One of the seventy elders seen by Ezekiel in his vision. Eze 8:11. A prince against whom Ezekiel was directed to prophesy. Eze 11:1.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 들으시는 자'라는 뜻. (1) 그다랴에게 경의를 표하러 미스바에 간 요하난 벤가레아와 함께한 부대장 중 하나(열왕기하 25:23). (2) 사반의 아들(에스겔 8:11). (3) 아술의 아들, 에스겔이 예언하도록 지시받은 백성의 지도자 중 하나(에스겔 11:1). (4) 레갑 사람, 예레미야의 아들(예레미야 35:3).

entries.definition: JAA'ZER, and JA'ZER (Jehovah helps), a city of Gilead, east of the Jordan, which was conquered and assigned to Gad and to the Levites. Num 21:32; Num 32:1; Josh 21:39. In the time of David it was held by Hebronites or Kohathites, 1 Chr 26:31, but in later times it was subject to Moab, and is often denounced in prophecies against that nation. Isa 16:8-9; Jer 48:32. It was situated at the massive ruins called Sar, about 4 hours (15 miles) north-east of Heshbon. Below the hill is a fountain with a stream which flows to the Jordan. Tristram found ancient terraces, probably vineyards, in illustration of Isa 16:9; Jer 48:32. There are mounds and rows of foundations at the head of the valley. In the A.V. the "Sea of Jazer" is referred to, Jer 48:32; but the passage may be rendered: "Thy shoots have overshot the sea, to Jazer have they reached;" the "sea" would then be the Salt or Dead Sea.
entries.definition_ko: 요단 동편 길르앗의 성읍으로 갓 지파와 레위인에게 배정되었다(민 21:32; 32:1). 후에는 모압에 속하게 되어 예언서에서 모압을 향한 심판의 대상으로 자주 언급되며(사 16:8-9; 렘 48:32), 헤스본 북동쪽 약 15마일 지점의 폐허와 동일시된다.

entries.definition: JAAZI'AH (whom Jehovah consoles), a Levite of the family of Merari. 1 Chr 24:26-27.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 위로하신다'는 뜻으로, 레위인 므라리의 후손(역대상 24:26,27).

entries.definition: JAA'ZIEL (whom God consoles), a Levite who played before the ark. 1 Chr 15:18. In 1 Chr 15:20 he is called Aziel.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 위로하시는 자'라는 뜻으로 궤 앞에서 연주한 레위인이다(대상 15:18). 대상 15:20에서는 아시엘이라 불린다.

entries.definition: JA'BAL (a stream), the son of Lamech, descendant of Cain; described as the "father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle." Gen 4:20.
entries.definition_ko: '시내'라는 뜻으로, 가인의 후손이며 유발의 형제; '장막에 거하며 가축 치는 자의 조상'(창세기 4:20). 이는 그가 유랑 생활을 했음을 나타낸다.

entries.definition: JAB'BOK (emptying), a stream rising about 25 miles east of the north end of the Dead Sea, and flowing east, then northward and westward, and finally south-west, into the Jordan about midway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea. It is now called the Zerka or "blue" river. It has a small branch flowing into it past Gerosh, but no branch from the north-east as indicated on most maps. Across this stream Jacob sent his family, and here his wrestling for a blessing occurred. Gen 32:22-24. The Israelites conquered the kingdoms of Og and Sihon, but not the Ammonite country nor the upper Jabbok, which explains Deut 2:37. Compare Num 21:24; Deut 3:16; Josh 12:2; Jud 11:13, Neh 11:22. The Jabbok before it enters the Jordan valley flows through a deep, narrow ravine, the hills being from 1600 to 2000 feet in height. They are covered with verdure and are very picturesque. The stream in most of its course is perennial, swollen, deep, and rapid in winter; it abounds in small fish of excellent flavor.
entries.definition_ko: '쏟아냄' 또는 '씨름'이라는 뜻으로, 요단강 동편의 시내 중 하나로 갈릴리 바다와 사해 중간쯤, 곧 갈릴리 바다에서 약 45마일 아래 지점에서 요단강에 합류한다. 길르앗 산지 동편에서 발원한다.

entries.definition: JA'BESH (dry), the father of Shallum, the fifteenth king of Israel. 2 Kgs 15:10, 2 Kgs 15:13-14.
entries.definition_ko: '마른'이라는 뜻. (1.) 야베스길르앗의 줄임(사무엘상 11:3,9,10). (2.) 살룸의 아버지(열왕기하 15:10,13,14)로, 스가랴가 죽자 이스라엘 왕위를 찬탈했다.

entries.definition: JA'BESH, and JA'BESH-GIL'EAD (dry Gilead), a city east of the Jordan; destroyed by the Israelites, Jud 21:8-14; delivered from Nahash by Saul, 1 Sam 11:1-11, and in gratitude therefor its people brought the bodies of Saul and his sons, which the Philistines hung upon the walls of Bethshan, to Jabesh, and caused them to be buried in a wood near by. 1 Sam 31:11-13. David blessed them, 2 Sam 2:4-6, but afterward removed the bones to Saul's ancestral burying-place. 2 Sam 2:4-6; 2 Sam 21:12-14. Robinson identifies it with ed-Deir, 23 miles south-east of the Sea of Galilee on the south side of Wady Yabis. Dr. S. Merrill, however, questions this as not conforming to the location assigned to it by Eusebius. He would identify Jabesh with the ruins of a town found about 7 miles from Pella, on the north side of Wady Yabis, on the mountain Jebel Aijlun, about 2300 feet above the Jordan valley. This seems to conform to the biblical statements concerning the place.
entries.definition_ko: 요단 동편의 성읍으로 이스라엘에 의해 멸망했다가(삿 21:8-14) 사울에 의해 나하스로부터 구원받았다. 이에 감사하여 주민들이 블레셋인들이 벧산 성벽에 걸어둔 사울과 아들들의 시신을 거두어 이곳에 장사했고(삼상 31:11-13), 다윗이 이들을 축복했다(삼하 2:4-6).

entries.definition:
JA'BEZ (he causes pain), the name of one whose prayer was answered. 1 Chr 4:9-10.

JA'BEZ (he causes pain), apparently a place; named only in 1 Chr 2:55, and doubtless named from Jabez of 1 Chr 4:9-10, though the Targumist regards it not as the name of a place, but of a person.
entries.definition_ko: 1) '그가 고통을 일으킨다'는 뜻으로 그 기도가 응답된 사람의 이름이다(대상 4:9-10). 2) 지명으로 보이며 대상 2:55에만 언급된다. 분명 대상 4:9-10의 야베스에게서 이름이 왔을 것이나, 탈굼 저자는 지명이 아니라 사람 이름으로 본다.

entries.definition: JA'BIIV (whom he-i.e. God-observes). King of Hazor, a northern district of Canaan. Josh 11:1. He attempted by a formidable alliance to oppose the progress of Joshua. He and his allies were utterly defeated in a battle at Merom, the city of Hazor was taken, and Jabin put to death. Another king of the same name and place, who had great wealth and power and oppressed the children of Israel for 20 years. Jud 4:2. His army was defeated by Deborah and Barak, and Sisera, his principal general, put to death.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 가나안 북부 지역 하솔의 왕이다(수 11:1). 막강한 동맹으로 여호수아의 진격을 막으려 했으나 메롬 전투에서 완전히 패했고, 하솔 성읍이 함락되어 야빈은 죽임을 당했다. 2) 같은 이름과 같은 곳의 또 다른 왕으로, 큰 부와 권세를 지니고 이스라엘 자손을 20년간 압제했다(삿 4:2). 그 군대는 드보라와 바락에게 패했고 군대 장관 시스라는 죽임을 당했다.

entries.definition: JAB'NEEL (Jehovah causes to be built). A town of Judah; called also Jabneh. Josh 15:11; 2 Chr 26:6. Uzziah captured it from the Philistines and destroyed its fortifications. It was noted during the wars of the Maccabees, and called by Josephus, Jamnia. It was a large and populous place, and after the destruction of Jerusalem was for some time the seat of a famous Jewish school of learning and of the Sanhedrin. It is identified with Yebnah, a considerable village about 3 miles from the Mediterranean and 12 miles south of Joppa. The Crusaders built a fortress here, of which the ruins still remain. A tomb is shown, reputed as the tomb of Gamaliel, a descendant of the noted Gamaliel who instructed Paul. There are the ruins of an ancient church. The port of Yebnah is naturally one of the best on the coast of Palestine below Csesarea, but there are dangerous reefs hidden beneath the waters. A place in Naphtali, Josh 19:33; called, in the Talmud, Caphar Yama. Conder identifies it with Yemma, 4 miles south-west of the Sea of Galilee.
entries.definition_ko: 유다의 성읍으로 얍네라고도 불린다(수 15:11; 대하 26:6). 웃시야가 블레셋에게서 빼앗아 요새를 헐었으며, 예루살렘 멸망 후 한동안 유명한 유대 학교와 산헤드린의 소재지였다.

entries.definition: JAB'NEH. See Jabneel.
entries.definition_ko: '건축'이라는 뜻(역대하 26:6)으로, 얍느엘과 같은 곳(여호수아 15:11).

entries.definition: JA'CHAN (affliction), a Gadite chief. 1 Chr 5:13.
entries.definition_ko: '애곡하는 자'라는 뜻으로, 바산에 있던 갓 지파 주요 '형제들' 중 하나(역대상 5:13).

entries.definition:
JA'CHIN (he shall establish). Fourth son of Simeon. Gen 46:10; Ex 6:15. Head of the twenty- first course of priests. 1 Chr 9:10; 1 Chr 24:17; Neh 11:10.

JA'CHIN (he shall establish) and BOAZ (lively) were the names of the two pillars Solomon set up. They were probably named after the givers. See Boaz.
entries.definition_ko: '견고한'이라는 뜻. (1.) 시므온의 넷째 아들(창세기 46:10)로 야립이라고도 불린다(역대상 4:24). (2.) 제사장 반열(스물한째)의 우두머리(역대상 24:17). (3.) 포로에서 돌아온 제사장 중 하나(역대상 9:10).

entries.definition: JA'CHINITES, THE, the descendants of Jachin, son of Simeon. Num 26:12.
entries.definition_ko: 시므온의 아들 야긴의 후손(민 26:12).

entries.definition: JACINTH, or HY'ACINTH, probably the same as the ligure, Ex 28:19, a gem of a yellowish-red or a dark-purple color, resembling the amethyst. Rev 9:17; Rev 21:20. In the former passage there is reference merely to its color.
entries.definition_ko: 정확히는 붉은빛 도는 청색 또는 짙은 자주색 꽃(히아신스)을 뜻하며, 따라서 그 색깔의 보석을 가리킨다(요한계시록 21:20). 출애굽기 28:19에 언급된 홍보석(히브리어 '레솀')과 같은 돌을 가리키는 것으로 추정되어 왔다.

entries.definition: JA'COB (heel-catcher, supplanter), the third of the Jewish patriarchs, the son of Isaac and Rebekah, and twin brother to Esau. He received his name from the circumstance which occurred at his birth. Gen 25:26. The family were then living at Lahai-roi. The twins greatly differed in tastes: Esau was a hunter, Jacob "a plain man, dwelling in tents." Gen 25:27. But though domestic, he was selfish and scheming. He bought the birthright from Esau, taking advantage of the latter's temporary weakness. Gen 25:29-34. When Isaac, fearing a sudden death, desired to bless Esau, whose manly character made him his favorite, while the more pliable Jacob was the favorite of Rebekah, Jacob was ready to fall in with his mother's plan, and, by deceiving his blind and aged father, to secure the elder brother's blessing. The event, so momentous to all parties, is related in detail in Gen 27. The hate of Esau, naturally aroused, compelled Jacob in fear to flee somewhere, and the anxiety of Rebekah lest Jacob should marry a daughter of Heth was the ostensible reason for turning his steps toward Padan-aram, where her brother Laban lived. Previous to his departure Isaac blessed him again, and thus with the assurance of divine favor, but with a heavy and fearful heart, did this man of at least 50 years (it is usual to call him 78 years old) turn his back upon his home and wearily go among strangers. But, though unworthy, he was the heir to the promises; and accordingly, God cared for him. At Bethel his eyes were opened to see a glorious vision and his ears to hear the voice of God. On awaking he made a vow to serve the Lord, giving the tenth, if the Lord on his part would protect and prosper him. Gen 28:20-22. An every-day incident introduced him to the family of Laban; an act of gallantry won him a home at once. Loving Rachel, he promised to serve Laban for her. But when the time was fulfilled, Laban, favored by the marriage-customs of the Orient, fraudulently married him to the elder daughter, Leah, but afterward to Rachel also. Jacob contrived an expedient whereby his flocks became larger and healthier than Laban's, and thus in the course of time the desire of his heart after the things of this life was gratified. He had "increased exceedingly, and had much cattle, and maidservants, and men-servants, and camels, and asses." Gen 30:43. Eleven sons and one daughter had been born to him by his two wives and their two servants, who were his concubines. But he yearned after his native land and determined to brave his brother's anger. Secretly, knowing Laban's feelings, he fled, but was followed and overtaken. A parley ensued. Jacob asserted his grievance: "I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle; and thou hast changed my wages ten times." A covenant of peace was made, of which a pillar was a reminder, Gen 31:45-54, and Laban left him with expressions of goodwill. Still dreading Esau, he sent messengers to him, and found Esau was approaching — he feared with hostile intentions. He prudently guarded against destruction by separating his company into two bands and by sending a handsome present to Esau. Fear acted like a slave to bring him to God. He prayed humbly, not to say cringingly, quoting the divine promises. After sending his family over the brook Jabbok, he tarried behind to see that nothing was forgotten, when there appeared "a man" who wrestled with him till the breaking of the day. The wrestling forms an extraordinary scene. Gen 32:24-32. God prevailed not against man. But when the day dawned the exhausted son of Isaac was no longer Jacob, but Israel; for though the sinew of his thigh shrank under the angel's touch, and though after this he was to know much sorrow, the all-night conflict had brought victory, so that the angel of the Lord could say, "As a prince hast thou power with God and with men; and hast prevailed." With the new name came the new nature. The man who met Esau was not Jacob, the supplanter, but Israel, the soldier of God. Behind him lay the guilty past; before him stretched the illimitable future, whose near part was full of trial, but whose far part was full of glory. Like many other awaited ills, the meeting with Esau was an agreeable disappointment. Esau was all kindness, and Jacob was compelled to refuse his friendly offers. After the brothers separated, Jacob finally settled near the city of Shechem, where he bought some land. Gen 33. In retaliation for the ravishment of Dinah by Shechem, the son of the prince of the country, by a stratagem the city was destroyed. See Dinah. The patriarch was therefore compelled to leave that part of the land. By divine direction he came to Bethel, where he paid the vow he had made so many years before, and here God again appeared unto him. On their way to Hebron, at Bethlehem, Benjamin was born, but Rachel, the beloved wife of Jacob, died. The memory of the event was ineffaceable. Gen 35:19. Shortly after his arrival, it would seem, Isaac died, and he and Esau buried him. Gen 35:29. The history now is taken up with Joseph, and Jacob does not play a prominent part until, lying upon his deathbed, he utters his prophetic blessing, tracing from the starting-point of individual character the fortunes of the tribes his twelve sons were destined to found. But the future was revealed to him only a little while before he belonged to the past for ever, for scarcely had he spoken out the pride, affection, apprehension, and warning of his fatherly heart than he "yielded up the ghost," aged 147 years, "and was gathered unto his people." Gen 49:33. He was buried with great pomp; his body was embalmed by the court-physicians and carried to Hebron, and there at last, after 147 years of wandering and trouble, Jacob rested with his ancestors in the cave of Machpelah. Gen 50:13. Jacob had more weaknesses and faults by nature than his father and grandfather, but his life was also more checkered and troubled, and his character purified by affliction, Abraham exemplifies heroic faith; Isaac, quiet humility; Jacob, patience and perseverance. His checkered life teaches us the lesson that through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of heaven. The terms "Jacob" and the "seed" or "children of Jacob" are often applied to the body of true believers generally. Deut 33:10: Ps 14:7; Ps 22:23; Ps 105:6; Ps 135:4; Isa 14:1; Isa 44:2; Mic 7:20.
entries.definition_ko: '남의 발꿈치를 따르는 자; 발뒤꿈치를 잡는 자'라는 뜻(창세기 25:26; 27:36; 호세아 12:2-4)으로, 이삭과 리브가 사이의 쌍둥이 아들 중 둘째. 아버지가 쉰아홉, 아브라함이 백쉰아홉일 때 아마도 라해로이에서 태어났다.

entries.definition: JA'COB'S WELL, the well at which Jesus sat and talked with the Samaritan woman, John 4:5-6, near Shechem; comp. Gen 33:19; Josh 24:32. Here our blessed Lord, weary of travel, but not of his work of saving love, offered to a poor woman the living water of eternal life and revealed to her the sublime truth of the true worship of God, who is a Spirit, in spirit and in truth. Here he sowed the seed for the harvest of the apostles. Acts 8. This is one of the few places in the Holy Land which can be identified with certainty. Christians, Jews, Mohammedans, Samaritans, all agree in regard to the site of Jacob's well. It is situated a mile and a half south-east of the town of Nablus, the ancient Shechem, at the eastern base of Mount Gerizim, near the edge of the plain of Moreh (Mukun), and close to the highway from Jerusalem to Galilee. The well is in an almost square enclosure, which measures 192 feet by 151 feet; the wall of this enclosure is almost Jacob's Well. entirely destroyed, and the ground is covered with shapeless ruins forming a large mound. The well is now 75 feet deep, 7 feet 6 inches in diameter, and the upper part lined with rough masonry. It must have been very much deeper in ancient times, for in the course of 10 years it decreased 10 feet in depth, and Robinson in 1838 found it 105 feet deep. Captain Anderson estimates that it has been filled up to probably more than half of its original depth by the stones thrown into it by visitors for the sake of hearing them strike, and by the debris from the ruined church built over the well during the fourth century. The bottom of the well is at times entirely dry, but in some seasons it contains water. Money has been contributed to the British Palestine Exploration Fund for the purpose of clearing out the well and preserving its sacred associations.
entries.definition_ko: (요한복음 4:5,6) 팔레스타인에서 논란이 없는 몇 안 되는 유적지 중 하나. 야곱이 하몰의 아들들에게서 사들인 '땅 한 뙈기'에 그가 직접 판 우물이기에 이 이름이 붙었다(창세기 33:19). 지금도 남아 있다.

entries.definition: JA'DA (knowing), a descendant of Judah. 1 Chr 2:28, 1 Chr 2:32.
entries.definition_ko: '지혜로운'이라는 뜻으로 오남의 아들이자 삼매의 형제, 여라므엘 족보에 속한다(역대상 2:28).

entries.definition: JADA'U (loving), one who had a foreign wife. Ezr 10:43.
entries.definition_ko: '사랑하는'이라는 뜻으로 이방인 아내를 취한 브네느보 가문 중 하나이다(에스라 10:43).

entries.definition: JADDU'A (known). One who sealed the covenant. Neh 10:21. The son of Jonathan, high priest of the Jews, who officiated a considerable time after the Captivity, and who is believed to be the same who lived in the time of Alexander the Great "by those who maintain that the list, Neh 12:11, of high priests from Joshua to Jaddua, or from b.c. 538-b.c. 336, cannot, in its present shape, have proceeded from Nehemiah's hand, or from that of a contemporary." -Bible (Speaker's) Commentary. He is the last of the high priests mentioned in the O.T.
entries.definition_ko: '알려진'이라는 뜻. 언약에 인친 사람(느 10:21), 그리고 요나단의 아들로 포로기 후 상당 기간 직무를 수행한 유대인 대제사장이 있다. 후자는 알렉산더 대왕 시대에 살았던 인물과 같다고 여겨지는데, 느 12:11의 예수아부터 얏두아까지(BC 538~336년) 대제사장 목록이 지금 형태로는 느헤미야나 동시대인의 손에서 나올 수 없다고 보는 이들이 그렇게 본다. 구약에 언급된 마지막 대제사장이다.

entries.definition: JA'DON (judge), one who helped build the wall of Jerusalem. Neh 3:7.
entries.definition_ko: '심판자'라는 뜻으로, 예루살렘 성벽 재건을 도운 므로놋 사람(느헤미야 3:7).

entries.definition: JA'EL (mountain-goat), the wife of Heber the Kenite. Jud 4:17. After the defeat of Jabin's army by Deborah and Barak, Sisera, the general, fled toward her tent, because Heber and Jabin were at peace. It was not unusual for the women to have a tent separate from the men, as in Sarah's case, Gen 24:67, and Leah's. Gen 31:33. This was a place of security, for then as now among the Arabs a stranger would not venture into the women's tent unasked. Jael invited him in, and concealed him. Fatigued and thirsty, he asked for water, and she gave him buttermilk, which greatly refreshed him. After instructing Jael to stand at the door of the tent, and to deny that he was within if any one should inquire for him, he fell into a sound sleep. She then took a tent-pin, and with a hammer drove it through his temples into the ground. Jud 4:21. Her act was treacherous, cowardly, and inhuman. It causes only a momentary perplexity, as we have no warrant for supposing her divinely commissioned. Hence, although Deborah appears to praise her in her song, Jud 5:24-27, she does not express any approval of the act upon moral grounds. Jael was a murderess from the Christian standpoint, and at best we can only justify her act by emphasizing the barbarity of her time and the usage of warfare, which is organized cruelty.
entries.definition_ko: 겐 사람 헤벨의 아내로, 드보라와 바락에게 패한 시스라 장군이 그녀의 장막으로 도망쳐 왔을 때 버터우유를 주고 재우다가 장막 말뚝으로 관자놀이를 뚫어 죽였다(삿 4:17-21). 드보라의 노래에서 칭송받으나(삿 5:24-27) 기독교적 관점에서는 배신적이고 잔인한 행위로 평가된다.

entries.definition: JA'GUR, a city on the south-eastern frontier of Judah, near Edom, Josh 15:21; perhaps to be associated with the following word. See Kinah.
entries.definition_ko: 에돔 근처, 유다 남동쪽 경계의 성읍이다(수 15:21). 어쩌면 다음 낱말과 연관될 수 있다. 기나 참조.

entries.definition: JAH. Ps 68:4. A contraction of the word "Jehovah," which imports the attribute of self-existence. It is part of the compound words "Adonijah" ("God is my Lord") and "Hallelujah" ("Praise the Lord"). See Jehovah.
entries.definition_ko: 시 68:4의 말이다. '여호와'의 축약형으로 스스로 계심의 속성을 담고 있다. '아도니야'('하나님은 나의 주')와 '할렐루야'('여호와를 찬양하라') 같은 합성어의 일부다.

entries.definition: JA'HATH (union). A descendant of Judah. 1 Chr 4:2. A Levite of the family of Gershom, and progenitor of Asaph. 1 Chr 6:20. A Levite, head of a branch of the same family. 1 Chr 23:10-11. A Levite of the Kohathites in the reign of David. 1 Chr 24:22. A Merarite Levite in the reign of Josiah, an overseer of the repairingwork in the temple. 2 Chr 34:12.
entries.definition_ko: '연합'이라는 뜻. (1.) 시므이의 아들이며 게르솜의 손자(역대상 23:10). (2.) 고핫 가문 슬로못의 아들 중 하나(역대상 24:22). (3.) 므라리 가문 레위인으로 성전 보수 감독관 중 하나.

entries.definition: JA'HAZ (place trodden down), a Moabitish city situated near the desert; afterward reckoned to the tribe of Reuben and assigned to the priests. Num 21:23; Deut 2:32; Isa 15:4; Jer 48:34. It is also called Jahaza, Josh 13:18, Jahazah, Josh 21:36; Jer 48:21, and Jahzah. 1 Chr 6:78. At this place the Israelites gained a victory over Sihon and conquered the territory between the Arnon and the Jabbok; but in later times Jahaz seems to have been occupied by the Moabites. Osborn locates Jahaz a mile south of the Arnon and 12 miles east of the Dead Sea.
entries.definition_ko: '짓밟힌'(야하사, 야하사라고도 불림)이라는 뜻으로, 시혼이 패배한 성읍으로 모압과 암몬 경계, 요단강 건너 아르논강 북쪽에 있었다(민수기 21:23; 신명기).

entries.definition: JAHAZA, JAHA'ZAH, JAH'ZAH. See Jahaz.
entries.definition_ko: 야하스 참조.

entries.definition: JAHAZI'AH (whom Jehovah beholds), one who helped Ezra in his marriage-reform. Ezr 10:15.
entries.definition_ko: 에스라의 혼인 개혁을 도운 사람(스 10:15).

entries.definition: JAHA'ZIEL (whom God beholds). A Benjamite chief who joined David at Ziklag. 1 Chr 12:4. A priest appointed by David to blow the trumpet before the ark. 1 Chr 16:6. A Kohathite Levite. 1 Chr 23:19; 1 Chr 24:23. A Levite of the sons of Asaph "inspired to encourage Jehoshaphat when marching against the Moabites and Ammonites." 2 Chr 20:14. The father of the chief of the sons of Shecaniah who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra. Ezr 8:5.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 보신'이라는 뜻. (1.) 헤브론의 셋째 아들(역대상 23:19). (2.) 시글락에서 다윗과 합류한 베냐민 지파 지도자(역대상 12:4). (3.) 궤를 예루살렘으로 옮길 때 동행한 제사장(역대상 16:6).

entries.definition: JAH'DAI (whom Jehovah directs), a name in the genealogies of Judah. 1 Chr 2:47.
entries.definition_ko: '붙잡는 자'라는 뜻으로, 헤스론 가문 갈렙의 후손(역대상 2:47).

entries.definition: JAH'DIEL (whom God makes joyful), the head of a family in the trans-Jordanic half-tribe of Manasseh. 1 Chr 5:24.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 기쁘게 하시는 자'라는 뜻으로 요단 동편 므낫세 지파 지도자였다(역대상 5:24).

entries.definition: JAH'DO (his union), a Gadite. 1 Chr 5:14.
entries.definition_ko: '연합된'이라는 뜻으로 갓 사람, 부스의 아들이자 여시새의 아버지이다(역대상 5:14).

entries.definition: JAH'LEEL (hoping in God), the youngest son of Zebulun, and founder of the Jahleelites. Gen 46:14; Num 26:26.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께 소망을 두는 자'라는 뜻으로 스불론의 세 아들 중 셋째이며 야흘르엘 자손의 조상이다(창세기 46:14).

entries.definition: JAHLEELITES, THE, descendants of Jahleel. Num 26:26.
entries.definition_ko: 야흘르엘의 후손(민 26:26).

entries.definition: JAH'MAI (whom Jehovah guards), a man of Issachar. 1 Chr 7:2.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 지키시는 자'라는 뜻으로 잇사갈 사람, 돌라 가문 지도자 중 하나이다(역대상 7:2).

entries.definition: JAH'ZEEL (whom God allots), the eldest son of Naphtali, and founder of the Jahzeelites. Gen 46:24; 1 Chr 7:13.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 나누어 주시는 자'라는 뜻으로 납달리의 맏아들이자 야스엘 족속의 조상이다(창 46:24, 대상 7:13).

entries.definition: JAHZEELITES, THE, descendants of Jahzeel. Num 26:48.
entries.definition_ko: 야스엘의 후손(민 26:48).

entries.definition: JAH'ZERAH (whom God leads back), a priest of the house of Immer, 1 Chr 9:12; called Ahasai in the duplicate passage in Neh 11:13.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 돌이키시는 자'라는 뜻으로 임멜 가문의 제사장이다(대상 9:12). 같은 내용의 느 11:13에서는 아흐새라 불린다.

entries.definition: JAH'ZIEL. 1 Chr 7:13. The same as Jahzeel, which see.
entries.definition_ko: 야스엘(JAHZEEL)과 동일하다(역대상 7:13).

entries.definition: JAI'LER. See Prison, Punishment.
entries.definition_ko: (빌립보의) 사도행전 16:23. 로마 간수의 회심은, '대체로 무감각하고 습관으로 굳어졌으며 복음의 메시지를 전하는 유대인들을 경멸하는 부류'에 속한 사람이 회심한 사례 중 하나다.

entries.definition: JA'IR (whom Jehovah enlightens). A chief warrior under Moses, descended from the most powerful family of Judah and Manasseh by his father and mother respectively. He took all the country of Argob (the modern Lejab) on the east side of Jordan, and, besides, some villages in Gilead, which he called Havoth-jair, "villages of Jair." 1 Chr 2:21-23; Num 32:41; Deut 3:14; comp. Josh 13:30. Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel 22 years. "He had thirty sons who rode on thirty ass-colts, and they had thirty cities, which are called Havothjair, which are in Gilead." Jud 10:3-5. A Benjamite, father of Mordeeai. Esth 2:5. In 1 Chr 20:5 in the A.V., Jair occurs, but it is a totally different name in Hebrew, meaning "whom God awakens." This Jair was the father of Elhanan, who killed Lachmi, the brother of Goliath. He is called Jaareoregim in 2 Sam 21:19.
entries.definition_ko: '빛을 비추는 자'라는 뜻. (1.) 스굽의 아들. 어머니와 함께 길르앗에서 자랐고 그곳에 소유지가 있었다(역대상 2:22). 바산을 향한 원정에서 두각을 나타내 길르앗 경계 아르곱 지역에 정착했다.

entries.definition: JA'IRTTE, THE, a descendant of Jair. 2 Sam 20:26.
entries.definition_ko: 야일의 후손(삼하 20:26).

entries.definition: JAI'RUS (whom Jehovah enlightens), an officer of the Jewish church who applied to Christ to restore to life his daughter, who was at the point of death when he left home. He evinced very strong faith. Christ with his disciples went to the ruler's house, and his daughter was restored. Mark 5:42.
entries.definition_ko: 가버나움 회당장으로, 그의 외동딸을 예수께서 살리셨다(마가복음 5:22; 누가복음 8:41). 베드로와 야고보와 요한, 그리고 소녀의 부모와 함께 죽음의 방으로 들어가 침상 앞으로 나아가셨다.

entries.definition: JA'KAN (sagacious), a son of Ezer the Horite; identical with Jaakan. 1 Chr 1:42.
entries.definition_ko: '현명한'이라는 뜻으로 호리 사람 에셀의 아들이다(역대상 1:42). 야아간(JAAKAN)과 동일하다.

entries.definition: JA'KEH (pious), the father of Agur, whose "words" are recorded in Prov 30.
entries.definition_ko: '경건한'이라는 뜻으로, 아굴의 아버지(잠언 30:1). 그에 대해 알려진 것은 없다.

entries.definition: JA'KIM (whom God sets up). A Benjamite. 1 Chr 8:19. Head of the twelfth course of the priests. 1 Chr 24:12.
entries.definition_ko: '세우는 자'라는 뜻. (1.) 열두째 제사장 반열의 우두머리(역대상 24:12). (2.) 베냐민 사람(역대상 8:19). (3.) 마태복음 1:11 난외주에서는 여호야김을 뜻한다.

entries.definition: JA'LON (abiding), a descendant of Judah. 1 Chr 4:17.
entries.definition_ko: '묵는 자'라는 뜻으로, 유다 지파 에스라의 네 아들 중 막내(역대상 4:17).

entries.definition: JAM'BRES. See Jannes and Jambres.
entries.definition_ko: 애굽에서 모세를 대적한 자 중 하나(디모데후서 3:8; 얀네 항목 참조).

entries.definition: JAMES (the same as "Jacob," the supplanter). James the Elder, one of the three favorite apostles, a son of Zebedee and Salome, and a brother of John the evangelist. With Peter and John, he was present at the raising of Jairus's daughter, the transfiguration, and the agony in Gethsemane. He was beheaded by order of King Herod Agrippa, and became the first martyr among the apostles, a.d. 44, thus fulfilling our Saviour's prediction concerning the baptism of blood. Matt 4:21; Matt 20:20-23; Ex 26:37; Mark 1:19-20; Mark 10:35; Acts 12:2. His apostolic labors seem not to have extended beyond Jerusalem and Judaea. Clement of Alexandria relates that the accuser of James on the way to the place of execution, stung by remorse, confessed faith and asked forgiveness; whereupon James said to him, "Peace be with thee!" gave him a brotherly kiss, and had him for a companion in martyrdom. His place was filled partly by James the brother of the Lord, partly by Paul. James the Less, or the Little, also one of the twelve apostles, a son of Alpheus and Mary. Mark 15:40; Mark 16:1; Matt 10:3; Matt 27:56; Acts 1:13. He labored, according to the tradition of the Greek Church (which distinguishes him from James, the brother of the Lord), in the south-western part of James the Less, or the Little, also one of the twelve apostles, a son of Alpheus and Mary. Mark 15:40; Mark 16:1; Matt 10:3; Matt 27:56; Acts 1:13. He labored, according to the tradition of the Greek Church (which distinguishes him from James, the brother of the Lord), in the south-western part of Palestine, afterward in Egypt, and was crucified in Lower Egypt. He is regarded by many as a cousin of Jesus. James, "the brother of the Lord," Gal 1:19; comp. Matt 13:55; Mark 6:3, or simply James, Acts 12:17; Acts 15:13; Gen 21:18; Gal 2:9; 1 Cor 15:7. By ecclesiastical writers he is also called James "the Just" and "the bishop of Jerusalem." Commentators are divided as to his relation to James the Less. Some identify him with the younger apostle of that name, and regard him simply as a cousin of Jesus, while others distinguish the two, and understand the designation "brother of the Lord" in the strict sense either of a uterine brother or a half-brother of Jesus. See Brother and Brethren of Jesus. It is certain, from the Acts of the Apostles, that this James, after the dispersion of the disciples and the departure of Peter, Acts 12:17, occupied the most prominent position in the church of Jerusalem, and stood at the head of the Jewish converts. He presided at the apostolic council, and proposed the compromise which prevented a split between the Jewish and the Gentile sections of the church. Acts 15 and Gal 2. He stood mediating between the old and the new dispensations, and conformed very nearly to the Jewish traditions and temple-service as long as there was any hope of a national conversion. He stood in high repute even among the Jews, but nevertheless was (according to Josephus) sentenced to be stoned by the Sanhedrin, a.d. 62. Hegesippus, an historian of the second century, puts his martyrdom later, A.D. 69, shortly before the destruction of Jerusalem, and adds that he was thrown by the Pharisees from the pinnacle of the temple, and then despatched with a fuller's club while on his knees, in the act of praying for his murderers. Epistle of James, "a servant (not an apostle) of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ," the same who is also called "the brother of the Lord." It is one of the catholic or general Epistles, and consists of five chapters. The design of the Epistle is, (1) To correct errors into which the Jewish Christians had fallen, especially relating to justification by faith; (2) To animate their hope, and strengthen their faith, in view of afflictions felt and feared; and (3) To excite the unbelieving Jews to repentance toward God and faith in the rejected Messiah. It is remarkable that the name of our blessed Lord occurs but twice in this Epistle, but with great reverence as the divine Master, Jas 1:1, and as "the Lord of glory." Ruth 2:1. The gospel is described as the perfect law of freedom. The Epistle strongly resembles the preaching of John the Baptist and the Sermon on the Mount. The main stress is laid on works rather than faith. It enforces an eminently practical Christianity which manifests itself in good fruits. Its doctrine of justification, ch. Jas 2, apparently conflicts with that of Paul, Rom 3-4, but in reality the two apostles supplement each other, and guard each other against abuse and excess. James opposes a dead orthodoxy, an unfruitful theoretical belief, and insists on practical demonstration of faith, while Paul, in opposition to Pharisaical legalism and self-righteousness, exhibits a living faith in Christ as the principle and root of all good works. The one judges the tree by its fruit, the other proceeds from the root. The Epistle of James was written before a.d. 62, perhaps much earlier, probably from Jerusalem, the scene of his labors, and is addressed to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, Jas 1:1 -that is, either to all the Jews of the Dispersion, or only to the Jewish Christians, as to the true spiritual Israel. The style is lively, vigorous, and impressive. What kindling words on patience in suffering, joy in sorrow, heavenly wisdom, the power of prayer as the most certain unfailing thing, from deep personal experience! There is a resemblance between the Epistle and the pastoral letter of the Council of Jerusalem, which was no doubt written by the same James as the presiding officer; both have the Greek form of "greeting," Acts 15:23; Jas 1:1, which otherwise does not occur in the N.T. or is changed into "grace and peace." This is an incidental proof of the genuineness of the Epistle. The theory recently advocated by Bassett (Commentary on fhe Catholic Epistle of St. James, London, 1876), that it was written by the elder James, the son of Zebedee, before a.d. 44, has little to support it. He assumes that the Epistle was addressed to all the Jews of the dispersion with the view to convert them by a moral rather than doctrinal exhibition of Christianity.
entries.definition_ko: (1) 세배대와 살로메의 아들, 요한의 형제로 '큰 야고보'라 불린다. 베드로·요한과 함께 변화산과 겟세마네에 참석했으며, 헤롯 아그립바에게 참수당해 사도 중 첫 순교자가 되었다(행 12:2). (2) 알패오의 아들 '작은 야고보'(막 15:40). (3) 주의 형제 야고보로 예루살렘 교회의 지도자가 되어 야고보서를 썼으며(약 1:1), 주후 62년경 순교했다.

entries.definition: JA'MIN (prosperity, right hand). The second son of Simeon, founder of the Jaminites. Gen 46:10; Ex 6:15; 1 Chr 4:24; Num 26:12. A man of Judah. 1 Chr 2:27. A Levite who expounded the Law with Ezra. Neh 8:7.
entries.definition_ko: '오른손'이라는 뜻. (1) 시므온의 둘째 아들, 야민 자손의 조상(창세기 46:10). (2) 여라므엘 사람 람의 둘째 아들, 유다 사람(역대상 2:27). (3) 백성에게 율법을 해설한 레위인 중 하나(느헤미야 8:7).

entries.definition: JA'MINITES, THE, descendants of Jamin. Num 26:12.
entries.definition_ko: 야민의 후손(민 26:12).

entries.definition: JAM'LECH (whom God makes king), a chief of Simeon. 1 Chr 4:34.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 왕이 되게 하신 자'라는 뜻으로 시므온 지파 지도자 중 하나이다(역대상 4:34).

entries.definition: JANG'LING means "babbling" in 1 Tim 1:6.
entries.definition_ko: 딤전 1:6에서 '헛된 말'이라는 뜻이다.

entries.definition: JAN'NA (whom Jehovah bestows), one of our Lord's ancestors. Luke 3:24.
entries.definition_ko: '번성하는'이라는 뜻으로 요셉의 아들이자 멜기의 아버지, 그리스도의 족보에 나온다(누가복음 3:24). 개정역에서는 얀나이로 표기된다.

entries.definition: JAN'NES and JAM'BRES, two famous magicians of Egypt, who are supposed to have used their art to deceive Pharaoh. 2 Tim 3:8; Ex 7:9-13.
entries.definition_ko: '얀네와 얌브레'는 애굽의 이름난 술객 둘로, 그 재주로 바로를 속인 것으로 여겨진다(딤후 3:8, 출 7:9-13).

entries.definition: JANO'AH (rest), a town of Naphtali, in northern Palestine, taken by the king of Assyria. 2 Kgs 15:29. Van de Velde and Porter propose to identify it with ruins at the village Hunis, between Abel-beth-Maachah and Kedesh; Conder with Yanuk, near the western limit of the ancient territory of Naphtali.
entries.definition_ko: 또는 야노아, '쉼'이라는 뜻. (1.) 요단 골짜기, 에브라임 북동쪽 경계의 성읍(여호수아 16:6,7). 나블루스 남동쪽 8마일의 오늘날 야눈과 동일시된다. (2.) 납달리 경계 안, 팔레스타인 북부의 성읍.

entries.definition: JANO'HAH (rest), a town on the north-east borders of Ephraim. Josh 16:6-7. At Yanus, about 8 miles south-east of Nablus, are extensive ruins, entire houses and walls, covered with immense heaps of earth, and these are identified as the site of Janohah.
entries.definition_ko: '쉼'이라는 뜻으로 에브라임 경계의 한 장소이며(여호수아 16:6) 나블루스에서 남동쪽 약 12마일, 아크라베에서 2마일 거리의 마을 야눈과 동일시된다.

entries.definition: JA'NUM (slumber), a place in the tribe of Judah. Josh 15:53. The margin has "Janus" ("flight"). It was not far from Hebron, and Conder proposes to identify it with Beni Naim.
entries.definition_ko: '잠'이라는 뜻으로 유다 지파의 한 곳이다(수 15:53). 난외주는 '야누스'('도망')로 되어 있다. 헤브론에서 멀지 않았고 콘더는 베니 나임과 동일시하려 한다.

entries.definition: JA'PHETH (enlargement), the second son of Noah. Gen 5:32; Gen 10:21. The prophetic blessing pronounced on Japheth by his father, Gen 9:27, was accomplished to the full extent of the promise. From him have come, (1) Gomer, or the Cymri or Celts; (2) Magog, or the Scythians and Sarmatians (Slavonians); (3) Madai, or the Medes or Aryans; (4) Javan, or the Greeks; (5) Tubal, or the Tibareni; (6) Meshech, or the Moschi; (7) Tiras, or the Teutons. The Japhetic races have occupied "'the isles of the Gentiles' — i. e. all the coastlands in Europe and Asia Minor and islands of the Mediterranean — whence they spread northward over Europe and much of Asia, from India and Persia in the east to the extreme west of Europe, and now to America and Australia." — Fausset: Englishman's Bible Cyclopaedia. The other branch of prophecy, "he (God) shall dwell in the tents of Shem," was fulfilled when the divine Presence was manifested in the tabernacle and temple; or if we read, "he (Japheth) shall dwell in the tents of Shem," it was fulfilled literally when the Greeks and Romans (descended from Japheth) subdued Judaea, the inheritance of Shem, and figuratively when the descendants of Japheth (the Gentiles) received the gospel, which the Jews, who were of the seed of Shem, rejected.
entries.definition_ko: '널리 퍼짐'이라는 뜻: '하나님이 야벳을 창대하게 하시고'(창세기 9:27). 노아의 아들 중 하나로 마지막 순서로 언급된다(창세기 5:32; 6:10; 7:13).

entries.definition:
JAPHI'A (splendid), the king of Lachish, one of the five kings of the Amorites who united against Joshua, but were defeated at Beth-horon and killed at Makkedah. Josh 10:3.

JAPHI'A (splendid), a place in the tribe of Zebulun. Josh 19:12. It is identified with a small village, called Yafa, a short distance south-west of Nazareth. See Josephus: Wars, 2:20, 6. Drake described some caves at this place unlike any other he had seen in Palestine. A passage 12 feet long leads into a circular chamber, in the floor of which are circular "man-holes" leading to two lower caves, which in turn lead to others. All the chambers are connected by intricate passage-ways. Mr. Drake conceives that they were not tombs, but places for the storage of grain.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 라기스 왕으로, 여호수아에 맞서 연합한 아모리 다섯 왕 중 하나다. 벧호론에서 패하고 막게다에서 죽임을 당했다(수 10:3). 2) 스불론 지파의 한 지명(수 19:12). 나사렛 남서쪽 조금 떨어진 야파라는 작은 마을로 확인된다. 드레이크는 이곳에서 팔레스타인 어디서도 본 적 없는 굴들을 묘사했는데, 12피트 길이의 통로가 둥근 방으로 이어지고 그 바닥의 둥근 구멍으로 아래 굴 둘로 내려가며 그것이 다시 다른 굴로 이어진다. 드레이크는 이것이 무덤이 아니라 곡식 저장고였다고 본다.

entries.definition: JAPH'LET (whom God delivers), an Asherite. 1 Chr 7:32-33.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 구원하시는 자'라는 뜻으로 브리아를 통한 아셀의 후손이다(역대상 7:32).

entries.definition: JAPH'LETI, a landmark of Ephraim west of Beth-horon. Josh 16:3.
entries.definition_ko: 벧호론 서쪽 에브라임의 경계 표지(수 16:3).

entries.definition: JA'PHO. Josh 19:46. See Joppa.
entries.definition_ko: '아름다움'이라는 뜻으로, 단 지파의 항구(여호수아 19:46); 욥바라고도 불린다(역대하 2:16; 에스라 3:7; 요나 1:3; 신약).

entries.definition: JA'RAH (honey), a descendant of Saul, 1 Chr 9:42; called in the parallel list, 1 Chr 8:36, Jehoadah.
entries.definition_ko: '꿀'이라는 뜻으로 사울의 후손, 미가의 아들이자 므비보셋의 증손이다(역대상 9:42).

entries.definition: JA'REB (an adversary). The marginal reading would indicate that it was the name of a place, but that is forbidden by the form of the original word. Hos 5:13; Neh 10:6. Some make it the name of a king, but it is better to translate it "the hostile king" — i.e. "the king of Assyria."
entries.definition_ko: '대적자'라는 뜻으로 나라 또는 인물의 고유명사, 동격 명사, 혹은 '다투다'를 뜻하는 어근에서 온 동사로 다양하게 해석된다(호세아 5:13). 아마도 아시리아의 한 도시 이름이거나 그 나라 자체의 또 다른 이름으로 추정된다.

entries.definition: JA'RED (descent), the father of Enoch. Gen 5:15-20; Luke 3:37. In 1 Chr 1:2 he is called Jered.
entries.definition_ko: '후손'이라는 뜻. (1.) 셋으로부터 넷째 홍수 이전 족장(창세기 5:15-20; 누가복음 3:37)으로 에녹의 아버지; 역대상 1:2에서는 예렛이라 불린다. (2.) 아마도 에스라의 아들(역대상 4:18).

entries.definition: JARESI'AH (whom Jehovah fattens), a Benjamite chief. 1 Chr 8:27.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 기르시는 자'라는 뜻으로 베냐민 사람, 브네여호람 가문이다(역대상 8:27).

entries.definition: JAR'HA (meaning uncertain), an Egyptian servant of Sheshan, and married to his daughter, 1 Chr 2:34-35.
entries.definition_ko: 엘리 시대 무렵 세산의 이집트인 종으로 주인이 그에게 딸이자 상속녀를 아내로 주었다(역대상 2:34).

entries.definition: JA'RIB (an adversary). A son of Simeon, 1 Chr 4:24; called Jachin in Gen 46:10. A companion of Ezra, "a chief man." Ezr 8:16. A priest married to a foreign wife. Ezr 10:18.
entries.definition_ko: '대적자'라는 뜻. (1.) 시므온의 아들(역대상 4:24). (2.) 에스라가 제사장들을 예루살렘으로 데려오도록 보낸 지도자 중 하나(에스라 8:16). (3.) 에스라 10:18.

entries.definition: JAR'MUTH. 1. A town in the low country of Judah. Josh 15:35. Its king, Piram, was one of the five who conspired to punish Gibeon for having made alliance with Israel, and who were defeated at Beth-horon and were hanged by Joshua at Makkedah. Josh 12:11; Josh 15:35. It was peopled after the Captivity. Neh 11:29. It is identified with Yarmak, 16 miles south-west of Jerusalem, on the crest of a rocky ridge, where hewn blocks of stone and other ruins of a town are found. A city of Issachar, allotted with its suburbs to the Gershonite Levites, Josh 21:29, and called Reneth and Ramoth. Josh 19:21; 1 Chr 6:73. Conder proposes to identify it with Rameh.
entries.definition_ko: 1) 유다 저지대의 성읍이다(수 15:35). 그 왕 비람은 기브온이 이스라엘과 화친했다 하여 벌하려 모의한 다섯 왕 중 하나로, 벧호론에서 패해 여호수아에게 막게다에서 매달렸다(수 10:3-27, 12:11). 포로기 이후 사람이 살았다(느 11:29). 예루살렘 남서쪽 16마일, 바위 능선 마루의 야르무크로 확인되며 다듬은 돌덩이와 성읍의 다른 유적이 발견된다. 2) 잇사갈의 성읍으로 그 들과 함께 게르손 자손 레위인에게 배정되었고(수 21:29) 라뭇이라고도 불린다(수 19:21, 대상 6:73).

entries.definition: JARO'AH (moon), a Gadite. 1 Chr 5:14.
entries.definition_ko: '달'이라는 뜻으로 갓 지파 지도자였다(역대상 5:14).

entries.definition: JA'SHEN (sleeping), the father of some of David's warriors, 2 Sam 23:32.
entries.definition_ko: '잠자는'이라는 뜻으로, 하솀이라고도 불림(역대상 11:34); 그의 여러 아들이 다윗의 호위병이었다(사무엘하 23:32).

entries.definition: JA'SHER, BOOK OF (upright). Twice referred to. Josh 10:13; 2 Sam 1:18; probably a collection of national songs, now lost.
entries.definition_ko: 두 번 언급된다(수 10:13, 삼하 1:18). 아마도 민족의 노래를 모은 책이었을 것이나 지금은 전해지지 않는다.

entries.definition: JASHO'BEAM (to whom the people turns), the chief of David's captains, who came to him at Ziklag and distinguished himself and his band by slaying 300 men at one time. 1 Chr 11:11; 1 Chr 12:6; 1 Chr 27:2. He is the same with Adino the Ezmite, 2 Sam 23:8, the difference in the Hebrew being slight.
entries.definition_ko: '백성 가운데 거하는 자; 또는 백성이 의지하는 자'라는 뜻으로, 학몬 사람(역대상 11:11)이며 시글락에서 다윗과 합류한 주요 용사 중 하나(12:6). 블레셋 진영을 뚫고 다윗을 위해 물을 길어 온 세 사람 중 첫째였다.

entries.definition: JASHTIBITES, THE, descendants of Jashub, 1. Num 26:24.
JASH'UB (he turns). One of the sons of Issachar; founder of the Jashubites. Num 26:24; 1 Chr 7:1; called Job in Gen 46:13. One who had a foreign wife. Ezr 10:29.
entries.definition_ko: '그가 돌이킨다'는 뜻. 잇사갈의 아들 중 하나이자 야숩 족속의 조상으로(민 26:24, 대상 7:1) 창 46:13에서는 욥이라 불린다. 또한 이방 여인을 아내로 둔 사람이다(스 10:29).

entries.definition: JASHUBILE'HEM (turner back for food), either a person or a place mentioned in the genealogical list of Judah. 1 Chr 4:22.
entries.definition_ko: '양식을 위해 돌아오는 자'라는 뜻으로 유다가 가나안 여인 밧수아를 통해 낳은 셀라의 후손 목록에 나오는 인물 또는 지명이다(역대상 4:22).

entries.definition: JA'SIEL (whom God has made), one of David's warriors, 1 Chr 11:47; same as Jaasiel.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 만드신 자'라는 뜻으로 다윗의 용사 목록 마지막에 나온다(역대상 11:47).

entries.definition: JA'SON (one who will heal), a Thessalonian, and probably a relative of Paul, whom he entertained, and in consequence received rough treatment at the hands of the unbelieving Jews. Acts 17; cf. Rom 9:3; Deut 16:21.
entries.definition_ko: '고칠 자'라는 뜻으로, 데살로니가에서 바울과 실라를 대접한 사람. 유대인들이 바울을 붙잡으려고 그의 집을 습격했으나 찾지 못하자 야손을 성의 관리들 앞으로 끌고 갔다(사도행전 17:5-9).

entries.definition: JAS'PER, the last stone in the breastplate of the high priest, and the first in the foundations of the new Jerusalem. Ex 28:20; Rev 21:19. Jasper is an opaque species of quartz, of different colors, often banded or spotted, and susceptible of a high polish. The darkgreen kind is supposed to be the variety of the Bible. From the apparent inconsistency of Rev 4:3; Rev 21:11 with the opaque character of this stone, it has been suggested that some transparent gem was denoted by jasper in the N.T. — perhaps the diamond or the translucent chalcedony. See Stones, Precious.
entries.definition_ko: 대제사장 흉패의 마지막 돌이자 새 예루살렘 기초의 첫 돌이다(출 28:20, 계 21:19). 벽옥은 여러 색을 띠는 불투명한 석영의 일종으로 흔히 띠나 반점이 있고 광을 잘 낼 수 있다. 짙은 녹색 종이 성경의 것으로 여겨진다. 계 4:3과 21:11이 이 돌의 불투명한 성질과 맞지 않아 보이므로, 신약의 벽옥은 어떤 투명한 보석 — 어쩌면 다이아몬드나 반투명한 옥수 — 을 가리킨다는 견해가 제기되었다.

entries.definition: JATH'NIEL (whom God bestows),a Levite porter or doorkeeper in the tabernacle. 1 Chr 26:2.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 주시는 자'라는 뜻으로 고라 가문 레위인, 므셀레먀 가문의 넷째이다(역대상 26:2).

entries.definition: JAT'TIR, a town of Judah in the mountain-districts, Josh 15:48; 2 Sam 21:14; David sent presents thither. 1 Sam 30:27; 1 Chr 6:57. Robinson identifies it with 'Attir, 6 miles north of Molada and 11 miles west of south of Hebron. Tristram noted there over 30 crypts, and found remains of terraces, many old wells, now dry and filled with rubbish, but only one modern building, a Moslem tomb.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 산지의 성읍으로(수 15:48, 21:14) 다윗이 예물을 보냈다(삼상 30:27, 대상 6:57). 로빈슨은 몰라다 북쪽 6마일, 헤브론 서남서 11마일의 아티르와 동일시한다. 트리스트람은 거기서 서른 개가 넘는 지하실을 확인했고 계단식 밭의 흔적과 지금은 말라 잡동사니로 찬 옛 우물을 여럿 찾았으나, 근대 건물은 이슬람 무덤 하나뿐이었다.

entries.definition: JA'VAN. In Isa 66:19 it is coupled with Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, and with Tubal and the "isles afar off;" again, in Eze 27:13, it is joined with Tubal and Meshech, as carrying on commerce with the Tyrians, who imported from these countries slaves and brazen vessels; in Dan 8:21; Num 10:20; Matt 11:2, in reference to the Macedonian empire; and in Zech 9:13, in reference to the Graeco-Syrian empire. From these passages it appears that "Javan" was regarded as a title for the Greek people and the Grecian empire. A town in the southern part of Arabia (Yemen), whither the Phoenicians traded, Eze 27:19; probably Uzal, a name of the capital of Yema, in Arabia, and famous for the manufacture of swordblades.
entries.definition_ko: 사 66:19에서 다시스, 불, 룻과 함께, 또 두발과 '먼 섬들'과 함께 언급된다. 겔 27:13에서는 두발, 메섹과 함께 두로 사람과 교역해 노예와 놋그릇을 수출한 나라로 나온다. 단 8:21, 10:20, 11:2에서는 마게도냐 제국을, 슥 9:13에서는 헬라-시리아 제국을 가리킨다. 이 구절들로 보아 '야완'은 헬라 민족과 헬라 제국을 가리키는 이름으로 여겨졌음을 알 수 있다. 또한 베니게인이 교역한 아라비아 남부(예멘)의 한 성읍 이름이기도 하며(겔 27:19), 아마도 예멘 수도의 이름 우살로 칼날 제조로 유명했다.

entries.definition: JA'VAN, the fourth son of Japheth, and the ancestor of the Grecians or lonians. Gen 10:2; 1 Chr 1:5, 1 Chr 1:7. Hence the word "Javan" in the O.T. denotes Greece, or the Greeks. Isa 66:19; Eze 27:13.
entries.definition_ko: (1.) 야벳의 넷째 '아들'(창세기 10:2)로, 그 후손이 그리스, 곧 히브리어로 '야완'이라 불리는 이오니아에 정착했다. 알렉산더 대왕은 '야완의 왕'이라 불린다(다니엘 8:21).

entries.definition: JAV'ELIN. See Arms.
entries.definition_ko: (1.) 히브리어 '하니트', 그 유연함에서 유래한 창(사무엘상 18:10,11; 19:9,10). (2.) 히브리어 '로마', 중무장 부대용 창으로 찌르는 데서 이름이 유래했다(민수기 25:7; 무기 항목 참조).

entries.definition: JA'ZER, Josh 21:39, or JAA'ZER, Num 21:32, a city of the Ammonites, near the river Jabbok, the ruins of which are still visible at Sar, about 15 miles from Hesban. Sea of, Jer 48:32, may be a lake existing in ancient times near the city of Jazer. There are round pools of water near Sar, but scholars have not agreed what the Sea of Jazer refers to.
entries.definition_ko: 얍복 강 근처 암몬 사람의 성읍으로(수 21:39, 민 21:32) 그 폐허가 헤스반에서 15마일쯤 떨어진 사르에 아직 보인다. '야셀 바다'(렘 48:32)는 옛날 야셀 성읍 근처에 있던 호수일 수 있다. 사르 근처에 둥근 못들이 있으나 야셀 바다가 무엇을 가리키는지에 대해 학자들의 견해가 일치하지 않는다.

entries.definition: JA'ZIZ (whom God moves), the Hagerite who was over David's flocks. 1 Chr 27:31.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님이 움직이시는 자'라는 뜻으로 하갈 사람, 다윗 왕의 양떼를 관리했다(역대상 27:31).

entries.definition: JEAL'OUSY. It is most frequently used to denote a suspicion of conjugal infidelity. 2 Cor 11:2. It is sometimes used for anger or indignation, Ps 79:5; 1 Cor 10:22, or an intense interest for the honor and prosperity of another. Zech 1:14; Zech 8:2. The same term, in a similar sense, is used in speaking of God, for he is represented as a husband, related to his Church by a marriage-covenant that binds her to be wholly for him, and not for another. The more sincere and constant the love, the more sensitive is the heart to the approach of a rival; and the thought of such affection being alienated or corrupted fills the soul with grief and indignation. So God commends the purity, the fervency, and the sincerity of his love to his Church by the most terrific expressions of jealousy. The various significations of the word "jealousy" are denoted usually by its connection. It is one of the strongest passions of our nature. Prov 6:34; Song 8:6. The Image of Jealousy, Eze 8:3, Song of Solomon 8:5, is the same with Tammuz, in Am 8:14. See Tammuz. Jealousy-offering, or Waters of Jealousy. See Adultery.
entries.definition_ko: 주로 배우자의 부정에 대한 의심을 가리키나(고후 11:2), 분노나 다른 이의 명예를 향한 강한 관심을 뜻하기도 한다(슥 1:14). 하나님도 자기 백성을 향한 언약적 사랑의 순전함을 이 표현으로 나타내신다.

entries.definition: JE'ARIM, MOUNT (mount of forests), a place named in noting the northern boundary of Judah. Josh 15:10. The boundary ran from Mount Seir to "the shoulder of Mount Jearim, which is Chesnlon" — that is, Chesalon was the landmark on the mountain. Keslu stands 7 miles due west of Jerusalem, on a high point on the north slope of a lofty ridge, which is probably Mount Jearim. Considerable woods still exist there.
entries.definition_ko: '수풀의 산'이라는 뜻으로 유다 북쪽 경계를 표시하는 데 나오는 곳이다(수 15:10). 경계가 세일산에서 '여아림 산 곧 그살론 곁'으로 이어졌으니, 그살론이 그 산 위의 표지였다. 케슬라는 예루살렘 정서쪽 7마일, 높은 산등성이 북쪽 비탈의 높은 지점에 있으며 이것이 여아림 산일 것이다. 지금도 상당한 숲이 남아 있다.

entries.definition: JEAT'ERAI (whom Jehovah leads), a Gershonite Levite, 1 Chr 6:21; called Ethni in 1 Chr 6:41.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 인도하시는 자'라는 뜻으로 게르손 가문 레위인, 세라의 아들이다(역대상 6:21).

entries.definition: JEBERACHI'AH (whom Jehovah blesses), the father of the Zechariah whom Isaiah took as a witness. Isa 8:2.
entries.definition_ko: 이사야가 증인으로 세운 스가랴의 아버지(사 8:2).

entries.definition: JE'BUS (place trodden down, threshing- floor), the ancient name of Jerusalem among the Canaanites, Jud 19:10-11; 1 Chr 11:4-5; probably derived from a descendant of Canaan, the son of Ham. Gen 10:16. The Jebusites were partially subdued by Joshua, Josh 10:23, Josh 10:40; Neh 12:10; Josh 15:63; Num 13:29; and they were permitted to remain after the conquest of Jebus by David. 2 Sam 5:6-9; 2 Sam 24:16-25; 1 Chr 11:48; Ezr 9:1-2. "Jebusi" is sometimes put for the city Jebus. Josh 18:16, Josh 18:28; Zech 9:7. Jebus was more accurately the south-west hill afterward called Mount Zion, or "city of David." Being surrounded on all sides by deep ravines, it was a place of great natural strength. See Jerusalem.
entries.definition_ko: '짓밟힌 곳', '타작 마당'이라는 뜻으로 가나안 사람들 사이에서 예루살렘의 옛 이름이다(삿 19:10-11, 대상 11:4-5). 아마도 함의 아들 가나안의 후손 이름에서 왔을 것이다(창 10:16). 여부스 족속은 여호수아에게 부분적으로 정복되었고(수 10:23,40, 15:63) 다윗이 여부스를 정복한 후에도 남아 있도록 허락되었다(삼하 5:6-9, 24:16-25). '여부스'가 때로 그 성읍을 가리키는 데 쓰인다(수 18:16,28). 여부스는 더 정확히는 후에 시온산 곧 '다윗 성'이라 불린 남서쪽 언덕이었다. 사방이 깊은 골짜기로 둘러싸여 천연의 요새였다.

entries.definition: JEBU'SI. Josh 15:8; Josh 18:16, Josh 18:28. A name for Jebus. See Jebus and Jerusalem.
entries.definition_ko: 여부스(JEBUS) 성읍을 가리키는 데 쓰인 이름이다(여호수아 15:8).

entries.definition:
JEB'USITES, the name of a tribe inhabiting the portion of Canaan about Jebus or Jerusalem in the time of Joshua, and which the Israelites were commanded to destroy. Deut 7:1; Deut 20:17. They joined Jabin against Joshua. Their king, Adoni-zedek, was slain and they defeated. Josh 11:3; Josh 10:15, 1 Kgs 10:26; later their city was burnt, but reoccupied by the Jebusites. Jud 1:21 and Josh 15:63; Josh 19:10-22. David conquered their stronghold, and it became a part of his capital, Jerusalem. 2 Sam 5:6, 2 Sam 5:8; 1 Chr 11:4-6. Solomon made the Jebusites pay tribute, 1 Kgs 9:20, and some were known after the captivity. Ezr 9:1. David bought the place of Araunah the Jebusite for an altar, and this afterward became the site of the temple. 2 Sam 24:16-25.

JEB'USITES, inhabitants of Jebus.
