entries.definition: ZAB'DI (gift of Jehovah). A Judite. Josh 7:1, 2 Sam 21:17, 1 Sam 30:18. A Benjamite. 1 Chr 8:19. The superintendent of David's vintage. 1 Chr 27:27. A musical Levite. Neh 11:17.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 선물'이라는 뜻. (1) 아간의 조상(여호수아 7:1), 역대상의 시므리와 동일 인물로 추정됨. (2) 베냐민 사람(역대상 8:19). (3) '시브마 사람'으로 다윗의 포도원 관리자(역대상 27:27). (4) 아삽의 아들 중 하나인 레위인(느헤미야 11:17).

entries.definition: ZAB'DIEL (gift of God). The father of the chief of David's guard. 1 Chr 27:2. A prominent priest who returned. Neh 11:14.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님의 선물'이라는 뜻. (1) 다윗의 관리 야소브암의 아버지(역대상 27:2). (2) 포로 후 제사장들의 감독(느헤미야 11:14).

entries.definition: ZA'BUD (given), "the friend" of Solomon. 1 Kgs 4:5.
entries.definition_ko: '선물'이라는 뜻으로 나단의 아들이며 솔로몬 궁정의 '왕의 벗'이었다(열왕기상 4:5).

entries.definition: ZAB'ULON, the Greek form of Zebulun, which see. Matt 4:13, 2 Sam 20:15; Rev 7:8.
entries.definition_ko: 스불론의 헬라어 형태다(마 4:13,15, 계 7:8).

entries.definition: ZACCAI (pure), the ancestor of seven hundred and sixty persons who returned with Zerubbabel. Ezr 2:9; Neh 7:14.
entries.definition_ko: '순결한'이라는 뜻으로 그 자손이 스룹바벨과 함께 예루살렘으로 돌아왔다(에스라 2:9). 삽배(ZABBAI) 항목 참조.

entries.definition: ZACCHAE'US (pure). The story of his conversion is related only by Luke 19:2-10. He was a rich Jew, resident in Jericho, and chief officer of the tax- or tribute-collectors in that place, and hence "a sinner," for the Jews regarded all publicans or tax gatherers in this light. The revenue in Jericho was doubtless considerable, and mainly derived from taxes on the balsam so abundantly produced in the neighborhood, all along the banks of the Jordan. His desire to see Christ was so much excited that he took pains to climb into a tree by the roadside that he might have a fair view of him as the crowd passed. Jesus, knowing his character and motives, proposed to spend the day with him, to which Zacchaeus gladly assented. His mind was probably brought at once under the influence of the Spirit of God, and on that very day he and his family became interested in the salvation of the gospel. He gave the best evidence of the sincerity of his conversion by declaring his intention to give half his goods to the poor and to restore fourfold for every illegal exaction he had made. Our Lord probably passed the night in his house, and on the next morning passed on with the Passover pilgrims to Jerusalem. The name Zacchaeus appears in the O.T. in the form "Zaccai."
entries.definition_ko: 예리고에 거주하던 부유한 세리장으로, 누가복음 19:2-10에만 기록된 회심 이야기의 주인공이다. 그리스도를 보려고 나무에 올라간 삭개오는 예수님이 자기 집에 머무시기로 하자 재산의 절반을 가난한 자에게 나누고 부당하게 취한 것을 네 배로 갚겠다고 선언했다.

entries.definition: ZACCHE'US. See Zacchaeus.
entries.definition_ko: 삭개오 참조.

entries.definition: ZAC'CHUR (mindful), a Simeonite. 1 Chr 4:26.
entries.definition_ko: 시므온 지파 미스마 가문 사람이다(역대상 4:26).

entries.definition: ZAC'CUR (mindful). A Reubenite. the father of the spy from that tribe. Num 13:4. A Merarite Levite. 1 Chr 24:27. A son of Asaph, and head of a course of singers. 1 Chr 25:2, 1 Chr 25:10; Neh 12:35. One who helped to build the wall. Neh 3:2. A Levite who sealed the covenant. Neh 10:12. A Levite, father of a treasurer under Nehemiah. Neh 13:13.
entries.definition_ko: '기억하는'이라는 뜻. (1) 모세가 보낸 정탐꾼 삼무아의 아버지(민수기 13:4). (2) 므라리 가문 레위인(역대상 24:27). (3) 아삽의 아들로 다윗이 세운 찬양대 반차 중 하나의 우두머리(역대상 25:2). (4)~(6) 느헤미야서에 언급된 인물들.

entries.definition: ZACHARI'AH (remembered by Jehovah). The name is the same in Hebrew as Zechariah, which also see. Son and successor of Jeroboam II., king of Israel, and the last of the house of Jehu. 2 Kgs 14:29. He reigned only six months, and then fell by the hand of Shallum, who took the throne. 2 Kgs 15:8-11; comp. Am 7:9. The father of Abi or Abijah, King Hezekiah's mother, 2 Kgs 18:2; called Zechariah in 2 Chr 29:1.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 기억하신다'는 뜻. (1) 이스라엘 왕 여로보암 2세의 아들로 왕위를 6개월간 유지하다가 살룸에게 암살당해 예후 왕조가 끝났다(열왕기하 15:8-12). (2) 히스기야의 어머니 아비의 아버지(열왕기하 18:2).

entries.definition: ZACHARI'AS, properly ZACHARI'AH (remembered by Jehovah). Our Lord mentions a Zacharias, son of Barachias, as having been slain between the "sanctuary " (not "altar," but the inner shrine) and the temple, Matt 23:35; Luke 11:51; probably the person of that name whose death under such circumstances is mentioned in 2 Chr 24:20-22. It is true that not this Zachariah, but Urijah, was the last O.T. martyr, Jer 26:23; but inasmuch as Second Chronicles was the last book of the canon according to the Jewish arrangement, our Lord took an instance from it, as he took Abel from Genesis, the first. The principal objection to this identification is that this Zacharias is stated to have been the son of Jehoiada, and not of Barachiah; but the word "son" may be used in its usual lax sense, and Barachiah may have been his grandfather. The father of John the Baptist, and husband of Elisabeth, which it is interesting to remark is the same name as "Elisheba," the name of the wife of Aaron. Ex 6:23. He was a priest of the course of Abia, which was the eighth of the twenty-four classes into which the descendants of Eleazar and Ithamar, the sons of Aaron, were divided. 1 Chr 24. Each of these ministered in the temple one week. But this fact does not enable us in any wise to determine the date of the occurrence mentioned in Luke 1. Of Zacharias and Elisabeth we read: "They were both righteous before God, walking in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord blameless. And they had no child, because that Elisabeth was barren, and they were both now well stricken in years." It was while Zacharias served one day in the temple that an angel appeared to him and prophesied the birth of a son. But, although for this he had long been praying, he did not believe that God would thus signally answer his prayer. He required a sign, and he received one - dumbness up to the time of the circumcision of the child. To the wonder of the attendant people he silently dismissed, but conveyed by action enough to let them know he had seen a vision, he was a deaf-mute until, in obedience to the angelic direction, he had named the infant born to him John. Then he not only spoke, but was filled with the Holy Ghost, and in a strain of the most devout gratitude and praise he poured out his soul. And, thus singing, he passes out of history.
entries.definition_ko: (1) 다윗이 정한 24반차 중 여덟째 아비야 반차의 제사장으로, 성전에서 분향하던 중 천사 가브리엘에게서 아내 엘리사벳이 아들(세례 요한)을 낳을 것이라는 예언을 듣고 믿지 못해 벙어리가 되었다가 아들의 이름을 '요한'이라 쓴 후 다시 말하게 되었다(누가복음 1:12-79). (2) 성전과 제단 사이에서 죽임당한 '바라가의 아들'(마태복음 23:35).

entries.definition: ZA'CHER (memorial), a Benjamite, 1 Chr 8:31; called Zechariah in 1 Chr 9:37.
entries.definition_ko: '기념'이라는 뜻으로 여히엘의 아들이며 스가랴라고도 불린다(역대상 8:31).

entries.definition: ZA'DOK (just). Son of Ahitub, of the family of Eleazar, and one of the two high priests in the time of David, Abiathar being the other. 2 Sam 8:17. He joined David at Hebron, 1 Chr 12:28, and was always faithful to him, staying behind in Jerusalem at his request during Absalom's rebellion, and subsequently anointed Solomon king, 1 Kgs 1:39, and was rewarded by Solomon for his faithful service by being made sole high priest. See Abiathar. A priest in the time of King Ahaziah. 1 Chr 6:12. The father of King Uzziah's wife. 2 Kgs 15:33; 2 Chr 27:1. One who repaired a part of the wall. Neh 3:4. 6, 7. Three other persons. Neh 3:29; Gen 10:21; Josh 13:13.
entries.definition_ko: '의로운'이라는 뜻. (1) 아히둡의 아들로 다윗과 솔로몬 시대의 대제사장이었다. 아도니야의 반역 때 다윗께 신실했던 사독은 대제사장직을 홀로 맡게 되었고 그 자손이 예루살렘 멸망 때까지 이어졌다(열왕기상 2:27-35). (2) 웃시야 왕의 아내이자 요담 왕의 어머니 여루사의 아버지(열왕기하 15:33). (3) 느헤미야가 성전 곳간을 맡긴 서기관(느헤미야 13:13). (4) 예루살렘 성벽 재건을 도운 바아나의 아들(느헤미야 3:4).

entries.definition: ZA'HAM (loathing), son of Rehoboam. 2 Chr 11:19.
entries.definition_ko: 르호보암과 아비하일(엘리압의 딸) 사이의 아들이다(역대하 11:19).

entries.definition: ZA'IR (small), a place in Idumaea where Joram overcame the Edomites. 2 Kgs 8:21. The name does not occur elsewhere. It has been regarded as equivalent to Zoar, and again to Seir, but more probably is identical with Zueirah, on the south-western side of the Dead Sea.
entries.definition_ko: '작은'이라는 뜻으로 요람이 에돔을 이긴 이두매의 한 곳이다(왕하 8:21). 이 이름은 다른 곳에 나오지 않는다. 소알과 같다고도, 세일과 같다고도 여겨져 왔으나 사해 남서쪽의 주에이라와 같을 가능성이 더 높다.

entries.definition: ZA'LAPH (bruise), the father of one who helped to build the wall. Neh 3:30.
entries.definition_ko: 예루살렘 성벽 재건을 도운 하눈의 아버지다(느헤미야 3:30).

entries.definition:
ZAL'MON (shady), one of David's guard, 2 Sam 23:28 called Ilai in 1 Chr 11:29.

ZAL'MON (shady), MOUNT, a hill near Shechem from which Abimelech cut boughs to burn the citadel. Jud 9:48. Possibly the same as Salmon. Ps 68:14. Mount Ebal is now called Jehel Sahimuyeh, in which some trace a resemblance to "Zalmon."
entries.definition_ko: (1) 다윗의 용사 중 하나로 아호아 사람으로 불리며 일래라고도 불린다(사무엘하 23:28). (2) 세겜 근처의 숲으로 아비멜렉과 그 부하들이 나뭇가지를 취해 세겜 요새를 불태운 곳이다(사사기 9:48).

entries.definition: ZALMO'NAH (shady), A station of the Israelites in the wilderness. Num 33:41-42. It lay to the east of Edom. Palmer and Raumer suggest its identity with Ma'an, a short distance east of Petra. Another suggested site is in Wady el-Ithm.
entries.definition_ko: '그늘진'이라는 뜻으로 광야에서 이스라엘이 진 친 곳이다(민 33:41-42). 에돔 동쪽에 있었다. 팔머와 라우머는 페트라에서 조금 동쪽의 마안과 동일시하자고 제안한다. 와디 엘이틈도 제시된 자리다.

entries.definition: ZALMUN'NA (shelter denied to one?), one of the two kings of Midian slain by Gideon. Jud 8:5-21; Ps 83:11.
entries.definition_ko: 여호와께서 기드온의 손에 넘기신 미디안의 두 왕 중 하나로, 세바와 함께 죽임을 당했다(사사기 8:5-21).

entries.definition: ZAMZUM'MIMS. Deut 2:20. See Zuzims.
entries.definition_ko: '거인 종족, 크고 많고 아낙 자손처럼 키가 큰 백성'으로(신명기 2:20,21) 암몬 사람들에게 정복당했으며 르바임 족속에 속했다.

entries.definition: ZANO'AH (marsh, bog), a name for two towns, A town in Judah, in the lowlands or "valley." Josh 15:34; Neh 3:13; Neh 11:30. Robinson fixed its site up the valley of Sorek, east of Beth-shemesh, at Zamu'a, on the slope of a hill, 14 miles west-south-west of Jerusalem. The Pal. Memoirs also accept this large ruin as the site of Zanoah. A town in the highlands of Judah. Josh 15:56. Robinson proposed Za'untah, 10 miles south-south-west of Hebron, and Conder, after proposing and abandoning another site, appears to accept Robinson's identification.
entries.definition_ko: '늪', '수렁'이라는 뜻으로 두 성읍의 이름이다. 하나는 유다 저지대 곧 '평지'의 성읍이고(수 15:34, 느 3:13, 11:30), 로빈슨은 소렉 골짜기를 거슬러 벧세메스 동쪽, 예루살렘 서남서 14마일의 언덕 비탈 자무아에 그 자리를 두었다. 다른 하나는 유다 산지의 성읍으로(수 15:56) 로빈슨은 헤브론 남남서 10마일의 자누타를 제안했다.

entries.definition: ZANO'AH. Jekuthiel is called, in the A.V. of 1 Chr 4:18, the father of Zanoah, but this means he was the founder of the village of that name. See Zanoah, 2.
entries.definition_ko: '습지'라는 뜻. (1) 소라 근처 유다 저지대의 성읍으로 포로 후 재정착되었다(느헤미야 11:30). (2) 헤브론 남서쪽 약 10마일 지점 유다 산지의 성읍(여호수아 15:56).

entries.definition: ZAPH'NATH-PAANE'AH, the name or title given by Pharaoh to Joseph immediately after his elevation. Gen 41:45. The etymology of the word is uncertain, some deriving it from a Hebrew root, "the revealer of mysteries," others from an Egyptian root, "the preserver of the age."
entries.definition_ko: 바로가 요셉에게 준 이름으로 랍비들은 '비밀을 푸는 자'로 해석했으나 콥트어에서는 '시대의 구원자'를 뜻하는 것으로 설명되기도 한다(창세기 41:45).

entries.definition: ZA'PHON (the north), a city of Gad, east of the Jordan. "in the valley." Josh 13:27. The word translated "northward" in Jud 12:1 is rendered in the Septuagint "to Zaphon." The Talmud identifies it as Amathus, and it is now represented by the ruined site Amateh, south-east of the Sea of Galilee.
entries.definition_ko: '북쪽'이라는 뜻으로 요단 동편, '골짜기에' 있던 갓의 성읍이다(수 13:27). 삿 12:1에서 '북쪽으로'라 옮긴 말이 칠십인역에서는 '사본으로'가 된다. 탈무드는 이를 아마투스와 동일시하며, 지금은 갈릴리 바다 남동쪽의 폐허 아마테가 그 자리다.

entries.definition: ZA'RA (rising of light), the son of Judah. Matt 1:3. See below.
entries.definition_ko: 유다의 아들(마 1:3). 아래 참조.

entries.definition: ZA'RAH (rising of light), a son of Judah by Tamar. Gen 38:30; Gen 46:12; called Zerah in Num 26:20; Josh 7:1, 1 Sam 30:18; Gen 22:20; 1 Chr 2:4, 1 Chr 2:6; 1 1 Chr 9:6; Neh 11:24, and Zara. Matt 1:3. The name is properly Zerah.
entries.definition_ko: 유다가 다말에게서 얻은 아들이다(창 38:30, 46:12). 민 26:20, 수 7:1, 대상 2:4,6에서는 세라라 불리고 마 1:3에서는 사라라 불린다. 이름은 정확히는 세라다.

entries.definition: ZA'REAH (hornets' town). Neh 11:29. See Zokah.
entries.definition_ko: 소라(Zorah)와 동일하다(느헤미야 11:29).

entries.definition: ZA'REATHITES, the inhabitants of Zareah or Zorah. 1 Chr 2:53.
entries.definition_ko: 사라 곧 소라의 주민을 가리킨다(대상 2:53).

entries.definition: ZA'RED (exuberant growth). Num 21:12. See Zered, Valley or Brook of.
entries.definition_ko: 세렛 골짜기 참조(민 21:12).

entries.definition: ZAR'EPHATH (smelting-house), and SAREP'TA. Luke 4:26. Zarephath was a town of Phoenicia, on the shore of the Mediterranean, between Tyre, which is 14 miles southward, and Sidon, which is 7 miles north. Scripture History. - At Zarephath, Elijah found shelter with a widow-woman during the great famine in Israel. 1 Kgs 17:8-24. The prophet Obadiah mentions it as marking the limits of Israel's victory. Ob 20. Jesus made reference to this incident in Elijah's life. Luke 4:26. Present Appearance. - Not a house now remains; only ruins mark the site. They extend for a mile along the seashore, and contain many fragments of columns. A little chapel, or uely. bears the name of El-Khuds, the Mohammedan title of Elijah, and possibly marks the site of the chapel erected by the Crusaders over the spot where the widow's house is supposed to have stood. There is no tomb within, because, as the Mussulmans say, Elijah is not yet dead: he "flies round and round the world." Tradition also claims this as the spot where our Lord rested when he visited these coasts. On the slope of a hill more than a mile back from the coast is the modern village of Surafend, which represents the ancient Zarephath.
entries.definition_ko: 두로와 시돈 사이 페니키아의 항구 도시로, 엘리야가 큰 기근 때 한 과부의 집에서 머물렀던 곳이다(왕상 17:8-24). 예수님도 이 사건을 언급하셨으며(눅 4:26), 현재는 유적만 남아 있고 근처 마을 수라펜드가 옛 사르밧으로 여겨진다.

entries.definition: ZAR'ETAN (cooling?). Josh 3:16. See Zererath or Zereda.
entries.definition_ko: 이스라엘이 요단강을 건널 때 물이 멈춰 쌓인 지점 근처의 성읍으로, '사르단 곁 아담 성읍'이라 불렸다(여호수아 3:16).

entries.definition: ZA'RETH-SHA'HAR (splendour of the dawn), a city in Reuben, on a hill in a valley. Josh 13:19. About a mile and a half east of the Dead Sea, near the mouth of the Wady Zerka Main, is a place called Zara, or Sara, a heap of stones in a little green plain, which may mark the site.
entries.definition_ko: '새벽의 광채'라는 뜻으로 '골짜기 산에 있는' 성읍이다(여호수아 13:19).

entries.definition: ZAR'HITES, THE, the descendants of Zarah, the son of Judah. Num 26:13, Ruth 4:20; Josh 7:17; 1 Chr 27:11, 1 Chr 27:13.
entries.definition_ko: 유다의 아들 세라의 후손인 유다 지파의 한 계열이다(민수기 26:13,20).

entries.definition: ZAR'TANAH (cooling), probably the present ruin Sarem, near Bethshean; but Drake would identify Sarem with Zarthan. 1 Kgs 4:12.
entries.definition_ko: '서늘함'이라는 뜻으로 아마도 벧산 근처의 오늘날 폐허 사렘일 것이다. 다만 드레이크는 사렘을 사르단과 동일시하려 한다(왕상 4:12).

entries.definition: ZAR'THAN (cooling), a town in the Jordan valley. 1 Kgs 7:46. Between it and Succoth were the clay-grounds in which Solomon cast the brass utensils for the temple-services. Drake mentions a very conspicuous mound, 3 miles south of Bethshean, called Tell Sarem - a name identical with ?'lapa't?, which the Alexandrine Codex has for Zarthan. This may be the same as Zereda, which see.
entries.definition_ko: '서늘함'이라는 뜻으로 요단 계곡의 성읍이다(왕상 7:46). 이곳과 숙곳 사이에 솔로몬이 성전 기물의 놋을 부어 만든 진흙 땅이 있었다. 드레이크는 벧산 남쪽 3마일에 텔 사렘이라는 매우 두드러진 언덕을 언급하는데, 알렉산드리아 사본이 사르단에 대해 쓴 이름과 같다. 이곳이 스레다와 같은 곳일 수 있다.

entries.definition: ZAT'THU, or ZAT'TU (a sprout), one whose descendants returned with Zerubbabel, Ezr 2:8; Neh 7:13, and married foreign wives. Ezr 10:27.
entries.definition_ko: '싹'이라는 뜻으로 그 후손이 스룹바벨과 함께 돌아왔고(스 2:8, 느 7:13) 이방 여인과 결혼했다(스 10:27).

entries.definition: ZA'VAN (disquieted). See Zaavan.
entries.definition_ko: 사아완(Zaavan, Or Zavan)을 가리킨다(역대상 1:42).

entries.definition: ZA'ZA (plenty), a son of Jonathan, and a descendant of Judah. 1 Chr 2:33.
entries.definition_ko: '풍성함'이라는 뜻으로 요나단의 아들이자 유다의 후손이다(대상 2:33).

entries.definition: ZEAL'OTS, the name of a party among the Jews, half religious and half political, founded by Judas the Galilean or the Gaulanite, Acts 5:37, and, after the death of him and his sons, led by Eleazar, one of his descendants. Contending that God was the only king of Israel and refusing to pay the tribute to the Romans, they broke out into open rebellion under the lead of Judas, but were soon dispersed, and, while afterward attempting to maintain themselves by a kind of guerilla-warfare, they gradually sunk into mere bands of robbers and brigands, and -were called Sicarii, from the Latin sica, "a dagger."
entries.definition_ko: 갈릴리 사람 또는 가울라니티스 사람 유다가 세운, 반은 종교적이고 반은 정치적인 유대인의 한 당파다(행 5:37). 그와 그 아들들이 죽은 후 그 후손 엘르아살이 이끌었다. 하나님만이 이스라엘의 왕이시라 주장하며 로마에 세금 바치기를 거부하고 유다의 지도 아래 공공연히 반란을 일으켰으나 곧 흩어졌다. 후에 일종의 유격전으로 버티려다 점차 강도와 산적 무리로 전락했고, 라틴어 '단검'에서 온 '시카리'라 불렸다.

entries.definition: ZEBADI'AH (gift of Jehovah). 1, 2, 3. Three Benjamites, sons of Beriah, 1 Chr 8:15, Elpaal, 1 Chr 8:17, and Jeroham of Gedor. 1 Chr 12:7. A Korhite Levite. 1 Chr 26:2. A Levite teaching the Law in the cities of Judah during the reign of Jehoshaphat. 2 Chr 17:8. A son of Asahel, the brother of Joab. 1 Chr 27:7. A son of Ishmael, of the house of Judah. 2 Chr 19:11. One who returned with Ezra. Ezr 8:8. A priest who had married a foreign wife after the return from Babylon. Ezr 10:20.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 선물'이라는 뜻. (1) 요압의 형제 아사헬의 아들(역대상 27:7). (2) 여호사밧이 세운 교육 제도의 교사 중 하나인 레위인(역대하 17:7,8). (3) 이스마엘의 아들로 유다 집안의 통치자(역대하 19:8-11). (4) 브리아의 아들(역대상 8:15). (5) 고라 가문의 문지기(역대상 26:2).

entries.definition: ZE'BAH (sacrifice), a Midianite king captured and killed by Gideon. Jud 8:5-21; Ps 83:11.
entries.definition_ko: 미디안의 두 왕 중 하나로 이스라엘을 침공했으나 기드온에게 결정적으로 패했다. 살문나와 함께 요단강을 건너 도망쳤으나 갈골에서 붙잡혀 처형되었다(사사기 8장).

entries.definition: ZEBA'IM (the gazelles). In Ezr 2:57; Neh 7:59 we read of a person named "Pochereth of Zebaim," Some, and Grove among them, suppose this name to be identical with "Zeboim." Others translate "Zebaim " as the plural of the Hebrew word signifying "antelope" or "gazelle," and render it "Pochereth-zebaim," "snaring the antelopes," as the name of some mighty hunter.
entries.definition_ko: '가젤들'이라는 뜻이다. 스 2:57과 느 7:59에 '스바임의 보게렛'이라는 사람이 나온다. 그로브를 비롯한 어떤 이들은 이 이름이 '스보임'과 같다고 본다. 다른 이들은 '스바임'을 '영양' 또는 '가젤'을 뜻하는 히브리어의 복수로 보아 '보게렛 스바임' 곧 '영양을 잡는 자'라 옮겨 어떤 이름난 사냥꾼의 이름으로 여긴다.

entries.definition: ZEB'EDEE (Jehovah's gift), the husband of Salome, Matt 27:56; Mark 15:40, and father of the apostles James the Great and John, Matt 4:21; lived as a fisherman in or near Bethsaida. When his two sons left him to follow Jesus, he made no objections. Matt 4:21-22; Mark 1:19-20, and his wife was one of the women who were in constant attendance on our Saviour, but he himself is not mentioned as being among the disciples, although doubtless friendly to Christ.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 선물'이라는 뜻으로 살로메의 남편이며(마 27:56, 막 15:40) 사도 큰 야고보와 요한의 아버지다(마 4:21). 벳새다나 그 근처에서 어부로 살았다. 두 아들이 예수를 따르려 떠날 때 반대하지 않았고(마 4:21-22, 막 1:19-20) 그 아내는 구주를 늘 섬긴 여인들 중 하나였다. 다만 그 자신이 제자들 가운데 있었다는 언급은 없으며, 그리스도께 우호적이었음은 분명하다.

entries.definition: ZEBI'NA (bought), one who had taken a foreign wife after the return from Babylon. Ezr 10:43.
entries.definition_ko: 포로 귀환 후 이방 아내를 둔 느보 가문 사람이다(에스라 10:43).

entries.definition: ZEBO'IM (valley of hyenas), THE VALLEY OF. It was a gorge or ravine apparently east of Michmash, and mentioned only in 1 Sam 13:18. The "wilderness" is the wild tract between the central hills and the valley of the Jordan. There are two ravines, 4 miles apart, near Jericho, called Shuk ed Dubba, "ravine of the hyaenas," which is the equivalent of the Hebrew.
entries.definition_ko: '가젤들' 또는 '노루들'이라는 뜻. (1) 소돔 평지의 '다섯 성읍' 중 하나로 아드마와 함께 언급되며 자체 왕(스메벨)이 있었으나 다른 성읍들과 함께 멸망했다(창세기 10:19). (2) 베냐민 기브아 근처의 골짜기(사무엘상 13:18). (3) 포로 후 베냐민 사람들이 거주한 곳(느헤미야 11:34).

entries.definition: ZEBO'IM, and ZEBOI'IM (roes). One of the "five cities of the plain ;" grouped with Sodom and Gomorrah. Gen 10:19; Gen 14:2, Acts 14:8; Deut 29:23; Hos 11:8. The question of the site of these cities is more fully discussed under Siddim, Sodom, and Zoar, which see. A place inhabited by the Benjamites after the Captivity. Neh 11:34. Its site is unknown.
entries.definition_ko: '가젤들' 또는 '노루들'이라는 뜻. (1) 소돔 평지의 '다섯 성읍' 중 하나로 아드마와 함께 언급되며 자체 왕(스메벨)이 있었으나 다른 성읍들과 함께 멸망했다(창세기 10:19). (2) 베냐민 기브아 근처의 골짜기(사무엘상 13:18). (3) 포로 후 베냐민 사람들이 거주한 곳(느헤미야 11:34).

entries.definition: ZEBU'DAH (given, bestowed), wife of Josiah and mother of Jehoiachim. 2 Kgs 23:36.
entries.definition_ko: 요시야의 아내이자 여호야김의 어머니이다(열왕기하 23:36).

entries.definition: ZE'BUL (habitation), Abimelech's officer in the city of Sheehem during his contest with the Canaanites. Jud 9:28-41.
entries.definition_ko: 세겜의 통치자로 아비멜렉 아래서 일했다(사사기 9:28). 세겜 사람들이 반란을 꾀함을 아비멜렉에게 알려 결국 세겜이 파괴되고 소금이 뿌려지게 했다.

entries.definition: ZEB'ULONITE, Jud 12:11. or ZEB'ULUNITES, Num 26:27, the descendants of Zebulun.
entries.definition_ko: 사사 엘론을 가리키는 명칭으로 스불론 지파 출신이다(사사기 12:11,12).

entries.definition:
ZEB'ULUN (habitation), Gen 30:20; Rev 7:8, the sixth son of Jacob and Leah, Gen 49:13, and the father of three sons who became the heads of large families.

ZEB'ULUN (a habitation), the territory possessed by the tribe of Israel descended from the sixth and last son of Leah and the tenth-born of Jacob, Gen 30:20; Gen 35:23, lay in the North of Canaan and between those of Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali. At the census of the wilderness Zebulun numbered 57,400. Num 1:30-31. In the encampment their position was to the east of the tabernacle. Num 2:7-8, and on the march they followed third under the standard of Judah. Num 10:14-16. At the second census their number was 60,500. Num 26:26. Zebulun was one of the six tribes stationed on Ebal to pronounce the curses. Deut 27:13. They joined Barak and Deborah against the army of Jabin. Jud 5:18. Situation and Extent. - In the prophetic blessing upon Zebulun. Jacob declared that "his border should be unto Zidon." Gen 49:3. The boundaries of the tribe are given in Josh 19:10-16, but many of those landmarks cannot be traced, and hence the exact limits of Zebulun are hard to determine. Asher lay to the west and north-west. Naphtali to the north-east, the Sea of Galilee and the Jordan on the east, and Issachar on the south. Some writers suppose that Zebulun did not touch the Sea of Galilee at any point, but others are of the opposite opinion, and suppose the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali to have met on the Sea of Galilee, not far from Capernaum. Matt 4:13, Ex 17:16. The territory included the great plain of Esdraelon and Mount Carmel and the plain of Acre, thus bringing it into immediate connection with the trade of Phoenicia and fulfilling the prophecy of Jacob. Gen 49:13. The territory was rich and fertile. It belonged to the hill-country, but the hills are lower and the strips of plain more productive than in the district of Naphtali, to the north. The plains and ridges toward the north melt away into the great plain. History. - Zebulun was one of the four northern tribes which bore little part in the great events of Jewish history, being comparatively isolated from Israel, and at the same time thrown into more intimate association with the adjoining heathen nations, especially with the Phoenicians. They did not drive out the natives. Jud 1:30. However. Zebulun bore a prominent part in the great victory celebrated by Deborah and Barak. Jud 5:14, 1 Sam 30:18; assisted Gideon, Jud 6:35. and David. 1 Chr 12:33, 1 Chr 12:40. This tribe became involved in gross idolatry, and some mocked the messengers of Hezekiah, although others united in the penitential services. 2 Chr 30:10-18. The territory of this tribe was depopulated in the captivity of Israel under Tiglath-pileser, 2 Kgs 15:20. and after that had no distinct tribal history. The tribe produced Elon, one of the judges, Jud 12:12, and also Jonah. 2 Kgs 14:25. In N.T. times the territory once occupied by Zebulun was a part of Galilee and honored by the presence and works of Jesus. Within its limits were Nazareth, Capernaum, Cana, and Tiberias. The great prophecy of Isaiah, Isa 9:1-2. was fulfilled by Jesus. Matt 4:13-16. The tribe is mentioned in Rev 7:8.

ZEB'ULUN (habitation), a place named in tracing the southern boundary of Asher. Josh 19:27; according to Josephus, "city of men." Perhaps the modern Sha'ab.
entries.definition_ko: 야곱과 레아의 여섯째 아들이며(창 30:20), 그 지파 영토는 가나안 북부 잇사갈·아셀·납달리 사이에 있었다. 광야 인구조사에서 57,400명이었으며(민 1:30-31), 드보라와 바락의 전쟁에서 용맹을 떨쳤다(삿 4:6). 이사야의 예언대로 예수님의 갈릴리 사역이 이 지역에서 이루어졌다(마 4:15-16).

entries.definition: ZECHARI'AH (Jehovah remembers). The eleventh of the twelve minor prophets, of priestly descent, and a contemporary of Haggai, returning from exile with Zerubbabel and the high priest Joshua. Ezr 6:1. He was the son of Berechiah, was born in Babylon, and was both a priest and a prophet. Scarcely anything is known of his life. His prophecies may be set down between b.c. 520 and 518. The Book of Zechariah consists of two divisions: I. Chs. 1-8; II. Chs. 9-14. The first division contains visions and prophecies from the second year of the reign of Darius Hystaspes, while the temple was rebuilding, exhortations to turn to Jehovah, and warnings against the enemies of the people of God. About the authorship of this part of the book there is no doubt. The second division gives a prophetic description of the future fortunes of the theocracy in conflict with the secular powers, the sufferings and death of the Messiah under the figure of the shepherd, the conversion of Israel to him, and the final glorification of the kingdom of God. About the authorship of this part of the book doubts have been raised, some ascribing it to Jeremiah because in Matt 27:9-10 a passage is quoted under the name of Jeremiah, while others have put it at a much earlier or much later period on account of the peculiarities of the style. Of all the prophets, Zechariah is the most obscure, owing to the brevity and conciseness of the diction, the predominance of symbolical and figurative language, and the peculiar character of the subject - the suffering Messiah. But he has a profound insight both into the spiritual meaning and object of the Mosaic dispensation as a schoolmaster leading to Christ, and into the character of the Messiah and the universality of his kingdom. The book contains six specific references to Christ: Zech 3:8; Zech 6:12; Zech 9:9; Zech 11:12; Neh 12:10; 2 Kgs 13:7, representing him as a lowly servant, a priest and king building Jehovah's temple, the meek and peaceful but universal monarch, the shepherd betrayed for the price of a slave (thirty pieces of silver), the leader to repentance, and the Fellow of Jehovah smitten by Jehovah himself, at once the Redeemer and the Pattern of his flock. Besides the prophet, twenty-seven other persons of the name Zechariah are mentioned in Scripture, among whom are - Seven Levites. 1 Chr 9:21; 1 Chr 15:18; 1 Chr 24:25; 1 Chr 26:11; 2 Chr 20:14; 2 Chr 29:13; 2 Chr 34:12. Four priests. 2 Chr 35:8; Neh 11:12; Neh 12:16, John 12:35, Ex 12:41. The son of the high priest Jehoiada, stoned in the court of the house of the Lord on the command of Joash, king of Judah. 2 Chr 24:20. Two chiefs who returned with Ezra from Babylon. Ezr 8:3, Rev 1:11. The father of Iddo, ruler of Manasseh in Gilead. 1 Chr 27:21. The son of Jeberechiah, whom the prophet Isaiah took as one of the faithful witnesses when he wrote about Maher-shalal-hash-baz. Isa 8:2.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 기억하신다'는 뜻. (1) 열두 소선지자 중 열한 번째로 다리오 왕 2년(주전 520년)부터 예언 사역을 시작했으며 학개와 동시대 인물이다. 그의 책은 1-8장(위로와 소망의 환상들)과 9-14장(메시아 강림과 마지막 때의 예언)으로 나뉜다. (2) 여호야다의 아들 또는 손자로 아하시야와 요아스 시대의 인물이며, 백성의 반역을 책망하다 돌에 맞아 성전 뜰에서 죽었다(역대하 24:20-21); 주님이 마태복음 23:35에서 이 사건을 언급하셨다. (3) 웃시야 시대의 선지자로 그에게 지혜로운 조언을 했다(역대하 26:5). 이 밖에도 성경에는 이 이름을 가진 여러 인물이 언급된다.

entries.definition: ZE'DAD (mountain-side) , a city on the northern boundary of the Israelites, as described by Moses and Ezekiel. Num 34:8; Eze 47:15. It has been identified with the modern Sudud, some 70 miles north-east of Damascus, and 35 miles south-south-east of Hums, the ancient Emesa. Sudud is still a large village, though it does not contain any relics of antiquity except a few fragments of columns built into the mud walls of the modern houses. It is surrounded by gardens and cultivated fields. The inhabitants are all members of the Jacobite Church, and constitute the only remnant of that ancient sect in Syria.
entries.definition_ko: '산비탈'이라는 뜻으로 모세와 에스겔이 묘사한 이스라엘 북쪽 경계의 성읍이다(민 34:8, 겔 47:15). 다메섹 북동쪽 약 70마일, 옛 에메사인 훔스에서 남남동으로 35마일 떨어진 오늘날의 수두드로 확인된다. 수두드는 지금도 큰 마을이나, 현대 가옥의 진흙 벽에 박힌 기둥 조각 몇 개 말고는 고대 유물이 없다. 동산과 경작지에 둘러싸여 있다. 주민은 모두 야곱파 교회 신자로 수리아에 남은 그 옛 분파의 유일한 잔존이다.

entries.definition: ZEDEKI'AH (justice of Jehovah). The last king of Judah, the son of Josiah, and the uncle of Jehoiachin. His proper name was "Mattaniah," but Nebuchadnezzar changed it to "Zedekiah" when raising him to the throne. He commenced his reign at twenty-one, and reigned eleven years, 598-588 b.c. 2 Chr 36:11. He was a weak man, and the people were completely demoralized. He had not courage to vindicate Jeremiah, but allowed the people to be led astray by false prophets; and the consequence was disastrous. In the ninth year of his reign he revolted against Nebuchadnezzar, in consequence of which the Assyrian monarch marched his army into Judaea and took all the fortified places. In the eleventh year of his reign, on the ninth day of the fourth month (July), Jerusalem was taken. The king and his people endeavored to escape by night, but, the Chaldaean troops pursuing them, they were overtaken in the plain of Jericho. Zedekiah was seized and carried to Nebuchadnezzar, then at Riblah, in Syria, who reproached him with his perfidy, caused all his children to be slain before his face and his own eyes to be put out, and then, loading him with chains of brass, ordered him to be sent to Babylon. 2 Kgs 25:1-11; 2 Chr 36:12, 2 Chr 36:20. Thus the double prophecy concerning him - that he should be carried to Babylon, but never see it - was literally fulfilled. Jer 32:4-5; Jer 34:3; comp. Eze 12:13. A false prophet in the reign of Ahab. 1 Kgs 22:11, 1 Kgs 22:24-25; 2 Chr 18:10, 2 Chr 18:23-24. 3. A false prophet who was put to death by Nebuchadnezzar. Jer 29:21-22. One of the princes at the court of Jehoiakim. Jer 36:12.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와는 의로우시다'는 뜻. (1) 유다의 마지막 왕으로 요시야의 셋째 아들이며 본명은 맛다니야였으나 느부갓네살이 왕으로 세우며 개명했다. 예레미야의 권고에도 불구하고 바벨론에 반기를 들어 느부갓네살의 침공을 초래했고, 예루살렘이 함락되자 자녀들이 죽는 것을 본 뒤 눈이 뽑히고 사슬에 묶여 바벨론으로 끌려갔다(열왕기하 25:1-7). (2) 아합 시대의 거짓 선지자, 그나아나의 아들(열왕기상 22:11). (3) 여호야김 시대 유다의 방백, 하나냐의 아들(예레미야 36:12).

entries.definition: ZEEB (wolf), a Midianite prince who was slain by the Ephraimites after the great victory of Gideon. Jud 7:25; Ps 83:11.
entries.definition_ko: '이리'라는 뜻으로 이스라엘을 침공한 미디안 대군의 두 지도자 중 하나이며 오렙과 함께 기드온에게 패해 죽임을 당했다(사사기 7:25).

entries.definition: ZEEB, THE WINE-PRESS OF, where Zeeb was slain. Jud 7:25. It was near a ford of the Jordan as one comes down from the mountains of Ephraim.
entries.definition_ko: 스엡이 죽임을 당한 곳이다(삿 7:25). 에브라임 산지에서 내려올 때 만나는 요단 나루 근처에 있었다.

entries.definition: ZE'LAH (a rib), a city of Benjamin, Josh 18:28, the site of the family tomb of Kish, the father of Saul, 2 Sam 21:14, and probably Saul's birthplace. Conder suggests Kummua as its site. See also Zelzah.
entries.definition_ko: '옆구리'라는 뜻으로 베냐민의 성읍이며(수 18:28) 사울의 아버지 기스의 가족 무덤이 있던 곳이고(삼하 21:14) 아마도 사울의 출생지일 것이다. 콘더는 쿰무아를 그 자리로 제안한다.

entries.definition: ZE'LEK (fissure), one of David's warriors. 2 Sam 23:37; 1 Chr 11:39.
entries.definition_ko: 암몬 사람으로 다윗의 용사 중 하나이다(사무엘하 23:37).

entries.definition: ZELO'PHEHAD (first-born), a descendant of Manasseh who died in the wilderness and left only daughters. It was then ordained that, in want of male heirs, females should succeed to the inheritance, but not be allowed to marry out of the tribe. Num 26:33; Deut 27:1, 1 Chr 27:7; Isa 36:2, Isa 36:6, Num 36:10-11; Josh 17:3; 1 Chr 7:15.
entries.definition_ko: 므낫세 지파 길르앗 가문 출신으로 광야에서 죽었으며 아들이 없었다. 그의 딸들이 모세에게 상속권을 호소해 아들이 없을 경우 딸이 아버지의 몫을 상속받도록 하는 규례가 제정되었다(민수기 27:1-11).

entries.definition: ZELO'TES. See Simon, Zealots.
entries.definition_ko: 셀롯인(SIMON; ZEALOTS) 항목 참조이다(누가복음 6:15).

entries.definition: ZEL'ZAH (shade from the sun), a place in Benjamin not far from Rachel's tomb. 1 Sam 10:2; identified by several writers (although Grove disputes the identification) with the little village of Biet Jala about a mile west of Rachel's tomb and 3 miles south-west of Jerusalem. Perhaps Zelah was the same place.
entries.definition_ko: '햇빛을 가리는 그늘'이라는 뜻으로 라헬의 무덤에서 멀지 않은 베냐민의 한 곳이다(삼상 10:2). 여러 저자가 라헬의 무덤 서쪽 1마일, 예루살렘 남서쪽 3마일의 작은 마을 베이트 잘라와 동일시한다(그로브는 반대한다). 어쩌면 셀라가 같은 곳이었을 것이다.

entries.definition: ZEMARA'IM (double mount?), a name of two places. A town in Benjamin. Josh 18:22. It has long been identified with Sunna, in the Jordan valley, 4 miles north of Jericho. The name is in the plural, and two ruins bearing the name of Sunna have been found close together. Mount Zemaraim, in the highlands of Ephraim, 2 Chr 13:4; possibly the name survives in the modern Tal'at esSumra.
entries.definition_ko: (1) 베냐민의 한 성읍(여호수아 18:22). (2) 예루살렘 북쪽 에브라임 산지의 한 산으로 아비야와 여로보암의 군대가 격돌해 이스라엘 왕이 대패한 곳이다(역대하 13:4-20).

entries.definition: ZEM'ARITES, THE, descendants of Canaan. Gen 10:18; 1 Chr 1:16.
entries.definition_ko: 가나안의 후손이다(창 10:18, 대상 1:16).

entries.definition: ZEMI'RA (a song), a descendant of Benjamin. 1 Chr 7:8.
entries.definition_ko: '포도 재배자'라는 뜻으로 베겔의 아들 중 하나인 베냐민 사람이다(역대상 7:8).

entries.definition: ZE'NAN (place of flocks), a place in the plain of Judah, apparently near the western coast, Josh 15:37; perhaps the same as the "Zaanan" of Micah 1:11. Among the suggested sites are Jem'a, a little village south-cast of Ascalon; Zanabra, 2 1/2 miles south-east of Mareshah (Schwartz); and Kerbetes Senat, a little north of Beit Jibrin (Knobel).
entries.definition_ko: '양 떼의 곳'이라는 뜻으로 유다 평지, 서쪽 해안에 가까웠던 것으로 보이는 곳이다(수 15:37). 아마도 미 1:11의 '사아난'과 같을 것이다. 제시된 자리로는 아스글론 남동쪽의 작은 마을 젬아, 마레사 남동쪽 2.5마일의 자나브라(슈바르츠), 베이트 지브린 조금 북쪽의 케르베트 에스세낫(크노벨)이 있다.

entries.definition: ZE'NAS, a Christian whom Paul wished Titus to bring along with him. Tit 3:13.
entries.definition_ko: '율법사'라 불린 제자로 바울이 디도에게 함께 데려오라고 부탁한 인물이다(디도서 3:13).

entries.definition: ZEPHANI'AH (Jehovah hides). The ninth of the minor prophets, was the son of Cushi, and lived in the days of Josiah. His prophecy was uttered in the early part of the ministry of Jeremiah, between b.c. 020 and 609. It is mainly designed to excite the Jewish nation to repentance, in view of threatened judgments, and to comfort the people of God with promises of the final triumph of righteousness. The description of the judgment in Zeph 1:14-15, "The great day of Jehovah is near" (in the Latin version Dies irae, dies illa), has furnished the keynote to the sublimest hymn of the Middle Ages, the Dies Irae of Thomas a Celano (1250) - so often translated, but never equalled - which brings before us, with most thrilling effect, the final judgment as an awful impending reality. A priest in the reign of Zedekiah. 2 Kgs 25:18-21; Jer 21:1; Jer 29:25-29; Job 37:3; Jer 52:24-27. A Kohathite Levite. 1 Chr 6:36. The father of Josiah. Zech 6:10.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 숨기셨다'는 뜻. (1) 구시의 아들로 열두 소선지자 중 아홉 번째이며 요시야 왕 시대(주전 641~610년)에 예언했다. 그의 책은 세상과 이스라엘에 대한 심판 선언, 이방 나라에 대한 심판, 예루살렘의 비참함, 구원의 약속으로 구성된다. (2) 마아세야의 아들로 스데기야 시대의 '둘째 제사장'이었으며(예레미야 21:1) 바벨론 왕에게 처형되었다(열왕기하 25:21).

entries.definition: ZE'PHATH (watch-tower), a city and tower in the mountains of the Amorites, near Kadesh, Judg 1:17; identified by Palmer and Drake with the ruins of a city called Sebaitah, in the midst of a fertile plain. It was the same as Hormah, which see.
entries.definition_ko: '망대'라는 뜻으로 가데스 근처 아모리 산지의 성읍이자 망대다(삿 1:17). 팔머와 드레이크는 비옥한 평야 한가운데 있는 세바이타라는 성읍의 폐허와 동일시한다. 호르마와 같은 곳이었다.

entries.definition: ZEPH'ATHAH (watch-tower), VALLEY OF, near Mareshah. 2 Chr 14:10. A deep valley is found near the site of Mareshah, running down to Beit Jibriu (Eleutheropolis), and thence into the plain of Philistia, which Porter identified with Zepliathah. See Mareshah.
entries.definition_ko: '망대'라는 뜻으로 마레사 근처의 골짜기다(대하 14:10). 마레사 자리 근처에 깊은 골짜기가 있어 베이트 지브린(엘류테로폴리스)으로 내려가 블레셋 평야로 이어지는데, 포터는 이를 스바다와 동일시했다.

entries.definition: ZE'PHI. 1 Chr 1:36. See Zepho.
entries.definition_ko: 스보(Zepho) 항목을 보라(역대상 1:36).

entries.definition: ZE'PHO (watch-tower). Gen 36:11, 2 Sam 20:15, or ZE'PHI, 1 Chr 1:36, a son of Kliphaz, the son of Esau.
entries.definition_ko: 에서의 아들 엘리바스의 아들로 에돔의 족장 중 하나다(창세기 36:11,15).

entries.definition: ZE'PHON (a looking-out), a son of Gad, Num 26:15; called Ziphion in Gen 46:16.
entries.definition_ko: 갓의 아들로 스본 족속의 조상이며 창세기에서는 시뵨으로 불린다(민수기 26:15; 창세기 46:16).

entries.definition: ZEPH'ONITES, the descendants of Zephon. Num 26:15.
entries.definition_ko: 스본의 후손을 가리킨다(민 26:15).

entries.definition: ZER (flint), a place in Naphtali; probably near the Lake of Gennesaret. Josh 19:35.
entries.definition_ko: 납달리 지파 영토의 요새 성읍으로 갈릴리 호수 남서쪽 인근으로 추정된다(여호수아 19:35).

entries.definition: ZE'RAH (a rising of light). An Ethiopian or Cushite king who with an immense army invaded the kingdom of Judah in the reign of Asa, but was completely routed at Mareshah, in the valley of Zephathah, 2 Chr 14:9; has by some been identified with Uraken I. or II. of the twenty-second dynasty of Egypt. A son of Reuel, and grandson of Esau. Gen 36:13, 2 Sam 21:17, 1 Sam 15:33; 1 Chr 1:37, 1 Chr 1:44. A son of Simeon, Num 26:13; 1 Chr 4:24; called Zohar in Gen 46:10. A Gershonite Levite. 1 Chr 6:21, 1 Chr 6:41.
entries.definition_ko: '해돋이'라는 뜻. (1) '에티오피아' 사람으로 아마 시삭 후계자 오소르콘 2세로 추정되며 아사 시대 유다를 침공했으나 스바다에서 대패했다(역대하 14:9-15). (2) 다말의 아들, 세라라고도 불림(창세기 38:30). (3) 게르손 가문 레위인(역대상 6:21).

entries.definition: ZERAHI'AH (whom Jehovah caused to he born). A priest of the line of Eleazar. 1 Chr 6:6, 1 Chr 6:51; Ezr 7:4. One whose descendants returned from Babylon with Ezra. Ezr 8:4.
entries.definition_ko: 북기의 아들이자 서기관 에스라의 조상, 또는 에스라와 함께 돌아온 엘리호에내의 아버지를 가리킨다(역대상 6:6,51; 에스라 8:4).

entries.definition: ZE'RED (exuberant growth - i.e., of trees), VALLEY or BROOK OF, a valley separating Moab from Edora. Deut 2:13-14; called "Zared" in Num 21:12. Robinson identified it with Wady el-Aksi; others, including Tristram, propose Wady Sidiyeh or the Seil Gharabi, a branch of the Sediyeh, down which runs a fine stream that empties into the south-eastern corner of the Dead Sea. This wady most likely constituted the boundary between Moab and Edom, as it is now the recognized boundary between Kerak and Petra.
entries.definition_ko: '세렛 골짜기' 또는 '세렛 시내'로 모압과 에돔을 가르는 골짜기다(신 2:13-14). 민 21:12에서는 '사렛'이라 불린다. 로빈슨은 와디 엘아사와 동일시했고, 트리스트람 등은 와디 시디예나 세일 가라비를 제안하는데, 그 아래로 좋은 시내가 흘러 사해 남동쪽 모퉁이로 들어간다. 이 와디가 모압과 에돔의 경계였을 가능성이 높으니, 지금도 케락과 페트라의 인정된 경계이기 때문이다.

entries.definition: ZER'EDA (cooling?), a place in Ephraim, in the plain of Jordan. 1 Kgs 11:26. Possibly it is the same as Zaretan. Josh 3:16; Zererath, Jud 7:22; Zartanah, 1 Kgs 4:12; Zeredathah, 2 Chr 4:17; and Zarthan. 1 Kgs 7:46. There seems to be much confusion about these names, but the Pal. Memoirs suggest as the site of Zereda, Siirdah, 2 1/2 miles north-west of Beitin (Bethel).
entries.definition_ko: '서늘함'이라는 뜻으로 요단 평지 에브라임의 한 곳이다(왕상 11:26). 사르단(수 3:16), 스레라(삿 7:22), 사르다나(왕상 4:12), 스레라다(대하 4:17), 사르단(왕상 7:46)과 같은 곳일 수 있다. 이 이름들에 관해 혼란이 많아 보이나, 팔레스타인 조사단은 스레다의 자리로 베이틴(벧엘) 북서쪽 2.5마일의 수르다를 제시한다.

entries.definition: ZERED'ATHAH. 2 Chr 4:17. Conder identifies it with Zartanah and the modern Tell es Sarem, 3 miles south of Beisan.
entries.definition_ko: 요단 평지의 한 장소로 사르단과 같은 곳이며(역대하 4:17) 솔로몬이 히람으로 하여금 성전용 청동 주물을 만들게 한 곳이다.

entries.definition: ZER'ERATH. Jud 7:22. This would appear to be the name of a district, and is generally connected with the Zarthan and Zaretan of other passages of the O.T. Conder formerly placed it below Jezreel and near Beisan, but later investigations have afforded little confirmation of this identification of Zererath. See Zereda.
entries.definition_ko: 삿 7:22의 지명으로 한 지역의 이름으로 보이며, 대개 구약 다른 구절의 사르단, 사르단과 연결된다. 콘더는 예전에 이스르엘 아래, 베이산 근처에 두었으나 후속 조사에서 이 비정을 뒷받침할 만한 것이 거의 나오지 않았다.

entries.definition: ZE'RESH, the wife of Haman, and his counsellor and instigator in iniquity. Esth 6:10.
entries.definition_ko: 하만의 아내로 모르드개를 처형할 교수대를 만들도록 부추겼다(에스더 5:10).

entries.definition: ZE'RETH (splendor), a descendant of Judah. 1 Chr 4:7.
entries.definition_ko: 드고아의 창시자 아술과 그 아내 헬라 사이의 아들이다(역대상 4:7).

entries.definition: ZE'RI (built), a son of Jeduthun. 1 Chr 25:3.
entries.definition_ko: 다윗 시대 여두둔의 아들 중 하나다(역대상 25:3).

entries.definition: ZE'ROR (a bundle), one of Saul's ancestors. 1 Sam 9:1.
entries.definition_ko: 베냐민 사람으로 사울의 아버지 기스의 조상이다(사무엘상 9:1).

entries.definition: ZERU'AH (leprous), the mother of Jeroboam I. 1 Kgs 9:26.
entries.definition_ko: 북이스라엘 열 지파의 첫 왕 여로보암의 어머니이다(열왕기상 11:26).

entries.definition: ZERUB'BABEL (begotten in Babylon), 1 Chr 3:19, or ZOROB'ABEL, Matt 1:12, was the leader of the first colony of Jews that returned from the captivity in Babylon, Ezr 2:2, and was of the family of David, a son of Salathiel or Shealtiel, Hag 1:1; Matt 1:12, but called a son of Pedaiah, the brother or son of Salathiel, in 1 Chr 3:17-19. To him Cyrus committed the sacred vessels that were returned to Jerusalem. He laid the foundations of the temple, Zech 4:6-10, and was chiefly instrumental in restoring the religious rites of the nation. The advances of the mixed population of Samaria, who wished to participate in the building of the temple, he refused, and their intrigues at the Persian court caused the work to be stopped, but only for a short time; finally, he succeeded in completing the building. Ezr 5:2; Hag 1:12, 2 Kgs 22:14; Gen 2:2, Hab 2:4; Zech 4:6, 1 Kgs 16:10. He was the governor of Judaea. Neh 12:47.
entries.definition_ko: 스알디엘(살라디엘)의 아들이며(학개 1:1) 역대상에서는 브다야의 아들로도 불린다. 페르시아 이름 세스바살로도 알려져 있으며, 고레스 왕 원년에 포로에서 돌아온 첫 무리 42,360명을 이끌었고 무너진 성전 자리에 제단을 세우고 성전 기초를 놓았다(에스라 3:8-13).

entries.definition: ZERUI'AH (cleft, wounded), a sister of David, and the mother of Joab. 1 Sam 26:6; 1 Chr 2:16.
entries.definition_ko: 다윗의 누이로 다윗의 군대에서 가장 뛰어난 세 용사인 아비새, 요압, 아사헬의 어머니이다(역대상 2:16).

entries.definition: ZE'THAM (olive tree), a Levite. 1 Chr 23:8; 1 Chr 26:22.
entries.definition_ko: 레위인이다(역대상 23:8).

entries.definition: ZE'THAN, a Benjamite chief. 1 Chr 7:10.
entries.definition_ko: 베냐민 사람이다(역대상 7:10).

entries.definition: ZE'THAR (star?), a eunuch of Ahasuerus. Esth 1:10.
entries.definition_ko: 아하수에로 왕의 일곱 내시 중 하나다(에스더 1:10).

entries.definition: ZI'A (motion), a Gadite. 1 Chr 5:13.
entries.definition_ko: 갓 사람이다(역대상 5:13).

entries.definition: ZI'BA (statue), a servant of Saul, 2 Sam 19:17, whom David appointed a sort of steward to Mephibosheth. 2 Sam 9:2-12.
entries.definition_ko: '사울 집안의 종'으로(사무엘하 9:2) 요나단의 아들 므비보셋이 살아있음을 다윗에게 알렸으나 훗날 므비보셋을 모함해 배신했다.

entries.definition: ZIB'EON (dyed), a son of Seir the Horite, but called a Hivite himself. Gen 36:2, 2 Kgs 22:14, Ruth 4:20, Jud 6:24, 1 Chr 2:29; 1 Chr 1:38.
entries.definition_ko: '물들인'이라는 뜻으로 세일 사람 호리의 아들이나, 그 자신은 히위 사람이라 불린다(창 36:2,14,20,24,29, 대상 1:38).

entries.definition: ZIB'IA (a roe), a Benjamite. 1 Chr 8:9.
entries.definition_ko: 베냐민 사람이다(역대상 8:9).

entries.definition: ZIB'IAH, the mother of Joash. 2 Kgs 12:1; 2 Chr 24:1.
entries.definition_ko: 요아스 왕의 어머니이다(열왕기하 12:1).

entries.definition: ZICH'RI (remembered, renowned). A Levite. Ex 6:21. 2, 3, 4. Three Benjamite chiefs. 1 Chr 8:19, 1 Chr 8:23, 1 Chr 8:27. A Levite, 1 Chr 9:15; called Zabdi in Neh 11:17. A Levite who descended from Moses. 1 Chr 26:25. A Reubenite. 1 Chr 27:16. The father of one of Jehoshaphat's captains. 2 Chr 17:16. One instrumental in making Joash king. 2 Chr 23:1. An Ephraimite who distinguished himself in the war between Pekah and Ahaz. 2 Chr 28:7. A Benjamite. Neh 11:9. A priest during the reign of Joiakim. Neh 12:17.
entries.definition_ko: '기억된', '이름난'이라는 뜻. 레위인(출 6:21), 베냐민 지도자 셋(대상 8:19,23,27), 레위인(대상 9:15; 느 11:17에서는 삽디), 모세의 후손인 레위인(대상 26:25), 르우벤 사람(대상 27:16), 여호사밧의 지휘관 중 하나의 아버지(대하 17:16), 요아스를 왕으로 세우는 데 힘쓴 사람(대하 23:1), 베가와 아하스의 전쟁에서 두각을 나타낸 에브라임 사람(대하 28:7), 베냐민 사람(느 11:9), 요야김 때의 제사장(느 12:17) 등을 가리킨다.

entries.definition: ZID'DIM (the sides), a place in Naphtali, Josh 19:35; perhaps the village of Kefr-Hattin, 5 miles west of Tiberias.
entries.definition_ko: '옆면들'이라는 뜻으로 납달리의 한 성읍이다(여호수아 19:35).

entries.definition: ZIDKI'JAH (justice of Jehovah), one who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah. Neh 10:1.
entries.definition_ko: 느헤미야와 함께 언약에 인친 인물이다(느헤미야 10:1).

entries.definition: ZI'DON (hunting; Heb. Tsidon). "Sidon," the Greek form, is found in Gen 10:15, Acts 1:19, in the Apocrypha generally, and in the N.T. Zidon was a rich and ancient Phoenician city. Situation. - It was situated on the Mediterranean coast, on the northern slope of a small promontory which juts out from a low plain, less than 2 miles broad, between the Lebanon and the sea. The city was 25 miles south of the modern Beirut, 25 miles north of Tyre, and 123 miles in a direct line north-west of Jerusalem. Its latitude is 33░ 34' north. Scripture References. - Zidon is one of the most ancient cities of the world. The person after whom it is named was the "first-born" of Canaan, the grandson of Noah. Gen 10:15; 1 Chr 1:13. This was b.c. 2218. In Joshua's time it was "great Zidon," Josh 11:8; Gen 19:28, and seems to have been the metropolis of Phoenicia. Zidon was one of the limits of the tribe of Asher, Josh 19:28, but was never possessed by the Israelites. Jud 1:31; Heb 3:3. In fact, the Zidonians oppressed Israel, Jud 10:12, seeming themselves to be secure from all attacks and living "careless." Jud 18:7, Acts 20:28. Tyre was one of the colonies - a "virgin daughter." Isa 23:12 - of Zidon, but subsequently became the more important town. The two names frequently recur together as denoting not only the cities, but the adjacent country; but the name of Zidon alone was sometimes used to denote the Phoenicians in general. Jud 3:3. The Zidonians were famous for commerce, manufactures, and arts. Their sailors and workmen were noted. Zidonians assisted in the work of building the temple. 1 Chr 22:4; 1 Kgs 5:6; Eze 27:8. From Zidon also came idolatrous abominations to corrupt Israel. 1 Kgs 11:5, 1 Kgs 11:33; 2 Kgs 23:13. The city was mentioned frequently in prophetic threatenings. but with much less severity than Tyre. Isa 23:2, Ex 6:4, Jud 4:12; Jer 25:22; 1 Sam 27:3; Jer 47:4; Eze 27:8; Eze 28:21-22; Eze 32:30; Joel 3:4; Zech 9:2. In N.T. times Zidon (called "Sidon") was visited by Jesus, Matt 15:21; Mark 7:24; Luke 4:26, although the "coasts" of Tyre and Sidon denoted the adjacent region as well as the cities themselves, and some think that the Saviour did not enter the cities. Hearers from among those people were drawn to his preaching. Mark 3:8; Luke 6:17; comp. Matt 11:22; Luke 10:14. Herod's displeasure with this region is noted. Acts 12:20. The apostle Paul touched at Zidon on his way to Rome, and visited the Christians there. Acts 27:3. Secular History. - Homer makes special mention of the skill of the Zidonian workmen. The embroidered robes of Andromache, the silver bowl given as a prize by Achilles at the games in honor of Patrocles, the bowl which Menelaus gave Telemachus, the purple of fierce Achilles, were specimens of Zidonian handicraft. Zidonian ships were present at the siege of Troy, and Herodotus declares that the Zidonian ships in the fleet of Xerxes were the best and the most renowned of the famous armada. Xerxes sat in a Zidonian ship, and the king of Zidon sat near to him in council. Zidon flourished under the Chaldiean and Persian dominion. It revolted against the Persians in the time Zidon (After Cassas.) of Artaxerxes III. Ochus, but was subdued, and 40,000 of its citizens perished in the conflagration of the city, the fire being kindled by the people themselves. The gates of the city were willingly opened to Alexander the Great after the battle of Issus, b.c. 333. During the Roman period it had its own archons, senate, and national council. A bishop of Zidon attended the council of Nicea, a.d. 325. After the conquest of Syria by the Muslims, a.d. 636, Zidon surrendered to these new masters. During the crusades it experienced terrible vicissitudes. Baldwin I. took it, after a six weeks' siege, in a.d. 1111; Saladin razed the town and its fortifications in 1187; the Crusaders again gained possession of it in 1197, but could not retain the town, which was once more destroyed. It was rebuilt and razed, refortified and again devastated. In 1291 it became the permanent possession of the Muslims, and was destroyed. For several centuries it was neglected, but gradually revived in the seventeenth century, and still continues to exist. Present Condition. - The site of ancient Zidon is occupied by the modern Saida, beautifully situated on a promontory in front of which lies an island. The northern harbor, protected by a ledge of rocks, is now used; the southern one is abandoned. The anchorage is bad, and the trade of the city is unimportant. Around the island are the remains of quays built of large hewn stones. The ruins of the ancient castle are approached by a causeway. The burying-grounds are extensive, and many curious sarcophagi have been discovered. One was the sarcophagus of King Ashmanezer; it has been placed in the Museum at Paris, and antiquarians fix its date at from b.c. 300 to b.c. 1000. The ancient ruins are few. There are fragments of marble and granite columns, mosaic pavement, pottery, etc. In its situation and surroundings Zidon is one of the most picturesque cities in Syria. The gardens and orchards environing it are charming and afford a great variety of fruits, such as oranges, lemons, citrons, bananas, and dates. The oranges of Zidon are very famous and better than those of Jaffa. The population is estimated at 10,000, of whom about 7000 are Muslims and the rest Greeks, Catholics, Maronites, and Jews. There are nine mosques in the town. The American Presbyterian Board has established a flourishing Protestant mission there.
entries.definition_ko: 두로 북쪽 25마일, 베이루트 남쪽 25마일의 페니키아 항구 도시로, 가나안의 장자 시돈의 이름에서 유래했다(창 10:15). 한때 페니키아에서 가장 강력한 도시였으나 후에 두로에 추월당했다. 유리 제조의 발명지로 알려져 있으며, 예수님이 이 지역을 방문하셨고(마 15:21) 바울이 로마로 가는 도중 기항했다(행 27:3).

entries.definition: ZIDO'NIANS, the inhabitants of Zidon. Jud 10:12.
entries.definition_ko: 가나안 민족 중 하나로 이스라엘 정착 초기 압제했으며(사사기 10:12) 사치스럽고 방종한 생활을 했다고 전해진다(사사기 18:7). 목재 벌목 기술이 뛰어나 솔로몬의 성전 건축에 고용되었으며 여신 아스다롯과 태양신 바알을 숭배했다(열왕기상 5:8, 11:5,33).

entries.definition: ZIF (bloom). 1 Kgs 6:1. See Month.
entries.definition_ko: '광채'라는 뜻으로 열왕기상 6:1에만 나오는 '둘째 달'을 가리키며 후대 유대인들은 이야르라고 불렀다.

entries.definition: ZI'HA (dry). One whose descendants returned with Zerubbabel. Ezr 2:43; Neh 7:46. A ruler among the Nethinim. Neh 11:21.
entries.definition_ko: (1) 느디님 가문의 이름(에스라 2:43). (2) 느디님의 지도자(느헤미야 11:21).

entries.definition: ZIK'LAG (outpouring of a fountain?), a city in the South of Judah, Josh 15:31; afterward given to Simeon. Isa 19:5. It was at times held by the Philistines. Achish, king of Gath, gave it to David, and it subsequently belonged to Judah. Its chief interest is in connection with the life of David. 1 Sam 27:6; 1 Sam 30:1, 1 Sam 30:14, 1 Sam 30:26; 2 Sam 1:1; 2 Sam 4:10; 1 Chr 4:30; 1 Chr 12:1-20. It was also inhabited after the return from the Captivity. Neh 11:28. Wilton suggested its identification with 'Aslaj, or Kanluj, in a deep valley among the hills of the south country, some 12 miles south of Beer-sheba. Conder suggested its identification with Zaheilikah, 11 miles south of east from Gaza, and 19 miles south-west of Neit Jibrin. The site is in the open, rolling plain, some distance from the low, open hills of the Shefalah. The ruins occur on three small hills, in the form of an equilateral triangle, nearly half a mile apart. There is a number of ancient ruined cisterns, of which the stones have been removed and the sites ploughed over. Neither of the above has been accepted as the site of Ziklag.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 남부 네게브의 성읍으로(여호수아 15:31) 다윗이 사울을 피해 도망칠 때 블레셋 왕 아기스가 거주지로 내준 곳이다(사무엘상 27:6). 다윗이 블레셋 원정에 나간 사이 아말렉 사람들에게 약탈당했으나 다윗이 추격해 포로를 되찾았다(사무엘상 30장).

entries.definition: ZIL'LAH (shade), one of the wives of Laniech. Gen 4:19, Josh 11:22, Heb 12:23.
entries.definition_ko: 가인 계열 라멕의 아내 중 하나로 두발가인의 어머니이다(창세기 4:19,22).

entries.definition: ZIL'PAH (dropping), the handmaid of Leah, and the mother of Gad and Asher. Gen 30:9.
entries.definition_ko: 레아의 몸종으로 갓과 아셀의 어머니이다(창세기 30:9-13).

entries.definition: ZIL'THAI (shade). A Benjamite. 1 Chr 8:20. A chieftain of Manasseh. 1 Chr 12:20.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와의 그늘(보호)'이라는 뜻. (1) 베냐민 사람(역대상 8:20). (2) 므낫세 지파 장군으로 다윗에게 시글락에서 합류했다(역대상 12:20).

entries.definition: ZIM'MAH (mischief), a Gorsbonite Levite. 1 Chr 6:20, 1 Chr 6:42; 2 Chr 29:12.
entries.definition_ko: '악행'이라는 뜻. (1)(2) 게르손 가문 레위인들(역대상 6:20,42). (3) 요아의 아버지(역대하 29:12).

entries.definition: ZIM'RAN (celebrated), a son of Abraham by Keturah. Gen 25:2; 1 Chr 1:32.
entries.definition_ko: '포도 재배자들', '유명한'이라는 뜻으로 아브라함이 그두라를 통해 낳은 아들 중 하나이다(창세기 25:2).

entries.definition: ZIM'RI (snug). A Simeonite chief. Num 25:14. 2. A captain under Elah, and a king of Israel. 1 Kgs 16:9-20. A descendant of Judah, 1 Chr 2:6; called Zabdi in Josh 7:1, Josh 7:17-18. A descendant of Saul. 1 Chr 8:36; 1 Chr 9:42.
entries.definition_ko: '찬양받을 만한'이라는 뜻. (1) 살루의 아들로 미디안 여인을 장막에 데려온 죄로 비느하스에게 죽임을 당했다(민수기 25:6-15). (2) 디르사에서 엘라를 암살하고 이스라엘 왕위에 올랐으나 오므리의 포위 공격에 궁전에 불을 지르고 스스로 죽었다(열왕기상 16:8-20).

entries.definition: ZIN (a low palm tree). The wilderness of Zin was a part of the Arabian desert south of Palestine. Num 13:21-22; Jer 34:3. It joined the territory of Judah, Josh 15:1, Num 1:3; and lay west of Idumaea. Num 20:1; Eze 27:14; Num 33:36. Kadesh is sometimes spoken of as in the wilderness of Zin, Num 33:36, and again as in the wilderness of Paran. Num 13:26. This is explained by the fact that "Paran" was the general name for the whole desert of et-Tih, while Zin was the south-eastern corner of that desert, between the Gulf of Akabah on the south and the head of Wady Garaiyeh. It was south and south-west of 'Azazimeh Mountains, and east of the Ghor and Arabah. Zl'NA. See Zizah.
entries.definition_ko: '낮은 종려나무'라는 뜻이다. 신 광야는 팔레스타인 남쪽 아라비아 사막의 한 부분이었다(민 13:21). 유다 지경에 접했고(수 15:1) 이두매 서쪽에 있었다(민 20:1, 33:36). 가데스가 때로 신 광야에 있다고 하고(민 33:36) 때로 바란 광야에 있다고 하는데(민 13:26), 이는 '바란'이 엣티 사막 전체의 일반 이름이고 신은 남쪽 아카바 만과 와디 가라이예 상류 사이 그 사막의 남동쪽 모퉁이였기 때문이다.

entries.definition: ZI'ON, and SI'ON (dry, sunny mount). "Zion" is sometimes used to denote the whole of Jerusalem, but in its literal and restricted meaning it was the south-western hill of Jerusalem. This hill was surrounded on every side but the north with deep valleys having precipitous sides. To the east was the valley of the Tyropoeon, separating Zion from Moriah, the temple-mount, and from Ophel. On the south and west was the deep valley of Hinnom, called on the west the "valley of Gihon." Upon the north only is the boundary of Zion indefinite. Some authorities think it extended to the tower of David, near the Damascus-gate, and suppose the Tyropoeon valley to have ended here. Others would extend Zion farther northward toward the Jaffa-gate. Zion was the higher hill, being 105 feet above Moriah and 2539 feet above the level of the Mediterranean. It was in the shape of a parallelogram. The valleys were originally much deeper than at present, so that Zion was really compassed on three sides by precipices. It was also guarded by a strong wall. Scripture History. - The hill is first mentioned as a stronghold of the Jebusites. Josh 15:63. It remained in their possession until captured by David, who made it "the city of David," the capital of his kingdom. He built there a citadel, his own palace, houses for the people, and a place for the ark of God. 2 Sam 5:7; 1 Kgs 8:1; 2 Kgs 19:21, 2 Kgs 19:31; 1 Chr 11:5; 2 Chr 5:2. The foregoing six passages are all in the historical books of the O.T. in which the name of Zion appears. But in the prophetical and poetical books it occurs no less than one hundred and forty-eight times - viz., in Psalms, 38 times; Canticles, 1; Isaiah, 47; Jeremiah, 17; Lamentations, 15; Joel, 7; Amos, 2; Obadiah, 2; Micah, 9; Zephaniah, 2; Zechariah, 8. In the N.T. it occurs seven times as "Sion," making the total number of times the name occurs one hundred and sixty-one. It was in the later books no longer confined to the south-western hill, but denoted sometimes Jerusalem in general, Ps 149:2; Ps 87:2; Isa 33:14; Joel 2:2, etc.; sometimes God's chosen people, Ps 51:18; Ps 87:5, etc.; sometimes the Church, Heb 12:22, etc.; and sometimes the heavenly city. Rev 14:1 , etc. Hence, Zion has passed into its present common use in religious literature to denote the aspirations and hopes of God's children. Josephus does not use the word "Zion," but speaks of that quarter of the city as the "city of David," "the upper city," and the "upper market-place." It was then the aristocratic quarter of the city, and contained the mansions of the great. At the north-west corner stood the magnificent palace erected by Herod the Great and afterward called "Praetorium," the residence of the Roman procurator. Mark 15:16. On the north of this were three famous towers or fortresses, of which one is now the "tower of David." Present Condition. - Less than one-half of the ancient hill of Zion is enclosed within the wall of modern Jerusalem. In this part are now the Armenian convent with its extensive grounds, synagogues of the Ashkenasim, St. James' church of the Armenians, the English Protestant church and school, the tower of David, etc. The only building outside the walls is the mosque and tomb of David, supposed to contain the tombs of David, Solomon, and other kings of Judah. In the upper part is the traditional "upper room" in which the Lord's Supper was instituted and the disciples waited for the descent of the Holy Ghost. Upon the slope of the hill are several cemeteries of different Christian denominations and nationalities, including the American and English. A part of the hill is cultivated, and thus the traveller is frequently reminded of the traveler, "Zion shall be ploughed like a field." Jer 26:18; Mic 3:12. The hill sinks into the valley of Hinnom in steep terraced slopes covered with grain-fields, vineyards, and olive trees. The excavations of the British Ordnance Survey brought to light many interesting facts in regard to the original levels, the ancient walls, etc., etc. see Jerusalem. Conder notes the fact that the name "Zion" has not been recovered, and says: "According to Gesenius, it means 'sunny,' and the proper equivalent in Arabic or Syriac, according to this same authority, is Sahyun. It is a remarkable fact that about 1 3/4 miles west of the Jaffagate there exists a valley having exactly this name, Wady Sahyun. . . . This discovery may perhaps lead students to consider the name 'Zion' as a name of a district rather than that of a particular mountain, but it would not accord with the scriptural representations of Zion."
entries.definition_ko: 예루살렘의 남서쪽 언덕으로, 사방이 깊은 골짜기(동쪽 두로뵈온, 남서쪽 힌놈)로 둘러싸여 있다. 다윗이 여부스인에게서 이 요새를 빼앗아 '다윗 성'이라 불렀으며(삼하 5:7), 법궤를 이곳으로 옮겼다(삼하 6:12). 넓은 뜻으로 예루살렘 전체, 유대 민족, 나아가 하늘의 성을 상징한다(히 12:22; 계 14:1).

entries.definition: ZI'OR. (smallness), a place in the mountains of Judah, near Hebron. Josh 15:54. Its probable site is at Sair, a ruin on a hill 5 miles north-north-east of Hebron.
entries.definition_ko: '작음'이라는 뜻으로 헤브론 근처 유다 산지의 한 곳이다(수 15:54). 그 자리는 아마도 헤브론 북북동 5마일 언덕의 폐허 사이르일 것이다.

entries.definition:
ZIPH (a flowing), a descendant of Judah. 1 Chr 4:16.

ZIPH (a flowing), a name for two places. A city in the South of Judah. Josh 15:24. A town in the highlands of Judah, Josh 15:55; fortified by Rehoboam. 2 Chr 11:8. When pursued by Saul, David hid himself "in the wilderness of Ziph." 1 Sam 23:14-15, 1 Sam 23:24; 1 Sam 26:2. The site is Ziph ia a hill about 4 miles south-east of Hebron, on the road to En-gedi. It is a conspicuous mound, and shows at the present day no trace of buildings, but there are large Jewish tombs and a quarry. On a low hill half a mile east are the remains of a town. As to the "wood of Ziph," 1 Sam 23:15, Conder asserts that in all probability it never had any real existence as a "wood," but was rather a town. "The existence," he says, "at any time, of a wood in this part of the country is geologically almost an impossibility. From Hebron to Beersheba not a single spring of any importance exists in the eastern hills. . . . The country is emphatically a dry land. Looking down on the barren wastes which lie above the Dead Sea between Masada and En-gedi, there is no moisture capable of supporting vegetable growth. The cistus and the belan bushes grow among the ledges, but not a single tree exists in the whole country." The translation in Josephus is said to be "in the new place belonging to Ziph," and the Vatican and Alexandrine manuscripts support this. One mile south of Tell Zif is Khirbet Khoreisa, an ancient locality of which Conder says: "We can have little hesitation in identifying with Choresh of Zif a village or hamlet belonging to the larger town of Tell Zif." Tristram, however (Land of Moab, pp. 19, 20), says: "How far the forest of Ziph extended it is not easy to say, but there are traces of it in an occasional tree, and there seems no reason, from the nature of the soil, why the woods may not have stretched nearly to the barren, sandy marl which overlies the limestone for a few miles west of the Dead Sea."
entries.definition_ko: 유다 남부의 성읍(수 15:24)과 유다 산지의 성읍(수 15:55) 두 곳이 있다. 후자는 르호보암이 요새화했으며 사울에게 쫓기던 다윗이 '십 광야'에 숨었다(삼상 23:14-15; 26:2). 헤브론 남동쪽 약 4마일 지점의 언덕으로 동일시된다.

entries.definition: ZI'PHAH, a descendant of Judah. 1 Chr 4:16.
entries.definition_ko: 유다의 후손이다(역대상 4:16).

entries.definition: ZIPH'IMS, the inhabitants of Ziph. Ps 54.
entries.definition_ko: 십 주민을 가리킨다(시 54편 표제).

entries.definition: ZI'PHRON, or ZIPH'RON (sweet odor), a city on the northern frontier of the dominions of Israel. Num 34:9. There is a place called Zaferaneh on the road from Hums (Emesa) to Hamah (Hamath), and about six hours' journey south-southeast of the latter, which may be the ancient Ziphron.
entries.definition_ko: '향기로운 냄새'라는 뜻으로 이스라엘 영토 북쪽 경계의 성읍이다(민 34:9). 훔스(에메사)에서 하맛으로 가는 길, 후자에서 남남동으로 여섯 시간 거리에 자페라네라는 곳이 있는데 옛 시브론일 수 있다.

entries.definition: ZIPII'ITES, the inhabitants of Ziph. 1 Sam 23:19; 1 Sam 26:1.
entries.definition_ko: 십 주민을 가리킨다(삼상 23:19, 26:1).

entries.definition: ZIPII'RON. See Zephon.
entries.definition_ko: 스본 참조.

entries.definition: ZIP'POR (a little bird), the father of Balak, king of Moab. Num 22:2, Ex 6:4, 1 Kgs 16:10, Ex 17:16; Gen 23:18; Josh 24:9; Jud 11:25.
ZIPPO'RAH, a daughter of a Midianite priest, who was married to Moses and bore him two sons. Ex 2:21-22.
entries.definition_ko: '암컷 새'라는 뜻으로 르우엘의 딸이며 모세의 아내가 되었다(출애굽기 2:21). 게르솜과 엘리에셀 두 아들을 두었다.

entries.definition: ZITH'RI (protection of Jehovah), a Levite. Ex 6:22.
entries.definition_ko: '여호와께서 지키신다'는 뜻으로 웃시엘의 아들인 레위인이다(출애굽기 6:22).

entries.definition: ZIZ, THE CLIFF OF. 2 Chr 20:16. The paraphrase of this passage is "the going up of Ha-Ziz," and Grove suggests the name may survive in Husasah. The Pal. Memoirs note a Wady Husasah, 8 miles north of Ain Jidy (En-gedi). The similarity of the name is striking, but the site seems too far from En-gedi. Others have identified Ziz with the pass and cliff near En-gedi, a route how taken by Arab marauding-parties. This pass was the ascent through which invaders from the south and east, after doubling the south end of the Dead Sea, entered the hill-country of Judaea. Ziz was the key of the pass.
entries.definition_ko: '시스 고개'(대하 20:16). 이 구절의 풀이는 '하시스의 오르막'이며 그로브는 그 이름이 후사사에 남아 있을 수 있다고 본다. 팔레스타인 조사단은 아인 지디(엔게디) 북쪽 8마일에 와디 후사사가 있다고 기록한다. 이름은 놀랍도록 비슷하나 그 자리는 엔게디에서 너무 멀어 보인다. 엔게디 근처의 고개와 벼랑, 곧 지금도 아랍 약탈대가 다니는 길과 동일시하는 이도 있다.

entries.definition: ZI'ZA (abundance). A chieftain of Simeon. 1 Chr 4:37. A son of Rehoboam. 2 Chr 11:20.
entries.definition_ko: '광채', '풍성함'이라는 뜻. (1) 시므온 지파의 방백(역대상 4:37). (2) 르호보암의 아들(역대하 11:20).

entries.definition: ZI'ZAH (abundance), a Gershonite Levite, 1 Chr 23:11; the same as Zina. 1 Chr 23:10.
entries.definition_ko: '풍성함'이라는 뜻으로 게르손 자손 레위인이다(대상 23:11). 대상 23:10의 시나와 같은 사람이다.

entries.definition: ZO'AN (low region? or place of departure?), a city of Lower Egypt: called by the Greeks Tanis; now San. Zoan was situated in Lower Egypt, on the east bank of the ancient Tanitic branch of the Nile. It stood in lat. 31░ N. and long. 31░ 55' E. To the east was a great plain, representing "the field of Zoan." History. - Zoan was an exceedingly ancient city, built seven years after Hebron. Num 13:22. Manetho gave an account of a city called "Avaris," fortified by the Shepherd-kings and garrisoned by 240,000 men. Avaris and Zoan are supposed to have been identical. Tradition makes it the town in which Moses had his memorable interviews with Pharaoh, recorded in the book of Exodus. The "field of Zoan" was the place of God's wonders. Ps 78:12, Acts 2:43. "When Isaiah wrote, it would appear to have been one of the chief cities in Egypt, as he speaks of "the princes of Zoan." Isa 19:11, 2 Kgs 11:13; Gen 30:4. Ezekiel foretells the fate of the city in the words: "I will set fire in Zoan." Eze 30:14. There are no other Scripture references to Zoan. Present Condition. - Zoan has been satisfactorily identified with the ancient Avaris and Tanis and the modern San. Very interesting discoveries have been made there within a few years past by Brugsch Bey and others. Among the inscriptions has been found one with the expression Sechet Tanet, which exactly corresponds to the "field of Zoan." Ps 78:43. Several colossal statues of kings of the various dynasties and a number of sphinxes have been brought to light by excavations. The mounds which mark the site of the town are remarkable for their height and extent, and cover an area a mile in length by three-fourths of a mile in width. The sacred enclosure of the great temple was 1500 feet long and 1250 feet wide. This temple was adorned by Barneses II. There are some dozen obelisks of great size, all fallen and broken, with numerous statues. " The whole constitutes," says Macgregor, "one of the grandest and oldest ruins in the world." The "field of Zoan" was a rich plain extending some 30 miles to the east. It is now almost covered by the great Lake Menzeleh, but some portions exhibit a rich black loam without fences or towns, and with only a few trees in sight. Brugsch-Bey is of the opinion that Zoan was identical with Rameses, but this location was made to fit his theory that the Israelites crossed the Serbonian bog instead of the Red Sea. An English Exploration Society is engaged in making explorations in San. It promises rich historical results in this ancient land.
entries.definition_ko: 하이집트의 도시로 그리스어로는 타니스, 현재는 산이라 불린다. 헤브론보다 7년 후에 건축된 극히 오래된 성읍이며(민 13:22), '소안 들'은 하나님의 기사가 행해진 곳이었다(시 78:12). 이사야는 '소안의 방백들'을 언급하고(사 19:11) 에스겔은 그 멸망을 예언했다(겔 30:14). 발굴을 통해 거대한 오벨리스크·석상·스핑크스 등이 발견되었다.

entries.definition: ZO'AR(smallness),one of the "cities of the plain," Gen 13:10; originally called "Bela." Gen 14:2, 1 Kgs 15:8. This "little city" was spared from the destruction which overtook Sodom and the other cities, and made a refuge for Lot. Gen 19:20-30. Zoar was included in the view Moses had from Pisgah. Deut 34:3. The prophets Isaiah, Isa 15:5, and Jeremiah, Jer 48:34, reckon Zoar among the cities of Moab. Situation. - The situation of Zoar, like that of the other cities of the plain, has been much discussed. The great majority of scholars, from Ptolemy, Josephus, Eusebius, and Jerome to the present time, have located it near the southeastern shore of the Dead Sea. The shore of the bay, which extends from the Dead Sea into the Lisan Peninsula, has been regarded as a probable site for Zoar. For the general discussion as to the relative merits of the sites at the northern and at the southern ends of the Dead Sea, see Siddim and Sodom. Tristram was confident that he had discovered the site of Zoar at Ziara, some 3 miles north-west of Nebo and 11 miles west of the northern end of the Dead Sea. Among the points he urges for this special identification are the strong resemblance of the names and the fact that this place would be in plain view of Moses from Nebo. Deut 34:3. He cites also several arguments for putting all the cities at the upper end of the Dead Sea. This seems to be among the mountains, and too far from the other to be a likely position for Zoar. Merrill suggests, as the site for Zoar, Tell Ektauu, in the Shittim plain, north-east of the Dead Sea, near to the mountains of Moab, although it cannot be reckoned as one of the foot-hills. There are ruins here of great age, and the name Ektauu, which has no meaning in Arabic, appears to be the Hebrew word Katan, which means "little," or "the little one." The site would be in the direction Lot would naturally take in hastening to the neighboring city, and its distance from other mounds in the Shittim plain (which Dr. Merrill would identify with the plain in which stood Sodom and Gomorrah) corresponds well with the time allowed the fugitive - namely, from dawn to sunrise. Conder, who would place the lost cities at the north "end" of the Dead Sea, suggests Tell esh-Shaghai as the site of Zoar. It is at the foot of the eastern mountains, immediately north of the Dead Sea, and about 6 miles south of Nimrin.
entries.definition_ko: 평지의 성읍 중 하나로 원래 벨라라 불렸다(창 14:2). 소돔의 멸망 때 롯의 피난처로 보존된 '작은 성읍'이며(창 19:20-30), 모세가 비스가에서 바라본 땅에 포함되었다(신 34:3). 대다수 학자는 사해 남동쪽 해안 부근에 위치시키나, 사해 북쪽 설도 있다.

entries.definition: ZO'BA, and ZO'BAH (station), a portion of Syria. It was one of the kingdoms of Aram, known as Aramzobah. See Aram. It embraced the country between the north-east of Palestine and the Euphrates. It was the home of a powerful nation, whose kings were engaged in frequent wars with Israel during the reigns of Saul, David, and Solomon. Saul "vexed them." 1 Sam 14:47. David defeated King Hadadezer and the Syrians who came to his assistance with great loss. 2 Sam 8:3-8, 2 Sam 8:12; 1 Chr 18:3-8; Ps 60, title. Again, in David's time, they and the "Syrians beyond the river," their allies, were defeated by Joab. 2 Sam 10:6-13; 1 Chr 19:6. One of David's mighty men was "the son of Nathan of Zobah." 2 Sam 23:36. The nation, though severely punished, was not destroyed, and we read of a Hadadezer, king of Zobah, in Solomon's time, 1 Kgs 11:23, and Solomon took Hamath-zobah. 2 Chr 8:3. See Hamath. Other towns of Zobah are mentioned - Betah, Berothal, and perhaps Helam. 2 Sam 8:8; 2 Sam 10:6. Porter suggests it as just possible that the biblical Zobah. which was situated between Hamath and Damascus, may be identical with Emesa, the modern Hums. The region possesses a rich soil, abundant water, and a genial climate, but the towns and villages are in ruins and the Bedouins are the principal inhabitants. The cities of Zobah are forsaken.
entries.definition_ko: '주둔지'라는 뜻으로 수리아의 한 지역이다. 아람의 왕국 중 하나로 아람소바로 알려져 있다. 팔레스타인 북동쪽과 유브라데 사이의 땅을 아울렀다. 강한 나라의 본거지로, 그 왕들이 사울과 다윗과 솔로몬 시대에 이스라엘과 자주 전쟁을 벌였다. 사울이 그들을 '괴롭게 했고'(삼상 14:47), 다윗은 하닷에셀 왕과 그를 도우러 온 시리아 사람들을 크게 무찔렀다(삼하 8:3-8, 대상 18:3-8).

entries.definition: ZOBE'BAH (slow moving), a descendant of Judah. 1 Chr 4:8.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 지파 곳스의 아들이다(역대상 4:8).

entries.definition: ZO'HAR (whiteness). The father of Ephron. Gen 23:8; Gen 25:9. See Zerah, 3.
entries.definition_ko: '광채'라는 뜻. (1) 헷 사람 에브론의 아버지(창세기 23:8). (2) 시므온의 아들 중 하나(창세기 46:10).

entries.definition: ZO'HELETH (serpent), a stone by "En-rogel," by which Adonijah "slew sheep and oxen and fat cattle." 1 Kgs 1:9. M. Ganneau found the steep rock-cut steps by which people from the village of Siloam pass down to the "Virgin's Fount," in the Kedron valley, bear among the Arabs the name of Zahweileh. This he would identify with the stone of Zoheleth. and En-rogel would be the Virgin's Fount instead of the Well of Job (Bir Eyub), as has been usually supposed.
entries.definition_ko: '뱀의 돌'이라는 뜻으로 실로암 마을 중심 근처, 엔로겔 샘 부근의 바위 대지이며, 아도니야가 솔로몬을 제외한 왕자들을 모아 잔치를 벌인 곳이다(열왕기상 1:5-9).

entries.definition: ZO'HETH (derivation unknown), a descendant of Judah. 1 Chr 4:20.
entries.definition_ko: 이시의 아들 중 하나이다(역대상 4:20).

entries.definition: ZO'PHAH (a cruse), an Asherite chief. 1 Chr 7:35-36.
entries.definition_ko: 헬렘의 아들로 아셀 지파의 방백이다(역대상 7:35).

entries.definition: ZO'PHAI (honeycomb), a Kohathite Levite, ancestor of Samuel. 1 Chr 6:26.
entries.definition_ko: 고핫 계열 레위인 엘가나의 아들이자 사무엘의 조상으로 다른 곳에서는 숩으로 불린다(역대상 6:26,35).

entries.definition: ZOPHAR, one of Job's three friends, Job 2:11, is called the Naamatliite, probably because he belonged to Naamah, Josh 15:41, a town assigned to Judah.
entries.definition_ko: 욥을 위로하러 온 친구 중 하나로(욥기 2:11) 나아마 사람으로 불린다.

entries.definition: ZO'PHIM (watchers). The field of Zophim was the place on the "top of Pisgah" to which Balak brought Balaam that the false prophet might see the camp of Israel. Num 23:14. Grove says that if the word rendered "field" be taken in its usual sense, then the "field of Zophim" was a cultivated spot high up on the top of Pisgah. The position of the field must of course depend upon the site assigned for Pisgah. If Jebel Siaghah be Pisgah, as supposed by Paine (but not confirmed), then Zophim, or "the top of Pisgah," was the third summit of Siaghah, running westward from Nebo, which is a little higher than the others and appears to look down upon them. See Pisgah.
entries.definition_ko: '파수꾼들'이라는 뜻이다. 소빔 들은 '비스가 꼭대기'에 있던 곳으로, 발락이 거짓 선지자 발람이 이스라엘의 진영을 볼 수 있도록 데려간 곳이다(민 23:14). 그로브는 '들'로 옮긴 말을 통상적 뜻으로 보면 '소빔 들'은 비스가 꼭대기 높은 곳의 경작지였다고 한다. 이 들의 위치는 물론 비스가를 어디로 보느냐에 달려 있다. 제벨 시아가가 비스가라면 소빔 곧 '비스가 꼭대기'는 느보에서 서쪽으로 뻗은 시아가의 셋째 봉우리로, 다른 것들보다 조금 높아 내려다보는 듯하다.

entries.definition: ZO'RAH, and ZORE'AH (hornets' town), and ZA'REAH, Neh 11:29, a town in the low-country of Judah; afterward assigned to Dan, Josh 15:33; Josh 19:41; the birthplace and burial place of Samson. Jud 13:2, Gal 4:25; Jud 16:31. From Zorah the Danites sent spies to search the land for a place of inheritance. Jud 18:2. Zorah was fortified by Rehoboam, 2 Chr 11:10, and inhabited after the return from captivity. Neh 11:29. The place still exists as Surah, 13 miles west of Jerusalem, 23 miles southeast of Joppa, and 2 miles north of Bethshemesh. It is situated on the crest of a hill, 1150 feet above the sea. It overlooks the valley of Sorek. Timnah stands some 2 or 3 miles to the southwest, across the valley.
entries.definition_ko: '말벌의 성읍'이라는 뜻으로(느 11:29에서는 사르아) 유다 저지대의 성읍이며 후에 단에게 배정되었다(수 15:33, 19:41). 삼손의 출생지이자 매장지다(삿 13:2,25, 16:31). 소라에서 단 사람들이 기업으로 삼을 땅을 정탐하러 보냈다(삿 18:2). 르호보암이 견고케 했고(대하 11:10) 포로에서 돌아온 후 사람이 살았다(느 11:29). 지금도 수라로 남아 있으며 예루살렘 서쪽 13마일, 욥바 남동쪽 23마일, 벧세메스 북쪽 2마일에 있다. 해발 1,150피트 언덕 꼭대기에 자리해 소렉 골짜기를 내려다본다.

entries.definition: ZO'RATHITES, a family of the tribe of Judah, probably inhabitants of Zorah. 1 Chr 4:2.
entries.definition_ko: 유다 지파의 한 가문으로 아마도 소라의 주민일 것이다(대상 4:2).

entries.definition: ZO'REAH. Josh 15:33. See Zorah.
ZO'RITES, probably inhabitants of Zorah. 1 Chr 2:54.
entries.definition_ko: 아마도 소라의 주민일 것이다(대상 2:54).

entries.definition: ZOROB'ABEL. See Zerubbabel.
entries.definition_ko: 스룹바벨(Zerubbabel)의 헬라식 형태다(마태복음 1:12,13; 누가복음 3:27).

entries.definition: ZUAR (smallness), father of Nethaneel. Num 1:8; Neh 2:5; Isa 7:18, Lev 7:23; Josh 10:15.
entries.definition_ko: 출애굽 당시 잇사갈 지파 지도자 느다넬의 아버지다(민수기 1:8).

entries.definition:
ZUPH (honeycomb), a Kohathite Levite, an ancestor of Samuel the prophet. 1 Sam 1:1; 1 Chr 6:35.

ZUPH (flag, sedge). Deut 1:1, margin. From the Hebrew Suph, signifying a kind of sea-weed, and the Hebrew name for the Red Sea, which see.
entries.definition_ko: 1) '벌집'이라는 뜻으로 고핫 자손 레위인이며 선지자 사무엘의 조상이다(삼상 1:1, 대상 6:35). 2) '갈대', '수초'라는 뜻이다(신 1:1 난외주). 일종의 해초를 뜻하는 히브리어 '숩'에서 왔으며 홍해의 히브리 이름이기도 하다.

entries.definition: ZUPH, THE LAND OF, the farthest point of the journey of Saul, and where he encountered Samuel at a certain city, the name of which is not given. 1 Sam 9:5-6. The whole of this journey has been a curious puzzle in Scripture topography, "for the starting-point is unknown, the point to which he returned doubtful," and the intermediate places have not been satisfactorily identified. Some resemblance to Zuph was thought to be found in Sola, 7 miles west of Jerusalem and 5 miles southwest of Neby Samwil. Conder notes that the Targum on the passage connects the name "Zuph" with the root zephah, meaning "to shine," and hence "to be conspicuous," whence come the words "Zephathah," "Zophim," "Zephir," and "Mizpeh." In other Targums the words "Zophira " and "Mizpeh" are used indiscriminately in speaking of one place, both words being applicable to a "watch-tower" or city in an elevated situation. "Zuph" was, however, also the name of a man, and it is not impossible that the land of Zuph may have been named after him. 1 Sam 1:1. In the first case the city in the land of Zuph would possibly be Shufa: in the second it would be Bethlehem, the home of Zuph. See Mizpeh.
entries.definition_ko: 사울의 여정의 가장 먼 지점이며, 이름이 밝혀지지 않은 어떤 성읍에서 사무엘을 만난 곳이다(삼상 9:5-6). 이 여정 전체가 성경 지리의 기묘한 수수께끼인데, '출발점을 알 수 없고 돌아온 지점도 불확실하며' 중간 지점들도 만족스럽게 확인되지 않았다.

entries.definition: ZUR (rock). A Midianitish prince. Num 25:15; Josh 13:21, who was slain, with others, by the Israelites when the Midianites suffered the judgments of God for their sins. Num 26:18. Son of the founder of Gibeon. 1 Chr 8:30; 1 Chr 9:36.
entries.definition_ko: '반석'이라는 뜻. 미디안의 방백으로(민 25:15, 수 13:21) 미디안이 그 죄로 하나님의 심판을 받을 때 다른 이들과 함께 이스라엘에게 죽임을 당했다(민 31:8). 또한 기브온의 조상의 아들이기도 하다(대상 8:30, 9:36).

entries.definition: ZU'RIEL (my rock is God), a chief Levite in the time of the Exodus. Num 3:35.
entries.definition_ko: '하나님은 나의 반석'이라는 뜻으로 출애굽 당시 므라리 가문의 지도자였다(민수기 3:35).

entries.definition: ZU'RISHAD'DAI (my rock is the Almighty), the father of the chief of Simeon at the time of the Exodus. Num 1:6; Num 2:12; Acts 7:36, John 7:41; Isa 10:19.
entries.definition_ko: '전능자는 나의 반석'이라는 뜻으로 시내산 진영 당시 시므온 지파장 슬루미엘의 아버지이다(민수기 1:6).

entries.definition: ZU'ZIMS, the Ammonite name. Gen 14:5, of doubtful derivation, for a tribe of gigantic stature and strength which inhabited the country east of the Jordan and the Dead Sea, probably between the Arnon and the Jabbok. They were attacked and routed by Chedorlaomer, and afterward expelled by the Ammonites. "All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:that the man of god may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all good works." - 2 Tim 3:16-17.
entries.definition_ko: 창 14:5의 암몬식 이름으로 어원은 불확실하며, 요단과 사해 동쪽 땅, 아마도 아르논과 얍복 사이에 살던 거인 같은 체구와 힘을 지닌 부족을 가리킨다. 그돌라오멜에게 공격받아 무너졌고 후에 암몬 사람에게 쫓겨났다.
